definition: Given a combustor or burner geometry, fuel and oxidizer streams and a chemistry model, compute flame structure, temperatures and emissions.
inputs: geometry; inlet compositions; reaction mechanism; turbulence-chemistry model
outputs: temperature and species fields; heat release; pollutant emissions
benchmark_note: TNF Workshop flames (Sandia flame D and others) have measured data
state_of_art: Ansys Fluent; Convergent Science CONVERGE; Simcenter STAR-CCM+

name: Wind flow around buildings
definition: Given buildings or structures and an atmospheric boundary-layer inflow, compute wind pressures, pedestrian-level wind and dispersion near structures.
inputs: building geometry; inflow wind profile and direction
outputs: surface pressure coefficients; pedestrian wind speeds
benchmark_note: Architectural Institute of Japan benchmark cases and the CEDVAL wind-tunnel data sets
state_of_art: Simcenter STAR-CCM+; Ansys Fluent; SimScale

name: Heat transfer and thermal analysis
definition: Given a part, assembly or spacecraft with thermal properties, heat loads and boundary conditions, compute temperatures and heat flows by conduction, convection and radiation.

name: Conduction heat transfer analysis
definition: Given a solid's geometry, conductivity and thermal boundary conditions, compute steady or transient temperature fields.
inputs: mesh; conductivity, density and specific heat; heat loads and boundary conditions
outputs: temperature fields over time; heat fluxes
benchmark_note: NAFEMS thermal benchmarks and closed-form conduction solutions
state_of_art: Ansys Mechanical; Abaqus; COMSOL Heat Transfer Module

name: Lumped thermal network analysis
definition: Given a system idealized as thermal nodes and conductors with heat sources, solve for node temperatures and heat flows over time.
inputs: nodes; conductors; capacitances; heat loads; boundary temperatures
outputs: node temperature histories; heat flows
benchmark_note: analytical network cases verify solvers; system models are proprietary
state_of_art: Thermal Desktop with SINDA/FLUINT; ESATAN-TMS; Siemens Simcenter Space Systems Thermal

name: Radiation exchange and orbital heating
definition: Given surface geometry, optical properties and an orbit or environment, compute view factors, radiative couplings and absorbed solar, albedo and planetary fluxes.
inputs: surface model; emissivity and absorptivity; orbit and attitude
outputs: view factors; radiative conductors; absorbed heat flux histories
benchmark_note: analytical view-factor catalogues give exact references
state_of_art: Thermal Desktop RadCAD; ESATAN-TMS Radiative; Simcenter Space Systems Thermal

name: Electronics cooling analysis
definition: Given a board, enclosure or package layout with component powers and cooling, compute component and junction temperatures.
inputs: board and enclosure geometry; component powers; fans and heat sinks
outputs: junction and board temperatures; airflow; thermal margins
benchmark_note: JEDEC JESD51 package test conditions are standard, but benchmark models are vendor-held
state_of_art: Siemens Simcenter Flotherm; Ansys Icepak; Cadence Celsius

name: Conjugate heat transfer
definition: Given coupled fluid and solid domains, solve fluid flow and solid conduction together to obtain wall temperatures and heat-transfer rates.
inputs: fluid and solid domains; properties; flow and thermal boundary conditions
outputs: temperature fields in fluid and solid; heat-transfer coefficients
benchmark_note: ASME V&V 20 example problems and heated-channel data sets
state_of_art: Ansys Fluent; Simcenter STAR-CCM+; COMSOL

name: Heat exchanger rating and design
definition: Given heat-exchanger type, geometry and stream conditions, compute duty, outlet temperatures and pressure drops, or size the exchanger for a required duty.
inputs: exchanger type and geometry; stream flows, temperatures and properties
outputs: duty; outlet temperatures; pressure drops; required area
benchmark_note: effectiveness-NTU closed forms; industrial rating correlations are proprietary
state_of_art: HTRI Xchanger Suite; Aspen Exchanger Design and Rating

name: Insulation and heat-loss calculation
definition: Given pipe, duct or equipment surfaces, insulation and ambient conditions, compute heat loss, surface temperature and economic insulation thickness.
inputs: surface geometry; insulation type and thickness; process and ambient temperatures
outputs: heat loss; surface temperature; economic thickness
benchmark_note: ASTM C680 procedures give deterministic reference results
state_of_art: 3E Plus

name: Fire and smoke simulation
definition: Given an enclosure or building, fuel and fire scenarios, compute fire growth, smoke and heat movement, detector and sprinkler response, structural heating and occupant egress.

name: Zone fire modeling
definition: Given compartments, vents and a heat release rate, compute upper-layer temperature, layer height and species over time with a two-zone model.
inputs: compartment geometry; vents; heat release rate; materials
outputs: layer temperatures and heights; species concentrations over time
benchmark_note: NUREG-1824 verification and validation of fire models gives measured experiments
state_of_art: CFAST; B-RISK; OZone

name: Field fire modeling
definition: Given a 3D enclosure, fuels and ignition, solve low-Mach reacting flow to compute temperature, smoke and toxic gas fields.
inputs: 3D geometry; fuel properties; ignition and heat release; ventilation
outputs: temperature, velocity, visibility and species fields
benchmark_note: the FDS Verification and Validation Guides compare against dozens of experiments
state_of_art: Fire Dynamics Simulator; Ansys Fluent; FireFOAM

name: Detector and sprinkler activation
definition: Given a fire growth curve, ceiling geometry and device response properties, compute the time to detector, sprinkler or vent activation.
inputs: heat release rate curve; ceiling height and spacing; response time index
outputs: activation times; heat release at activation
benchmark_note: ceiling-jet correlations are closed form; activation test data exist in NIST reports
state_of_art: DETACT-QS; FDS; CFAST

name: Smoke control system analysis
definition: Given a building's flow paths, fans and stack effect, compute pressure differences and smoke movement for a smoke management design.
inputs: building flow network; leakage areas; fans; temperatures
outputs: pressure differences across barriers; airflow rates; smoke spread
benchmark_note: network airflow cases verify solvers; system tests are building-specific
state_of_art: CONTAM; FDS

name: Structural fire response
definition: Given fire exposure and structural members, compute member temperatures and the resulting loss of strength and stability.
inputs: member geometry; thermal and mechanical properties at temperature; fire exposure curve
outputs: temperature histories; deflections; time to failure
benchmark_note: ISO 834 furnace tests and the Cardington tests provide data
state_of_art: SAFIR; Abaqus; Ansys Mechanical

name: Window breakage and fire spread
definition: Given a compartment fire and glazing properties, predict when windows break and the resulting change in ventilation.
inputs: glass properties; fire exposure; frame shading
outputs: time to glass breakage
benchmark_note: small-scale breakage experiments exist
state_of_art: BREAK1; B-RISK

name: Egress and evacuation simulation
definition: Given a building layout, occupant population and behaviors, compute required safe egress times and congestion.
inputs: floor plans; exits; occupant numbers and profiles; pre-movement times
outputs: evacuation times; flow rates; congestion locations
benchmark_note: IMO MSC.1/Circ.1533 verification tests are used to compare evacuation models
state_of_art: Pathfinder; EXODUS; MassMotion; STEPS

name: Fire risk assessment
definition: Given a building, fire scenarios with frequencies and protection systems, compute expected risk to life by combining fire, smoke and egress models over scenarios.
inputs: scenario set with probabilities; building and protection data
outputs: expected life risk; fire cost expectation
benchmark_note: results depend on scenario weights with no ground truth
state_of_art: B-RISK; CESARE-Risk

name: Multibody dynamics and mechanisms
definition: Given bodies connected by joints, forces and contacts, compute motions, joint reactions and interaction forces of mechanisms, machines, robots and human bodies.

name: Mechanism kinematic analysis
definition: Given a linkage or cam mechanism and input motions, compute positions, velocities and accelerations of all members and check interference.
inputs: bodies; joints; driver motions
outputs: position, velocity and acceleration histories; interference
benchmark_note: closed-form four-bar and slider-crank solutions
state_of_art: Adams; Simcenter 3D Motion; SolidWorks Motion

name: Rigid multibody dynamics
definition: Given rigid bodies, joints, forces and initial conditions, integrate the equations of motion to compute motions and joint reactions.
inputs: masses and inertias; joints; force elements; initial state
outputs: motion histories; joint reaction forces; energy
benchmark_note: the IFToMM library of computational benchmark problems for multibody dynamics
state_of_art: Adams; RecurDyn; Simpack; Altair MotionSolve

name: Flexible multibody dynamics
definition: Given a mechanism with deformable members represented by modal or nodal flexibility, compute coupled large motion and elastic deformation.
inputs: multibody model; flexible body reductions or meshes; loads
outputs: motions; elastic deformations; dynamic stresses
benchmark_note: IFToMM benchmarks include flexible cases (for example the flexible slider-crank)
state_of_art: Adams Flex; Simpack; RecurDyn RFlex

name: Granular flow by discrete elements
definition: Given particle shapes and contact laws and a container, chute or mill geometry, simulate bulk material flow and forces on equipment.
inputs: particle size, shape and contact parameters; equipment geometry and motion
outputs: flow patterns; mass flow rates; wall forces and wear
benchmark_note: published DEM benchmark tests check contact models; calibration dominates real cases
state_of_art: Altair EDEM; Rocky DEM

name: Belt conveyor dynamic analysis
definition: Given a belt conveyor profile, belt, drives and material loading, compute belt tensions, power and starting and stopping transients.
inputs: conveyor profile; belt properties; drives and take-ups; material flow
outputs: tension distribution; drive power; transient tensions
benchmark_note: CEMA design method gives reference steady-state tensions
state_of_art: Belt Analyst; Helix delta-T

name: Robot and grasp physics simulation
definition: Given a robot model, objects and contact properties, simulate contact-rich motion and evaluate grasp quality or controller behavior.
inputs: robot description; object geometry and mass; contact and friction; controller
outputs: trajectories; contact forces; grasp quality metrics
benchmark_note: grasp and manipulation benchmarks exist (YCB object set), but scoring mixes control and physics
state_of_art: NVIDIA Isaac Sim; Webots; CoppeliaSim

name: Human body biomechanics
definition: Given a posture or motion, anthropometry and external loads, compute joint loads, muscle forces and strength capability of the human body.
inputs: body segment model; posture or motion capture; external forces
outputs: joint moments and compressive forces; muscle forces; percent capable
benchmark_note: the Grand Challenge Competition to Predict In Vivo Knee Loads gives measured joint forces
state_of_art: Siemens Jack; AnyBody Modeling System; 3DSSPP

name: Vehicle and vessel performance
definition: Given a ship, aircraft, spacecraft or road vehicle and its operating environment, compute its stability, resistance, motions, trajectory or energy use.

name: Ship hydrostatics and stability
definition: Given a hull form, compartments and loading, compute hydrostatics, intact and damaged stability and compliance with stability criteria.
inputs: hull offsets; compartments; weights and tank loads; damage cases
outputs: hydrostatic tables; righting-arm curves; criteria compliance
benchmark_note: IMO intact stability criteria are deterministic, but reference hull sets are not public
state_of_art: GHS; NAPA; Maxsurf Stability

name: Ship resistance and propulsion
definition: Given hull particulars and propulsor data, predict calm-water resistance, propulsor performance and required power versus speed.
inputs: hull form or parameters; propeller geometry; speed range
outputs: resistance and effective power curves; propeller efficiency; delivered power
benchmark_note: the Gothenburg and Tokyo CFD workshops (KCS, KVLCC2, DTMB 5415) have towing-tank data
state_of_art: NavCad; Simcenter STAR-CCM+

name: Seakeeping and wave loads
definition: Given a floating body and sea states, compute wave-induced motions, loads and response statistics.
inputs: hull or panel mesh; mass properties; wave spectra
outputs: response amplitude operators; motion statistics; wave loads
benchmark_note: ITTC seakeeping data and the IEA Wind OC3 to OC6 floating-platform code comparisons
state_of_art: Ansys Aqwa; WAMIT; Orcaflex; Sesam

name: Mooring analysis
definition: Given a moored vessel, lines, fenders and environmental loads, compute line tensions and vessel offsets.
inputs: vessel data; line and fender properties; wind, current and wave loads
outputs: line tensions; vessel excursions; safety factors
benchmark_note: OC-series floating-wind comparisons include moorings; terminal cases are proprietary
state_of_art: OPTIMOOR; OrcaFlex; Ariane

name: Powertrain and drive-cycle simulation
definition: Given vehicle, engine or motor, transmission and battery models, simulate a drive cycle to compute fuel or energy use, emissions and performance.
inputs: vehicle parameters; powertrain component maps; drive cycle
outputs: fuel or energy consumption; emissions; acceleration and gradeability
benchmark_note: certification cycles are standard, but vehicle models are proprietary
state_of_art: AVL CRUISE M; GT-SUITE; Autonomie

name: Flight and projectile trajectory
definition: Given an aircraft, missile or projectile with aerodynamic and mass data, simulate six- or three-degree-of-freedom flight through the atmosphere.
inputs: aerodynamic coefficients; mass properties; propulsion; atmosphere and initial state
outputs: trajectory; attitude; flight performance
benchmark_note: NASA six-degree-of-freedom flight simulation check-cases have reference trajectories
state_of_art: MATLAB Aerospace Blockset; X-Plane; PRODAS

name: Orbit propagation and mission analysis
definition: Given orbital elements, force models and maneuvers, propagate spacecraft orbits and compute access, coverage and maneuver costs.
inputs: initial orbit state; gravity, drag and third-body models; maneuvers
outputs: ephemerides; access windows; delta-v budgets
benchmark_note: published SGP4 verification vectors and GMAT-STK cross-comparisons give references
state_of_art: Ansys STK; FreeFlyer

name: Vehicle collision reconstruction
definition: Given crash damage, rest positions and vehicle data, reconstruct impact speeds and trajectories by momentum, crush-energy or simulation methods.
inputs: vehicle masses and stiffness; crush profiles; scene measurements
outputs: impact speeds and delta-v; pre- and post-impact trajectories
benchmark_note: staged collision tests (RICSAC) give measured speeds for scoring
state_of_art: PC-Crash; Virtual CRASH; HVE

name: Electromagnetic field simulation
definition: Given conductors, magnetic and dielectric materials, sources and boundaries, solve Maxwell's equations for static, low-frequency or full-wave fields and derived forces, losses and radiation.

name: Low-frequency magnetic field analysis
definition: Given magnetic materials, coils and permanent magnets, compute static or eddy-current magnetic fields, forces, inductances and losses.
inputs: geometry; B-H curves and conductivities; coil currents or circuits; motion
outputs: flux density; forces and torques; inductance; eddy and core losses
benchmark_note: COMPUMAG TEAM workshop problems have measured reference data
state_of_art: Ansys Maxwell; Simcenter MAGNET; JMAG; Altair Flux; Opera

name: Electrostatic and quasi-static field analysis
definition: Given conductors at potentials and dielectrics, compute electric fields, capacitances and field stress on insulation.
inputs: geometry; permittivities and conductivities; potentials or charges
outputs: potential and field distributions; capacitance matrix; peak field stress
benchmark_note: analytical capacitor and sphere-gap solutions give references
state_of_art: Ansys Maxwell; COMSOL AC/DC Module; Simcenter ELECTRO

name: Electric machine performance
definition: Given motor, generator or transformer geometry, windings and materials, compute torque, back-EMF, efficiency maps and losses.
inputs: machine cross-section or 3D geometry; windings; materials; operating points
outputs: torque-speed and efficiency maps; losses; cogging torque
benchmark_note: TEAM problem 30 (induction motor) gives reference torque
state_of_art: Ansys Motor-CAD; JMAG; Simcenter SPEED

name: High-frequency full-wave analysis
definition: Given antennas, waveguides, components or scatterers, solve full-wave Maxwell's equations to compute S-parameters, radiation patterns and scattering.
inputs: geometry; materials; ports or incident waves; frequency band
outputs: S-parameters; field distributions; radiation patterns; radar cross-section
benchmark_note: the Austin RCS benchmark suite and IEEE Std 1597.2 validation problems
state_of_art: Ansys HFSS; CST Studio Suite; Altair Feko; Remcom XFdtd

name: Electromagnetic compatibility and exposure
definition: Given a device, enclosure or body model and sources, compute shielding, coupling, emissions or specific absorption rate.
inputs: device and enclosure geometry; cables; sources; tissue models
outputs: shielding effectiveness; coupled currents; SAR distributions
benchmark_note: IEC/IEEE 62704-1 SAR benchmark models and IEEE Std 1597.2 problems
state_of_art: CST Studio Suite; Sim4Life; Remcom XFdtd

name: Radio propagation and coverage prediction
definition: Given transmitter sites, antennas and terrain, compute path loss and predicted coverage.
inputs: transmitter parameters; antenna patterns; terrain and clutter data
outputs: path loss; coverage maps; link margins
benchmark_note: ITU-R Study Group 3 measurement databanks
state_of_art: Forsk Atoll; Infovista Planet; Remcom Wireless InSite

name: Charged particle beam simulation
definition: Given electrodes, magnets and particle sources, track charged particles through fields to compute beam trajectories, optics and space-charge effects.
inputs: field maps or geometry; particle source distribution
outputs: trajectories; beam envelopes; emittance; current deposition
benchmark_note: analytic beam-optics cases check solvers; device data are proprietary
state_of_art: Opera; CST Particle Studio; SIMION

name: Optical and photonic simulation
definition: Given lenses, mirrors, sources, waveguides or nanostructures, compute light propagation by ray tracing or wave optics and derive image quality, illumination or mode and transmission properties.

name: Imaging optical system design
definition: Given a lens or mirror prescription and field and wavelength specifications, trace rays to compute aberrations and image quality and optimize the prescription.
inputs: surface prescriptions; materials; fields; wavelengths; merit function
outputs: spot diagrams; MTF; wavefront error; optimized prescription
benchmark_note: reference ray traces for published prescriptions verify tracers; design quality is open-ended
state_of_art: Ansys Zemax OpticStudio; Synopsys CODE V; OSLO

name: Illumination and stray light analysis
definition: Given sources, optics and mechanical surfaces with scatter properties, trace non-sequential rays to compute illuminance, intensity and stray light.
inputs: source models; optical and mechanical geometry; surface scatter properties
outputs: illuminance and intensity maps; stray-light paths; efficiency
benchmark_note: CIE 171:2006 includes test cases; scatter models limit accuracy
state_of_art: LightTools; ASAP; TracePro; FRED

name: Waveguide mode solving and propagation
definition: Given a waveguide or fiber cross-section and indices, compute guided modes and propagate fields along the structure.
inputs: cross-section geometry; refractive indices; wavelength
outputs: mode profiles; effective indices; propagation loss and coupling
benchmark_note: slab and step-index fiber modes have analytic solutions
state_of_art: Ansys Lumerical MODE; FIMMWAVE; Synopsys RSoft BeamPROP

name: Nanophotonic full-wave simulation
definition: Given a nanostructured or photonic-crystal device, solve Maxwell's equations in the time or frequency domain to compute transmission, reflection and band structure.
inputs: device geometry; dispersive materials; sources and monitors
outputs: transmission and reflection spectra; band diagrams; near fields
benchmark_note: Mie scattering and photonic-crystal band structures have exact references
state_of_art: Ansys Lumerical FDTD; Synopsys RSoft FullWAVE; Flexcompute Tidy3D

name: Thin-film and multilayer optics
definition: Given a stack of thin layers with complex indices, compute reflectance, transmittance and absorption versus wavelength and angle.
inputs: layer thicknesses; complex refractive indices; wavelengths and angles
outputs: reflectance, transmittance and absorptance spectra
benchmark_note: transfer-matrix results are exact
state_of_art: OptiLayer; TFCalc; Essential Macleod

name: Photonic integrated circuit and laser simulation
definition: Given a photonic circuit of lasers, modulators, waveguides and detectors, simulate time- or frequency-domain optical and electrical signals.
inputs: component models; circuit topology; drive signals
outputs: optical spectra and waveforms; eye diagrams; laser dynamics
benchmark_note: laser rate-equation solutions verify solvers; component models are foundry-specific
state_of_art: Ansys Lumerical INTERCONNECT; PICWave; VPIphotonics

name: Physical optics and adaptive optics simulation
definition: Given an optical system, atmospheric turbulence and a wavefront sensing and correction scheme, propagate wavefronts and compute corrected image quality.
inputs: pupil and optics model; turbulence profile; sensor and deformable mirror models
outputs: residual wavefront error; Strehl ratio; point-spread functions
benchmark_note: diffraction-limited cases are exact; AO system results depend on configuration
state_of_art: PROPER; YAO

name: Acoustics, noise and vibration
definition: Given a structure, enclosure, room or outdoor site with sound or vibration sources, compute sound fields, transmission, noise levels and vibration response, or identify modal properties from tests.

name: Vibro-acoustic finite and boundary element analysis
definition: Given a vibrating structure and an interior or exterior fluid domain, compute sound pressure fields, radiated power and transmission.
inputs: structural and acoustic meshes; material and fluid properties; excitations
outputs: sound pressure fields; radiated power; transfer functions
benchmark_note: the EAA computational acoustics benchmark platform publishes reference cases
state_of_art: Simcenter 3D Acoustics; Actran; COMSOL Acoustics Module; Ansys Mechanical

name: Statistical energy analysis
definition: Given a system divided into subsystems with coupling and damping loss factors, compute high-frequency energy distribution and noise levels.
inputs: subsystem definitions; loss factors; input powers
outputs: subsystem energies; sound and vibration levels by band
benchmark_note: two-subsystem analytic cases verify solvers; vehicle data are proprietary
state_of_art: ESI VA One; Simcenter SEA

name: Outdoor sound propagation
definition: Given noise sources, terrain, buildings and barriers, compute sound levels at receivers by standard propagation methods.
inputs: source sound power; terrain and buildings; ground and meteorology
outputs: receiver levels; noise maps; barrier attenuation
benchmark_note: ISO/TR 17534-3 gives quality-assurance test cases for ISO 9613-2 implementations
state_of_art: SoundPLAN; CadnaA; IMMI

name: Room acoustics simulation
definition: Given a room geometry, surface absorption and sources, compute impulse responses and acoustic parameters such as reverberation time and clarity.
inputs: room geometry; absorption and scattering coefficients; source and receiver positions
outputs: impulse responses; reverberation time; clarity and speech indices
benchmark_note: PTB round robins and the BRAS database give measured rooms
state_of_art: ODEON; CATT-Acoustic; Treble

name: Loudspeaker and enclosure modeling
definition: Given driver parameters, enclosure and crossover design, compute frequency response, excursion and impedance.

outputs: frequency response; cone excursion; impedance

name: Experimental modal analysis
definition: Given measured frequency response functions or operating responses, identify natural frequencies, damping and mode shapes.
inputs: measured FRFs or response time histories; sensor geometry

name: Coupled multiphysics simulation
definition: Given a device whose behavior depends on interacting physics, solve the coupled fluid, structural, thermal, electrical or electrochemical fields together.

name: Fluid-structure interaction
definition: Given a flexible structure in a flow, solve coupled fluid and structural dynamics to compute deformation, loads and flutter or vortex-induced vibration.
inputs: fluid and structural models; coupling interface; flow conditions
outputs: coupled deformation and flow histories; loads; stability
benchmark_note: Turek-Hron FSI benchmark has reference values
state_of_art: Ansys System Coupling; Simcenter STAR-CCM+; Abaqus co-simulation; ADINA FSI

name: Microelectromechanical device simulation
definition: Given a micro-device layout, process stack and drive conditions, compute coupled electrostatic, mechanical and damping behavior.
inputs: layout and process stack; materials; drive voltages
outputs: displacements; capacitance; resonance; pull-in voltage
benchmark_note: parallel-plate pull-in has a closed form; device data are proprietary
state_of_art: CoventorMP; IntelliSuite; COMSOL MEMS Module

name: Electro-thermal-mechanical coupling
definition: Given conductors, piezoelectric or thermoelectric materials and electrical loads, compute coupled Joule heating, temperature, stress and electrical response.
inputs: geometry; coupled material properties; electrical and thermal loads
outputs: current density; temperature; stress; electrical response
benchmark_note: analytic coupled cases exist; few shared device benchmarks
state_of_art: COMSOL; Ansys Mechanical; Abaqus

name: Battery and fuel cell modeling
definition: Given cell geometry, electrochemical parameters and load cycles, compute voltage, current distribution, temperature and degradation.
inputs: electrode and electrolyte parameters; cell geometry; current or power profile

state_of_art: COMSOL Battery Design Module; GT-AutoLion; Simcenter Battery Design Studio

name: Semiconductor process and device simulation
definition: Given a fabrication recipe or a device structure, compute the resulting doping and geometry and the device's electrical behavior from carrier transport physics.

name: Semiconductor process simulation
definition: Given a starting wafer and a sequence of implant, diffusion, oxidation, deposition and etch steps, compute dopant profiles and the resulting device geometry.
inputs: wafer material and orientation; process step sequence with doses, energies, temperatures and times; mask layout
outputs: dopant concentration profiles; layer thicknesses; device cross-section geometry
benchmark_note: measured dopant depth profiles for standard implants and anneals are published; production recipes are proprietary
state_of_art: Synopsys Sentaurus Process; Silvaco Victory Process

name: Semiconductor device simulation
definition: Given a device structure with doping and applied biases, solve the coupled electrostatic and carrier transport equations for currents, capacitances and internal fields.
inputs: device geometry and doping; material and mobility models; bias conditions
outputs: current-voltage and capacitance-voltage curves; potential, field and carrier distributions
benchmark_note: the ideal diode and the MOS capacitor have closed-form solutions, and measured curves for reference devices are published
state_of_art: Synopsys Sentaurus Device; Silvaco Victory Device

name: Optical lithography simulation
definition: Given a mask pattern, illumination settings and a resist stack, compute the aerial image and the developed resist profile.
inputs: mask layout; illumination source and projection optics; resist and film stack
outputs: aerial image intensity; resist profile; process window
benchmark_note: mask-optimization contests publish optical models and test layouts; resist models are proprietary
state_of_art: KLA PROLITH; Synopsys Sentaurus Lithography

name: Manufacturing process simulation
definition: Given a part, tooling and process parameters, simulate a forming, casting, molding, joining, additive or machining process to predict defects, residual stress and final shape.

name: Casting fill and solidification
definition: Given a casting and gating design, alloy and process conditions, simulate mold filling and solidification to predict porosity, shrinkage and microstructure.
inputs: casting and mold geometry; alloy properties; pouring conditions
outputs: fill sequence; solidification times; porosity and shrinkage risk
benchmark_note: the Sirrell-Campbell sand-casting benchmark has measured results
state_of_art: MAGMASOFT; ESI ProCAST; Flow Science FLOW-3D CAST

name: Injection molding simulation
definition: Given a plastic part, gates, cooling and process settings, simulate filling, packing and cooling to predict weld lines, sink and warpage.
inputs: part and runner geometry; polymer data; process settings
outputs: fill pattern; pressures; shrinkage and warpage

name: Sheet metal forming simulation
definition: Given a blank, die surfaces and press conditions, simulate forming to predict thinning, splits, wrinkles and springback.
inputs: blank and die geometry; sheet material model; binder and press parameters
outputs: thickness and strain distributions; forming limit margins; springback
benchmark_note: NUMISHEET benchmark problems have measured results
state_of_art: AutoForm; ETA Dynaform; PAM-STAMP; Simufact Forming

name: Forging and extrusion simulation
definition: Given a billet, dies and process conditions, simulate bulk deformation to predict material flow, die fill, loads and defects.
inputs: billet and die geometry; flow stress data; temperatures and speeds
outputs: material flow; forming loads; laps and underfill

state_of_art: DEFORM; QForm; Simufact Forming; Forge NxT

name: Welding distortion and residual stress
definition: Given a weld joint, heat source and sequence, simulate thermal and mechanical history to predict distortion and residual stress.

outputs: temperature history; distortion; residual stress

state_of_art: ESI SYSWELD; Simufact Welding; Abaqus Welding Interface

name: Additive manufacturing process simulation

inputs: part and supports; layer and scan parameters; material
outputs: distortion; residual stress; melt-pool size; compensated geometry
benchmark_note: NIST AM-Bench challenge problems have measured results
state_of_art: Ansys Additive; Simufact Additive; Autodesk Netfabb Simulation

name: Metal cutting process simulation
definition: Given tool geometry, workpiece material and cutting parameters, predict cutting forces, temperatures, chip formation and tool wear.
inputs: tool geometry; workpiece flow stress; cutting speed, feed and depth
outputs: cutting forces; tool temperature; chip shape; wear
benchmark_note: CIRP cutting-model comparisons exist; results vary with friction assumptions
state_of_art: Third Wave AdvantEdge; DEFORM

name: Heat treatment and quenching simulation
definition: Given a part, steel grade and heat-treatment schedule, predict phase transformations, hardness, distortion and residual stress.
inputs: part geometry; alloy transformation data; heating and quench schedule
outputs: phase fractions; hardness; distortion; residual stress
benchmark_note: Jominy end-quench tests give reference hardness
state_of_art: DANTE; ESI SYSWELD; DEFORM-HT

name: Chemical process simulation
definition: Given chemical components, thermodynamic models, unit operations and stream connections, compute heat and material balances, phase behavior and equipment performance of a process.

name: Physical property and phase equilibrium
definition: Given a mixture composition, temperature and pressure and a property method, compute phase split, densities, enthalpies and transport properties.
inputs: components; property method and parameters; state conditions
outputs: phase fractions and compositions; thermodynamic and transport properties
benchmark_note: IAPWS-IF97 verification tables and NIST ThermoML experimental data

name: Computational thermochemistry
definition: Given elements, species databases, temperature and pressure, minimize Gibbs energy to compute equilibrium phases and compositions, including high-temperature and metallurgical systems.
inputs: species and solution databases; elemental amounts; temperature and pressure
outputs: equilibrium phases and amounts; phase diagrams; heat balances
benchmark_note: NIST-JANAF tables and assessed phase diagrams give references
state_of_art: FactSage; Thermo-Calc; HSC Chemistry

name: Steady-state flowsheet simulation
definition: Given feeds, unit operations and recycle connections, solve the plant heat and material balance.
inputs: feed streams; unit models and specifications; property method; topology
outputs: stream tables; equipment duties; converged recycles
benchmark_note: textbook flowsheets (for example Williams-Otto) have known answers; no maintained scored suite
state_of_art: Aspen Plus; Aspen HYSYS; AVEVA Process Simulation (PRO/II); CHEMCAD

name: Dynamic process simulation
definition: Given a flowsheet with holdups, equipment sizes and controllers, integrate plant behavior through disturbances, startups and shutdowns.

outputs: time histories of flows, levels, pressures and compositions
benchmark_note: the Tennessee Eastman challenge process is a shared reference plant
state_of_art: Aspen HYSYS Dynamics; gPROMS; AVEVA Dynamic Simulation

name: Reactor modeling and kinetics
definition: Given a reaction mechanism with rate laws and a reactor type, compute conversion, selectivity and temperature profiles.
inputs: reaction mechanism and rate constants; reactor type and size; feeds
outputs: conversion and selectivity; concentration and temperature profiles
benchmark_note: textbook reactor problems have closed forms; industrial kinetics are proprietary
state_of_art: Aspen Plus; Ansys Chemkin-Pro; gPROMS

name: Distillation and absorption column design
definition: Given feeds, column configuration and specifications, compute stage-by-stage compositions, duties and column sizing.
inputs: feed streams; stages and feed locations; specifications; property method
outputs: stage profiles; condenser and reboiler duties; tray or packing sizing
benchmark_note: published column test cases exist; no scored suite

name: Batch and bioprocess simulation
definition: Given a recipe of batch steps or a fermentation and purification train, compute material balances, cycle times and equipment utilization.
inputs: batch recipe or unit procedures; equipment; feeds; kinetics

state_of_art: SuperPro Designer; Aspen Batch Process Developer

name: Agitated vessel and mixing design
definition: Given a stirred vessel, impeller and fluid properties, compute power draw, blend time, heat transfer and suspension.
inputs: vessel and impeller geometry; fluid properties; speed
outputs: power number and draw; blend time; heat-transfer coefficient
benchmark_note: power-number correlations and published mixing experiments give references
state_of_art: VisiMix; M-Star CFD

name: Heat integration and pinch analysis
definition: Given hot and cold process streams, compute minimum utility targets and design a heat-exchanger network.

outputs: composite curves; utility targets; exchanger network

state_of_art: Aspen Energy Analyzer; PinCH; SuperTarget

name: Power plant heat balance
definition: Given a thermal power cycle of turbines, boilers, heaters and condensers, compute the heat balance, heat rate and off-design performance.
inputs: cycle topology; component characteristics; ambient and load conditions

state_of_art: Thermoflow; EBSILON Professional; PEPSE

name: Power system analysis
definition: Given an electrical network of generators, lines, transformers, loads and protection, compute power flows, fault currents, protection behavior, stability and transients.

benchmark_note: IEEE PES distribution test feeders have reference results
state_of_art: CYME; Synergi Electric; PowerFactory

state_of_art: ETAP; SKM PowerTools; EasyPower; PowerFactory

state_of_art: SKM CAPTOR; ETAP Star; ASPEN OneLiner

name: Arc flash hazard analysis

state_of_art: ETAP; SKM Arc Flash; EasyPower

benchmark_note: IEEE PES task-force benchmark systems (Kundur two-area, IEEE 39-bus) have reference responses

name: Electromagnetic transient simulation

outputs: instantaneous voltage and current waveforms; overvoltages

state_of_art: PSCAD/EMTDC; EMTP; RTDS

name: Harmonic analysis
definition: Given a network and nonlinear loads or converters, compute harmonic voltages and currents, distortion indices and resonances.

benchmark_note: IEEE harmonics modeling task-force test systems have reference results
state_of_art: ETAP; SKM HI_WAVE; PowerFactory

outputs: voltage drop; conductor and conduit sizes
benchmark_note: National Electrical Code examples give reference sizes
state_of_art: ETAP; SKM; Trimble Design Master Electrical

name: Power electronic converter simulation
definition: Given a converter topology, switches, passive components and control, simulate switching waveforms, losses and control response.
inputs: converter schematic; device models; control scheme
outputs: voltage and current waveforms; losses; efficiency; ripple

definition: Given a turbine's blades, tower, controller and wind fields, simulate coupled aero-servo-elastic response to compute loads and power.

outputs: load time series; fatigue equivalent loads; power

name: Hybrid and microgrid system sizing
definition: Given loads, renewable resources, storage, generators and costs, simulate dispatch over a year and select the least-cost system configuration.

outputs: energy production; payback and net present value; emissions

name: Water distribution network analysis
definition: Given a pressurized water network, demands, pumps, tanks and controls, compute flows, pressures and water quality over an extended period.
inputs: pipe network; demands and patterns; pumps, tanks and valves; controls
outputs: pressures and flows over time; tank levels; water age and chlorine
benchmark_note: EPANET example networks and the Battle of the Water Networks challenges
state_of_art: WaterGEMS; InfoWater Pro; KYPipe

name: Sewer and storm drainage network analysis
definition: Given a gravity sewer or storm drain network and inflows, compute flows, depths, surcharging and overflows over time.

benchmark_note: SWMM ships verification examples; no shared scored benchmark

name: Site stormwater runoff and detention

name: Multiphase well and pipeline flow
definition: Given wells and flowlines with oil, gas and water, compute pressure and holdup profiles and deliverability.

state_of_art: DOE MEASUR; AIRMaster+

name: Radiation transport and nuclear systems
definition: Given a reactor, shield or fissile system with materials and sources, compute neutron and photon transport, criticality, dose rates, isotopic depletion and reactor thermal-hydraulic response.

name: Monte Carlo radiation transport
definition: Given 3D geometry, material compositions, cross-section data and sources, track particles to compute fluxes, dose rates and reaction rates.
inputs: geometry; materials; nuclear data libraries; source definition; tallies
outputs: flux and dose-rate tallies with statistical uncertainty
benchmark_note: the SINBAD shielding benchmark database has measured experiments
state_of_art: MCNP; Serpent; SCALE KENO/Shift

name: Deterministic radiation transport
definition: Given geometry, multigroup cross sections and sources, solve the transport equation by discrete ordinates or similar methods for flux distributions.
inputs: geometry; multigroup cross sections; sources; angular quadrature
outputs: angular and scalar flux distributions; dose rates
benchmark_note: Kobayashi 3D transport benchmarks and SINBAD experiments
state_of_art: DORT/TORT; PARTISN; Attila

name: Point-kernel shielding calculation
definition: Given source strengths, simple shield geometries and buildup factors, compute gamma dose rates at receptor points.
inputs: source spectra; shield layers and distances; buildup data
outputs: dose rates at receptors
benchmark_note: Monte Carlo reference cases check point-kernel results
state_of_art: MicroShield; QAD-CGGP; RayXpert

name: Criticality safety analysis
definition: Given a fissile system's geometry and compositions, compute the neutron multiplication factor and safety margins.
inputs: geometry; fissile and moderator compositions; nuclear data
outputs: k-effective with uncertainty; margins to subcritical limits
benchmark_note: the ICSBEP handbook has thousands of evaluated critical experiments
state_of_art: SCALE KENO; MCNP; Serpent

name: Isotopic depletion and decay
definition: Given fuel compositions, irradiation history and cross sections, compute isotopic inventories, decay heat and source terms over time.
inputs: initial compositions; power or flux history; decay and cross-section data
outputs: isotopic inventories; decay heat; activity and radiation sources
benchmark_note: the SFCOMPO spent-fuel isotopic database gives measured inventories
state_of_art: SCALE ORIGEN; Serpent; FISPACT-II

name: Reactor core physics
definition: Given a reactor core loading, assemblies and operating state, compute power distributions, reactivity coefficients and control-rod worths.
inputs: assembly and core geometry; fuel loading; thermal feedback state
outputs: power distribution; k-effective; reactivity coefficients
benchmark_note: the C5G7 benchmark and the VERA core physics progression problems
state_of_art: CASMO/SIMULATE; Serpent; PARCS

name: Reactor system thermal-hydraulics
definition: Given a reactor coolant system model and an accident or transient scenario, compute two-phase flows, temperatures and pressures over time.
inputs: system nodalization; component models; initial state; transient scenario
outputs: pressure, temperature and flow histories; peak cladding temperature
benchmark_note: OECD/NEA International Standard Problems compare codes against experiments
state_of_art: RELAP5; TRACE; CATHARE

name: Simulation pre- and post-processing
definition: Given CAD geometry and analysis intent, prepare simulation-ready geometry and meshes and assemble solver models; given results, extract and visualize derived quantities.

name: Simulation geometry preparation
definition: Given CAD geometry, remove small features, repair gaps and extract midsurfaces or beam idealizations for analysis.
inputs: CAD solids or surfaces; defeaturing rules; idealization choices
outputs: watertight or idealized geometry ready for meshing
benchmark_note: defeaturing quality lacks agreed metrics
state_of_art: Ansys SpaceClaim; Altair HyperMesh; Simcenter 3D

name: Surface and volume mesh generation
definition: Given analysis geometry and sizing controls, generate surface and volume meshes that meet element quality targets.
inputs: geometry; size fields; element types; quality targets
outputs: mesh; quality statistics
benchmark_note: the AIAA Geometry and Mesh Generation Workshop compares meshing for shared geometries
state_of_art: Pointwise; Altair HyperMesh; Ansys Meshing; ANSA

name: Solver model assembly
definition: Given a mesh and analysis intent, assign materials, properties, loads, constraints and solver controls and write a solver input deck.
inputs: mesh; material and section data; load and boundary definitions
outputs: complete solver input deck
benchmark_note: correctness is judged only through solver results
state_of_art: Altair HyperMesh; Simcenter Femap; Ansys Workbench; ANSA

name: Simulation result visualization
definition: Given solver result fields, compute derived quantities and render contours, streamlines, iso-surfaces and animations.
inputs: result files with field data; derived-quantity definitions
outputs: plots, images and animations; extracted values
benchmark_note: rendering quality has no reference answer
state_of_art: Tecplot 360; EnSight; Altair HyperView

name: Design optimization, uncertainty and validation
definition: Given parameterized simulation models, objectives and uncertainties, search for optimal designs, propagate uncertainty, and verify and validate the models against references and tests.

name: Structural topology optimization
definition: Given a design space, loads, constraints and a material budget, compute the material layout that optimizes stiffness or another response.
inputs: design domain mesh; loads and supports; volume fraction; manufacturing constraints
outputs: optimal material density field; interpreted geometry
benchmark_note: MBB beam and cantilever problems have well-known reference compliances
state_of_art: Altair OptiStruct; Tosca; Ansys Mechanical topology optimization

name: Shape and sizing optimization
definition: Given a parameterized model and constraints, adjust shape or size variables to optimize performance using gradients or search.
inputs: design parameters and bounds; objectives; constraints; simulation model
outputs: optimal parameters; constraint margins; sensitivities
benchmark_note: classical ten-bar truss and airfoil design cases are shared; most problems are bespoke
state_of_art: Altair HyperStudy; Dassault Isight; MSC Nastran SOL 200; modeFRONTIER

name: Multidisciplinary design optimization
definition: Given coupled discipline models of a system, couple and optimize them together across disciplines.
inputs: discipline models; coupling variables; system objectives and constraints
outputs: optimal system design; discipline trade-offs
benchmark_note: the NASA MDO test suite and the Sellar problem give references
state_of_art: ModelCenter; Isight; HEEDS

name: Uncertainty propagation and structural reliability
definition: Given a model with random inputs, compute output distributions, sensitivities and probabilities of failure.
inputs: model; input distributions and correlations; limit states
outputs: output statistics; sensitivity indices; failure probability
benchmark_note: published structural reliability benchmark studies give reference failure probabilities
state_of_art: Ansys optiSLang; Dakota; UQLab

name: Reduced-order and surrogate modeling
definition: Given high-fidelity simulation results, build a fast approximate model that reproduces the response over a parameter range.
inputs: training simulations; parameter ranges; accuracy target
outputs: surrogate or reduced model; error estimates
benchmark_note: shared parametric test problems exist; accuracy depends on the training budget
state_of_art: Ansys Twin Builder; Altair romAI; optiSLang

name: Simulation verification and validation
definition: Given a simulation code or result and reference solutions or experiments, quantify numerical error and model-form error.
inputs: code or results; manufactured or analytical solutions; mesh series; experimental data
outputs: convergence orders; discretization uncertainty; validation metrics
benchmark_note: manufactured solutions and the ASME V&V 20 example give exact checks
state_of_art: Dakota

name: Plan and control production
definition: Turning a design into made things: programming machine tools and robots, programming and running plant-floor control, executing and scheduling production, and checking what was made.

name: Manufacturing process planning
definition: Given a product design and the plant's resources, decide how it will be made: operations and their order, machines, setups, tooling, routing and expected cost.

name: Machining process plan generation
definition: Given a part model with features and tolerances, stock and available machines, produce setups, operation sequence and machine, fixture and tool assignments.
inputs: part model with machining features and tolerances, stock, machine and tooling catalogue
outputs: process plan: setups, ordered operations, resource assignments
benchmark_note: setup count, tool changes and estimated machining time can be scored on shared test parts, but no standard suite exists
state_of_art: Siemens Teamcenter Manufacturing Process Planner; DELMIA Process Engineer

name: Manufacturing bill and routing authoring
definition: Given an engineering bill of materials and plant layout, produce a manufacturing bill of materials grouped by station and a routing of operations with work centres and standard times.
inputs: engineering bill of materials, plant work centres, standard times
outputs: manufacturing bill of materials, routing (bill of process)
benchmark_note: correct structure depends on plant conventions and there is no reference data
state_of_art: Siemens Teamcenter Manufacturing; PTC Windchill MPMLink; DELMIA Process Engineer

name: Work instruction authoring
definition: Given a process plan, 3D models and quality requirements, produce step-by-step operator instructions with visuals, parameters and checks.
inputs: process plan, product models, quality checks
outputs: illustrated work instructions per station
benchmark_note: quality is judged by operators and there is no benchmark
state_of_art: Dozuki; VKS; Tulip

name: Manufacturing cost estimation
definition: Given a part model or drawing, material, process route and shop rates, estimate cycle time, piece cost and tooling cost.
inputs: part model or drawing, material, process route, machine and labour rates
outputs: cycle-time and cost estimate, quote
benchmark_note: estimates can be scored against actual costed jobs, but such data are private
state_of_art: aPriori; Costimator; Paperless Parts; PRICE TruePlanning; Galorath SEER; Aspen Capital Cost Estimator

name: Cutting tool and cutting data management
definition: Given tool assemblies, workpiece materials and machines, maintain the tool library and compute recommended speeds, feeds and tool life.
inputs: tool components and assemblies, workpiece material, machine limits
outputs: tool library records, cutting parameters, expected tool life
benchmark_note: recommended cutting data can be checked against measured tool life and force data, which are scarce
state_of_art: Sandvik Coromant CoroPlus ToolGuide; ZOLLER TMS Tool Management Solutions; TDM Systems; HSMAdvisor; MachiningCloud

name: Milling toolpath programming
definition: Given part and stock geometry, fixtures, cutting tools and the machine's axis configuration, generate collision-free milling toolpaths that bring the stock to the part within tolerance.

name: 2.5-axis milling
definition: Given 2D profiles or prismatic features with depths, generate contouring, pocketing, facing, slotting, chamfering and engraving paths at discrete Z levels.
inputs: 2D profiles or prismatic features, depths, tools, stock, fixture
outputs: cutter location path or controller code
benchmark_note: machining time, air-cutting fraction and gouge-free coverage are computable by stock simulation on shared prismatic parts; config/capabilities.csv already lists cam-bench for CAM
state_of_art: Mastercam Mill; Autodesk Fusion; SolidCAM

name: Hole-making cycles
definition: Given hole features (diameter, depth, thread, tolerance), choose drilling, peck, tapping, boring, reaming or thread-milling cycles and an efficient visiting order.
inputs: hole features, tools, machine canned-cycle set
outputs: ordered hole operations with canned cycles
benchmark_note: cycle choice can be checked against thread and depth specifications and the visiting order is a travelling-salesman instance
state_of_art: Mastercam Mill; Siemens NX CAM; ESPRIT

name: Three-axis surface roughing
definition: Given 3D part and stock, remove bulk material with constant-engagement (adaptive, trochoidal) or Z-level clearing, leaving uniform stock for finishing.
inputs: part surfaces, stock model, tools and holders, engagement limits
outputs: roughing toolpath, remaining stock model
benchmark_note: removal rate, engagement violations and remaining stock are computable by stock simulation on reference parts
state_of_art: Autodesk PowerMill; Mastercam Dynamic Motion; hyperMILL

name: Three-axis surface finishing
definition: Given freeform surfaces and remaining stock, generate parallel, waterline, scallop, pencil and rest-machining passes that meet a scallop-height and surface tolerance.
inputs: part surfaces, remaining stock, ball or bull-nose tools, tolerance, scallop height
outputs: finishing toolpaths
benchmark_note: scallop height, gouges and deviation from the design surface are computable from simulated stock
state_of_art: Autodesk PowerMill; Tebis; WorkNC; Cimatron

name: Indexed five-axis (3+2) milling
definition: Given a part on a rotary-tilting machine, choose fixed tool orientations that reach all features in few setups, and generate three-axis paths in each tilted work plane.
inputs: part model, machine rotary limits, fixture, tools
outputs: set of tool orientations and per-plane toolpaths
benchmark_note: number of orientations and feature accessibility are scoreable; tilted-plane output must be checked by machine simulation
state_of_art: hyperMILL; Mastercam Multiaxis; Siemens NX CAM

name: Simultaneous four-axis rotary milling
definition: Given a part machined around one rotary axis, generate wrapped and rotary-contouring paths that move the rotary axis during cutting.
inputs: part model, rotary axis definition, tools
outputs: four-axis toolpath
benchmark_note: wrap accuracy is checkable by simulation but few reference parts exist
state_of_art: Mastercam Multiaxis; Autodesk Fusion; ESPRIT

name: Simultaneous five-axis milling
definition: Given freeform or ruled surfaces, generate paths with a continuously varying tool axis (swarf, flowline, impeller, port) that avoid holder and spindle collisions and keep the axis smooth.
inputs: part surfaces, tools and holders, machine kinematics and limits
outputs: five-axis toolpath with tool-axis vectors
benchmark_note: the ISO 10791-7 cone frustum and similar test pieces give reference geometry; gouges, collisions and axis reversals are measurable in simulation
state_of_art: hyperMILL; Siemens NX CAM; Autodesk PowerMill; Mastercam Multiaxis

name: Feature-based automatic programming
definition: Given a solid model, recognize machining features and apply stored strategies to produce a complete program with little manual input.
inputs: solid model, feature-strategy knowledge base, tools, machine
outputs: recognized features and complete toolpath set
benchmark_note: feature recognition is scoreable on labelled CAD sets (MFCAD, MFCAD++) and the resulting programs by stock simulation
state_of_art: CAMWorks; Autodesk FeatureCAM; Siemens NX CAM

name: Turning, mill-turn and grinding programming
definition: Given a rotational part, bar or blank stock and a lathe, multitasking or grinding machine configuration, generate synchronized programs for its spindles, turrets and axes.

name: Two-axis turning
definition: Given a turned profile and stock, generate facing, OD and ID roughing and finishing, grooving, threading and parting with tool-nose compensation.
inputs: rotational profile, stock, turning tools
outputs: lathe program
benchmark_note: cycle time and profile deviation after simulated cutting are scoreable on reference turned parts
state_of_art: Mastercam Lathe; ESPRIT; GibbsCAM; Autodesk Fusion

name: Live-tool C and Y-axis milling
definition: Given a turned part with flats, cross holes and slots, generate milling on a lathe using polar or cylindrical interpolation with the C axis and optional Y axis.
inputs: part model, lathe with live tools, C and Y axis limits
outputs: combined turning and milling program
benchmark_note: verifiable only by machine simulation with the specific turret and spindle model
state_of_art: ESPRIT; GibbsCAM; Mastercam Mill-Turn

name: B-axis mill-turn multitasking
definition: Given a complex part on a machine with a tilting milling head, main and sub-spindles, order turning and multi-axis milling operations and spindle transfers.
inputs: part model, multitasking machine model, tools
outputs: multitasking program with transfers
benchmark_note: needs full machine kinematic models; cycle time and collisions are measurable in simulation
state_of_art: ESPRIT; Mastercam Mill-Turn; Siemens NX CAM; hyperMILL MILL-TURN

name: Multi-channel and Swiss-type synchronization
definition: Given operations for a sliding-headstock or twin-turret lathe, assign them to channels, insert wait and sync codes and balance the cycle.
inputs: operation list, machine channels, turrets and spindles
outputs: synchronized multi-channel program and timing chart
benchmark_note: channel balancing is a scheduling problem and sync validity is checkable in simulation, but machine models are proprietary
state_of_art: ESPRIT; GibbsCAM; Autodesk PartMaker

name: Tool and cutter grinding programming
definition: Given a cutter specification (flutes, helix, rake, relief, point), generate wheel paths for a multi-axis tool grinder.
inputs: cutter geometry, wheel set, grinder kinematics
outputs: grinding program and simulated tool geometry
benchmark_note: the simulated ground geometry can be compared with the specification, but grinder models are machine-specific
state_of_art: ANCA ToolRoom; Walter Helitronic Tool Studio; NUMROTOplus

name: Sheet and profile cutting programming
definition: Given flat, linear or tubular stock and part outlines or sheet-metal models, lay parts out on the stock and generate cutting, punching, bending or wire-erosion programs.

name: Two-dimensional profile cutting paths
definition: Given nested part outlines and a laser, plasma, oxyfuel, waterjet or knife cutter, generate cut paths with lead-ins, kerf compensation, pierce points, micro-joints and a cut order that limits heat and tip-up.
inputs: nested layout, cutting process and machine parameters
outputs: cutting program
benchmark_note: cut length, pierce count and rapid travel are scoreable; cut quality is not
state_of_art: SigmaNEST; ProNest; Lantek Expert; TRUMPF TruTops Boost

name: Irregular nesting on sheet and plate
definition: Given irregular part shapes, quantities and sheets or plates, place parts with allowed rotations to maximize utilization, using common-line cutting and part-in-part where possible.
inputs: part outlines, quantities, rotation rules, sheet sizes and remnants
outputs: nested layouts, utilization, remnant definitions
benchmark_note: ESICUP irregular nesting instances (albano, dagli, jakobs, shapes, swim) have best-known utilizations
state_of_art: SigmaNEST; ProNest; Lantek Expert; TRUMPF TruTops Boost

name: Rectangular and guillotine panel cutting
definition: Given rectangular parts and boards or glass sheets, generate cutting patterns that respect guillotine stages and saw constraints with minimum waste.
inputs: rectangular part list, board sizes, kerf, guillotine stage limits
outputs: cutting patterns and saw programs
benchmark_note: the ROADEF/EURO 2018 glass-cutting challenge and classical guillotine instances give reference solutions
state_of_art: HOMAG Cut Rite

name: Linear cutting stock optimization
definition: Given required lengths of bars, tubes, extrusions or lumber and the stock lengths available, choose cutting patterns that minimize waste.
inputs: required lengths and quantities, stock lengths, kerf
outputs: cutting patterns and cut lists
benchmark_note: BPPLIB and classic one-dimensional instances (Falkenauer, Scholl) have proven optima
state_of_art: SigmaNEST; Lantek Expert

name: Turret punch programming
definition: Given nested sheet parts and a punch press tool turret, assign tools to stations and sequence hits, nibbling and repositioning to avoid clamps.
inputs: nested layout, punch tool library, turret configuration, clamp positions
outputs: punch program with tool setup
benchmark_note: hit count, tool changes and travel are scoreable, but machine constraints vary by vendor
state_of_art: TRUMPF TruTops Punch; Vero RADAN; JETCAM Expert

name: Press brake bend programming
definition: Given a sheet-metal part, unfold it, choose bend sequence and tooling, set backgauge positions and check part-tool-machine collisions.
inputs: sheet-metal model, material, press brake and tool library
outputs: flat pattern, bend sequence, tool setup, press brake program
benchmark_note: bend-sequence feasibility is checkable by collision simulation, but no public part set exists
state_of_art: AMADA Dr. ABE_Bend; TRUMPF TruTops Bend; Bystronic BySoft; LVD CADMAN

name: Tube and profile cutting programming
definition: Given tubes or structural shapes with cut features, generate rotary laser or plasma cutting paths with bevels and nest parts along the stock length.
inputs: tube or profile part models, stock lengths, rotary cutter model
outputs: tube cutting program and length nest
benchmark_note: path validity and stock use are computable in simulation, but machine models are proprietary
state_of_art: Lantek Flex3d; BLM Artube; TRUMPF TruTops Boost

name: Wire electrical discharge machining programming
definition: Given 2D contours or ruled upper and lower profiles, generate two-axis and four-axis taper wire paths with skim cuts, tabs and threading points.
inputs: part contours or ruled surfaces, wire and machine technology tables
outputs: wire erosion program
benchmark_note: contour offsets and taper geometry are checkable by simulation; technology tables are vendor-specific
state_of_art: Mastercam Wire; ESPRIT; PEPS; FIKUS Visualcam

name: Fabric marker making
definition: Given graded garment pattern pieces, fabric width and rules for grain, nap and pattern matching, nest pieces into a marker and generate the cutter program.
inputs: graded pattern pieces, size ratios, fabric width and properties, matching rules
outputs: marker layout, efficiency, knife-cutter program
benchmark_note: ESICUP apparel instances (shirts, trousers) are standard irregular strip-packing benchmarks
state_of_art: Gerber AccuMark; Lectra Diamino

name: NC post-processing and verification
definition: Given toolpaths or NC programs and a model of the machine and controller, produce controller-specific code, verify it by simulation, optimize it, and deliver it to the machine.

name: Post-processor development
definition: Given a machine's kinematics, controller dialect and cycles, build and configure a post-processor that turns neutral toolpath data into that machine's code.
inputs: machine kinematic chain and limits, controller manual, sample programs
outputs: post-processor configuration or script
benchmark_note: a post can be scored by round-tripping reference toolpaths through a machine simulator
state_of_art: ICAM CAM-POST; IMSpost; Siemens NX Post Configurator

name: Two and three-axis code generation
definition: Given toolpaths for a lathe or three-axis mill, emit controller code with correct arcs, canned cycles, compensation, tool changes and safe starts.
inputs: cutter location data, post-processor, controller dialect
outputs: controller program
benchmark_note: output can be executed in an open controller interpreter and the resulting path compared with the source toolpath
state_of_art: Autodesk post processors; Mastercam post processors; IMSpost

name: Five-axis kinematic transformation
definition: Given tool positions and axis vectors, compute rotary and linear axis values for a table-table, head-head or head-table machine, choosing solutions, handling singularities and wrap, and linearizing large rotary moves.
inputs: tool position and orientation sequence, machine kinematics and limits
outputs: axis-space program with feed rates (including inverse-time)
benchmark_note: axis solutions are exactly checkable from the kinematics, and singularity and wrap handling are scoreable on standard test paths
state_of_art: ICAM CAM-POST; IMSpost; Siemens NX Post Configurator

name: NC program verification by material removal
definition: Given an NC program, stock, tools and design model, simulate material removal and report gouges, excess stock and program errors.
inputs: NC program, stock, tool assemblies, design model
outputs: simulated in-process stock, deviation map, error list
benchmark_note: deviation between simulated stock and the design model is computable, and programs with seeded errors make a test set
state_of_art: VERICUT; NCSIMUL; CIMCO Machine Simulation

name: Machine collision simulation
definition: Given an NC program and a full machine model with fixtures and holders, simulate controller-level motion and report collisions, near misses and overtravel.
inputs: NC program, machine model, fixtures, tool assemblies
outputs: collision and overtravel report
benchmark_note: collisions and overtravel on seeded test programs are exact pass or fail checks
state_of_art: VERICUT; NCSIMUL

name: Physics-based feed-rate optimization
definition: Given an NC program, tools and material, adjust feed per segment so that chip load or cutting force stays within limits while minimizing cycle time.
inputs: NC program, stock simulation, tool and material cutting model
outputs: optimized NC program, predicted cycle time and forces
benchmark_note: cycle-time reduction is computable, but force limits need cutting-force models calibrated per material
state_of_art: VERICUT Force; NCSIMUL Optitool

name: Shop-floor and conversational programming
definition: Given a drawing at the machine, write or edit NC code by hand or through a controller's conversational dialogs, with backplot and checks.
inputs: part drawing, controller dialect or conversational cycles
outputs: edited or conversational NC program
benchmark_note: hand or machine-written G-code can be scored by simulation against a target part; conversational dialects are vendor-specific
state_of_art: CIMCO Edit; NCPlot; FANUC MANUAL GUIDE i

name: NC program transfer and management
definition: Given approved NC programs and networked machines, deliver programs by DNC or file transfer, drip-feed large programs, and keep revisions and comparisons.
inputs: NC programs, machine connections, approval state
outputs: transferred programs, revision history
benchmark_note: a transfer and revision-control function whose only metric is correctness
state_of_art: CIMCO NC-Base; Predator DNC

name: Additive manufacturing build preparation
definition: Given 3D part models, an additive process and a machine, produce a validated build: repaired meshes, orientation, supports, layout and machine-specific layer or scan data.

name: Build orientation and part packing
definition: Given parts and a build volume, choose each part's orientation (support volume, surface quality, height) and arrange them on the plate or in the powder volume.
inputs: part meshes, machine build volume, orientation criteria
outputs: oriented parts, build layout, packing density
benchmark_note: packing density, build height and support volume are computable on shared part sets
state_of_art: Materialise Magics; Autodesk Netfabb

name: Support structure generation
definition: Given an oriented part and process rules, detect overhangs and generate block, tree or lattice supports.
inputs: oriented mesh, overhang angle and process rules
outputs: support geometry
benchmark_note: support volume and contact area are computable, but printability needs physical trials
state_of_art: Materialise Magics; Autodesk Netfabb; Formlabs PreForm

name: Material extrusion slicing
definition: Given a mesh and printer and material profile, slice into layers and generate perimeters, infill, travel and temperatures as printer code.
inputs: mesh, printer profile, material profile
outputs: printer G-code, time and material estimate
benchmark_note: print time, material use and geometric fidelity of the toolpath are computable without printing
state_of_art: Ultimaker Cura; PrusaSlicer; Bambu Studio; Simplify3D; Stratasys GrabCAD Print

name: Vat photopolymerization slicing
definition: Given a supported mesh and resin profile, produce layer images or laser paths with exposure settings, hollowing and drain holes.
inputs: supported mesh, resin and printer profile
outputs: layer image stack or laser scan file
benchmark_note: layer images are checkable against the mesh, but cure behaviour needs physical calibration
state_of_art: Formlabs PreForm; CHITUBOX; Lychee Slicer

name: Powder bed fusion scan preparation
definition: Given a packed build, generate contour and hatch vectors, scan strategy (stripes, islands, rotation) and region parameters as a machine build file.
inputs: build layout, material parameter sets, machine specification
outputs: layer scan vectors and build file
benchmark_note: vector coverage and scan time are computable; melt-pool quality needs simulation or trials
state_of_art: EOSPRINT; Materialise Magics; Autodesk Netfabb; 3D Systems 3DXpert; Renishaw QuantAM

name: Directed energy deposition path planning
definition: Given a part or repair region, plan bead paths and deposition-head orientation for multi-axis wire or powder deposition, including non-planar layers.
inputs: part or repair geometry, bead model, multi-axis machine or robot
outputs: deposition toolpath
benchmark_note: coverage and bead overlap are computable, but deposited geometry needs process models
state_of_art: Siemens NX Additive Manufacturing; ADAXIS AdaOne; Autodesk PowerMill

name: Jetting build preparation
definition: Given multi-material or coloured models, assign materials and colours per voxel and produce halftoned layer images for material or binder jetting.
inputs: coloured or multi-material models, printer material set
outputs: per-layer droplet or binder images
benchmark_note: colour and material placement are checkable against the model, but appearance needs printing
state_of_art: Stratasys GrabCAD Print; HP SmartStream 3D Build Manager

name: Industrial robot programming
definition: Given a work cell (robots, tools, fixtures, parts) and a process, produce executable robot programs with validated reach, collision-free motion, calibrated frames and acceptable cycle time.

name: Robot program authoring
definition: Given a cell and task description, write the robot program in the vendor language with frames, I/O handshakes and error recovery.
inputs: cell layout, task description, I/O list, frames
outputs: robot program (vendor language)
benchmark_note: programs can run in vendor virtual controllers, but the languages are proprietary and benchmarks are only emerging
state_of_art: ABB RobotStudio; FANUC ROBOGUIDE; KUKA.WorkVisual; Universal Robots PolyScope

name: Offline programming and cell simulation
definition: Given 3D models of robots, tools, fixtures and parts, program and simulate the cell with a virtual controller to check reach, collisions and cycle time before download.
inputs: cell CAD, robot models, virtual controller, program
outputs: validated program, reach and cycle-time report
benchmark_note: reach and cycle time are computable in simulation, but accuracy on the real cell depends on calibration
state_of_art: ABB RobotStudio; FANUC ROBOGUIDE; Siemens Process Simulate; DELMIA Robotics; RoboDK; Visual Components; KUKA.Sim

name: Collision-free motion planning
definition: Given robot kinematics, start and goal poses and the cell's obstacles, compute a collision-free, time-parameterized joint trajectory.
inputs: robot model, obstacle geometry, start and goal
outputs: joint trajectory
benchmark_note: MotionBenchMaker and OMPL benchmarking score success rate, path quality and planning time
state_of_art: Realtime Robotics RapidPlan; Siemens Process Simulate

name: Process path generation
definition: Given part geometry and a process (arc or spot welding, painting, dispensing, deburring, machining), generate tool paths, orientations and process parameters for the robot.
inputs: part CAD with seams or surfaces, process tool, robot and positioner
outputs: robot process paths with parameters
benchmark_note: coverage uniformity and seam-following error are computable in simulation; process quality needs trials
state_of_art: Octopuz; RoboDK; DELMIA Robotics; ABB RobotStudio

name: Robot task sequencing and coordination
definition: Given many operations (welds, picks) and one or more robots with shared zones, allocate and order them to minimize cycle time without interference.
inputs: operation list with poses, robots, interference zones
outputs: per-robot sequences and interlocks, cycle time
benchmark_note: the core is a generalized travelling-salesman problem with public instances, but cell interference constraints are not standardized
state_of_art: Siemens Process Simulate; DELMIA Robotics

name: Robot and tool calibration
definition: Given measurements of the robot and tool, identify tool centre point, user frames, camera-to-robot transform and kinematic parameter corrections.
inputs: measured poses or images, nominal kinematics
outputs: calibrated tool, frames and kinematic parameters
benchmark_note: residual pose error after calibration can be scored on simulated or published measurement sets against ISO 9283 criteria
state_of_art: ABB Absolute Accuracy; Dynalog DynaCal; RoboDK

name: Vision-guided picking
definition: Given 2D or 3D sensor data of parts in a tray or bin, estimate part poses, choose grasps and plan the approach.
inputs: images or point clouds, part models, gripper model
outputs: part poses, ranked grasps, pick trajectories
benchmark_note: the BOP 6D pose benchmark and GraspNet-1Billion score pose estimation and grasp quality

name: Robot safety configuration

name: Programmable controller programming
definition: Given a control specification and I/O list for a machine or process, author, test and deploy controller logic in the IEC 61131-3 or IEC 61499 languages.

name: Function block diagram programming

name: Sequential function chart programming

name: Distributed function block applications
definition: Given a control application spanning several devices, model it as event-driven IEC 61499 function block networks and map them to devices.

definition: Given axis mechanics and motion requirements, configure servo and frequency drives, program PLCopen motion blocks, cams and electronic gearing, and tune axes.

definition: Given a cause-and-effect matrix and safety requirements, program safety controller or instrumented-system logic with voting, bypass and reset handling.

definition: Given controller code and a simulated machine or plant, test and formally verify the logic before startup.

outputs: test results, counterexamples, commissioning report

name: Supervisory and process control
definition: Given a running plant with field instruments and controllers, show its state to operators, acquire and archive data, raise alarms, and compute regulatory and advanced control actions.

name: Operator display design
definition: Given a process and its tags, build overview and detail displays, faceplates and navigation following high-performance HMI practice.
inputs: process diagrams, tag list, display standards
outputs: HMI screens and faceplates

name: Distributed control strategy configuration

name: Control loop performance monitoring

name: Advanced process control
definition: Given plant step-test data and operating constraints, identify multivariable models and configure a model predictive or rule-based supervisory controller over the base control layer.

outputs: controller models and configuration, predicted benefits

definition: Given a dynamic plant model and an emulated control system, run training scenarios (start-up, upsets, trips) and record trainee performance.

name: Batch control and recipe management

name: Formula and specification management
definition: Given ingredient specifications and product targets, maintain formulas, scale them, apply substitutions and compute composition and cost.

name: Work order execution and operator guidance

inputs: work order, routing, work instructions, bill of materials

name: Machine and production data collection
definition: Given connected machines and lines, capture states, counts, cycle times and process parameters through equipment interfaces.
inputs: machine signals over MTConnect, OPC UA, SECS/GEM or I/O

name: Production performance analysis
definition: Given equipment states and production counts, compute overall equipment effectiveness, loss categories and other operations key performance indicators.

name: Production planning and scheduling

definition: Given a multipurpose batch plant with shared units, intermediate storage and campaign rules, schedule batches to meet demand.

definition: Given equipment lists, nameplate data and site structure, build a functional-location and equipment hierarchy with classes and attributes.
inputs: equipment lists, nameplate data, drawings, site and system structure
outputs: asset hierarchy with taxonomy classes, attributes and parent-child links
benchmark_note: classifying free-text equipment descriptions into ISO 14224 classes can be scored against labeled registers, but few public registers exist
state_of_art: IBM Maximo Application Suite; SAP S/4HANA Asset Management; HxGN EAM; IFS Cloud EAM

name: Work request and order lifecycle
definition: Given a reported problem or due task, create, prioritize, assign, track and close a work order with labor, parts and completion data.
inputs: work requests, asset, priority rules, crews, parts
outputs: work orders with status history, labor and material charges, completion notes
benchmark_note: priority and trade assignment from request text is scoreable; the lifecycle itself is workflow, not computation
state_of_art: IBM Maximo; SAP Plant Maintenance; eMaint; Fiix; UpKeep; Limble CMMS
open_tools: openMAINT; Atlas CMMS; ERPNext; Odoo Maintenance

name: Preventive maintenance scheduling
definition: Given time-, meter- or calendar-based maintenance rules and asset usage readings, generate due preventive tasks, calibration recalls and inspection routes.
inputs: PM rules (intervals, meters, seasons), usage and meter readings, asset groups
outputs: due-task list and generated work orders, route sheets, forecasts of upcoming work
benchmark_note: due dates from rules and meter histories have exact answers
state_of_art: IBM Maximo; SAP Plant Maintenance; Fleetio; AssetWorks FleetFocus

name: Maintenance planning and crew scheduling
definition: Given a backlog of planned jobs with durations, crafts, parts and equipment-outage windows, produce a feasible weekly or shutdown schedule.
inputs: backlog with job plans, craft availability, parts status, outage windows, priorities
outputs: scheduled jobs by crew and day, shutdown or turnaround schedule, schedule compliance
benchmark_note: resource-constrained scheduling instances can be scored on feasibility and makespan or weighted lateness
