state_of_art: SAP Plant Maintenance with Multi-Resource Scheduling; IBM Maximo Scheduler; Oracle Primavera P6 for turnarounds; Prometheus Group Planning and Scheduling

name: Maintenance history and failure coding
definition: Given completed work orders and technician narratives, code each event by failure mode, mechanism, cause and action, and compute maintenance indicators.
inputs: work order history, technician free text, downtime records
outputs: coded failure events, mean time between failures and to repair, maintenance key performance indicators
benchmark_note: the MaintNet logbook datasets and ISO 14224-coded work orders allow scored text classification
state_of_art: IBM Maximo; SAP Plant Maintenance; GE Vernova Asset Performance Management

name: Aircraft continuing airworthiness tracking
definition: Given an aircraft's configuration, flight hours and cycles, maintenance program, directives and logbook entries, compute due inspections, life-limited part status and deferral limits.
inputs: aircraft and component configuration, hours and cycles, maintenance program, airworthiness directives, logbook entries
outputs: forecast of due tasks, life-limited part remaining life, directive compliance status, deferred defect limits
benchmark_note: due-limit computations from hours, cycles and calendar rules have exact answers
state_of_art: Swiss AviationSoftware AMOS; IFS Maintenix; TRAX; CAMP Systems; Ramco Aviation

name: Statutory inspection and test compliance
definition: Given installed regulated equipment and the inspection codes that apply, schedule required inspections and tests and record results and deficiencies.
inputs: regulated equipment inventory (fire protection, elevators, boilers, railcars, ships), applicable codes, inspection results
outputs: inspection schedule, deficiency lists, compliance status and certificates
benchmark_note: interval rules are checkable, but code applicability needs expert judgment
state_of_art: Inspect Point; BuildingReports; ABS Nautical Systems

name: Repair shop order management
definition: Given a unit brought in for repair, record complaint, cause and correction, look up labor times and parts, and produce the repair order and its history.
inputs: unit identity (VIN, serial), customer complaint, labor-time guides, parts lookups
outputs: repair order with diagnosis, labor and parts lines, unit service history
benchmark_note: labor-time and parts lookup can be scored against published guides; the rest is record keeping
state_of_art: Mitchell 1 Manager SE; Tekmetric; Shopmonkey; CDK Global service module; RepairShopr; Cleancloud

name: Asset strategy and lifecycle planning
definition: Given asset inventories, failure behavior, consequences, costs and budgets, decide what maintenance to do, what spares to hold and when to renew or replace assets.

name: Asset criticality ranking
definition: Given assets with failure likelihoods and safety, environmental, production and cost consequences, rank them on a risk matrix.
inputs: asset list, consequence categories and scores, likelihood estimates, risk matrix
outputs: criticality scores and ranked asset list
benchmark_note: scoring is mechanical once matrices are fixed, but consequence inputs are judgment
state_of_art: GE Vernova APM Strategy; AVEVA Asset Strategy Optimization; ARMS Reliability OnePM

name: Reliability-centered maintenance analysis
definition: Given system functions, functional failures and failure modes with consequences, select an applicable and effective maintenance task for each mode.
inputs: functions, failure modes and effects, consequence categories, candidate tasks
outputs: maintenance program: task type, interval and justification per failure mode
benchmark_note: decision-logic outcomes for given failure-mode data are checkable, but realistic cases need expert labels
state_of_art: ReliaSoft RCM++; Isograph Availability Workbench RCMCost; ARMS Reliability OnePM

name: Maintenance interval optimization
definition: Given a failure distribution and costs of planned and unplanned replacement or inspection, compute cost- or availability-optimal maintenance intervals.
inputs: life distribution parameters, preventive and corrective costs, downtime, detection probability
outputs: optimal replacement or inspection interval with cost rate curve
benchmark_note: age-replacement and inspection-interval problems have analytic optima
state_of_art: Isograph Availability Workbench; ReliaSoft BlockSim; OREDA-based in-house tools

name: Critical spares optimization
definition: Given demand rates for repairable or consumable spares, lead times, costs and availability targets, choose stock levels and locations.
inputs: part failure rates, repair turnaround, lead times, costs, availability target
outputs: recommended stock levels and expected availability or backorders
benchmark_note: METRIC-type multi-echelon models have computable optima for given inputs
state_of_art: Isograph Availability Workbench spares module; PTC Servigistics; Baxter Planning; Systecon Opus10

name: Life cycle cost analysis
definition: Given acquisition, operating, maintenance and disposal cost elements over an asset's life, compute and compare discounted life cycle costs of alternatives.
inputs: cost breakdown structure, rates, reliability and maintenance assumptions, discount rate, horizon
outputs: life cycle cost per alternative, sensitivity results
benchmark_note: discounted cost calculations for defined cases have exact answers
state_of_art: Isograph Availability Workbench LCC; PTC Windchill Risk and Reliability LCC

name: Infrastructure deterioration and renewal planning
definition: Given condition ratings of networked infrastructure (pavements, bridges, pipes), deterioration models and budgets, forecast condition and choose a renewal program.
inputs: inventory with condition ratings, deterioration curves or Markov transition matrices, treatment costs, budgets
outputs: condition forecasts and a multi-year treatment or replacement program
benchmark_note: forecasts can be backtested on public bridge-inventory histories; program optimality depends on the chosen objective
state_of_art: AASHTOWare Bridge Management; PAVER; Deighton dTIMS; AgileAssets; Copperleaf; Autodesk InfoAsset Planner

name: Vehicle and aircraft diagnostics
definition: Given access to a vehicle's, engine's or aircraft's controllers and test equipment, read faults and live data, test performance and reprogram modules to locate and fix defects.

name: On-board diagnostic scanning
definition: Given a connection to a light vehicle's diagnostic port, read and clear trouble codes, freeze-frame and live parameters, and readiness monitors.
inputs: vehicle network connection, protocol and parameter definitions
outputs: trouble codes with descriptions, live data streams, monitor status
benchmark_note: protocol conformance and code decoding can be tested against recorded vehicle traffic
state_of_art: Snap-on ZEUS; Autel MaxiSys; Bosch ESI[tronic]; Launch X431

name: Heavy-duty, marine and powersport engine diagnostics
definition: Given a connection to a heavy-duty, marine or motorcycle engine controller, read proprietary and standard faults, run actuator and cylinder tests, and adjust parameters.
inputs: controller connection (J1939, proprietary links), OEM parameter definitions
outputs: active and stored faults, test results, parameter changes, trip and duty-cycle reports
benchmark_note: decoding J1939 diagnostic messages is testable; OEM-specific tests are closed
state_of_art: Cummins INSITE; Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link; Noregon JPRO; Caterpillar Electronic Technician; Texa IDC

name: Control module programming and configuration
definition: Given a replacement or outdated vehicle control module and the manufacturer's calibration files, flash software and perform configuration and coding.
inputs: module identity, calibration and software files, pass-through interface
outputs: reprogrammed and configured module, programming log
benchmark_note: UDS service sequences can be tested against simulated electronic control units
state_of_art: Drew Technologies CarDAQ with OEM portals; Bosch Mastertech; Autel MaxiFlash

name: Engine performance and dynamometer testing
definition: Given dynamometer or engine-analyzer sensor readings, compute corrected power, torque, combustion and cylinder balance figures and compare with specification.
inputs: load cell, speed, pressure and temperature traces, ambient conditions, engine specification
outputs: corrected power and torque curves, cylinder and combustion diagnostics, pass or fail
benchmark_note: corrected power from recorded runs has exact answers under the SAE correction standard
state_of_art: Dynojet Power Core; SuperFlow WinDyn; Land & Sea DYNO-MAX; Savvy Aviation engine monitor analysis

name: Wheel alignment and frame measurement
definition: Given wheel-target or body-point measurements, compute alignment angles or body dimensions, compare them with the manufacturer's specification and guide adjustment.
inputs: camera or probe measurements, vehicle specification database
outputs: camber, caster, toe or point-to-point deviations, adjustment guidance
benchmark_note: angle computation from target geometry is testable, but specification databases are proprietary
state_of_art: Hunter WinAlign; John Bean V3D; Car-O-Liner Vision; Chief Meridian

name: Aircraft fault isolation and health monitoring
definition: Given onboard maintenance system messages, flight-deck effects and line-replaceable-unit test results, identify the failed unit and the fault-isolation procedure.
inputs: maintenance messages, fault codes, flight data, built-in test results
outputs: isolated faulty unit, fault isolation manual reference, health trend alerts
benchmark_note: fault-to-unit mapping is scoreable on proprietary fleet data; NASA has public avionics fault datasets for some subsystems
state_of_art: Boeing Airplane Health Management; Airbus Skywise Health Monitoring; Honeywell Forge Flight Efficiency

name: Electrical test and instrument calibration
definition: Given installed electrical apparatus, circuits or instruments and test equipment, run and evaluate tests that show whether they work within specification.

name: Protective relay testing
definition: Given relay settings and a test set, inject currents and voltages, measure operating times and compare with the settings' characteristic curves.
inputs: relay settings file, test plan, injected quantities, measured trip times
outputs: pass or fail per test point, characteristic plots, test report
benchmark_note: expected trip times follow from settings and standard curve equations
state_of_art: OMICRON Test Universe; Doble Protection Suite; Megger RTMS

name: Electrical apparatus test evaluation
definition: Given test results for transformers, breakers, cables and rotating machines (insulation resistance, power factor, winding resistance, timing), compare with limits and history and rate condition.
inputs: test results by apparatus, nameplate data, acceptance limits, prior results
outputs: condition ratings, trend plots, test reports
benchmark_note: limit checks are exact; condition ratings need expert labels
state_of_art: Megger PowerDB; Doble DTA; Doble Test Assistant

name: Power quality and disturbance analysis
definition: Given recorded voltage and current waveforms or event records, classify disturbances (sags, swells, harmonics, transients, faults) and locate their cause.
inputs: waveform captures, fault and disturbance records, system data
outputs: event classification, harmonic and flicker indices, fault type and estimated location
benchmark_note: synthetic and labeled disturbance datasets exist for event classification
state_of_art: Fluke Energy Analyze Plus; Dranetz Dran-View; SEL SYNCHROWAVE Event; Grid Protection Alliance openXDA

name: Motor and winding testing
definition: Given static and dynamic test measurements on motors and generators (surge, resistance, current signature, commutator profile), detect winding, rotor and commutator faults.
inputs: surge waveforms, resistance and inductance readings, current spectra, commutator profile traces
outputs: fault indications per test, condition rating, report
benchmark_note: public motor current signature datasets with seeded broken-bar and bearing faults exist
state_of_art: SKF Baker AWA; PdMA MCEMAX; ALL-TEST Pro

name: Circuit board fault finding
definition: Given a faulty circuit board and a known-good reference, compare in-circuit signatures and functional tests to locate failed components.
inputs: board under test, reference signatures or schematic, probe measurements
outputs: suspect components and nets, test log
benchmark_note: signature comparison can be scored on seeded faults, but no public dataset
state_of_art: Huntron Workstation; ABI Electronics SYSTEM 8

name: Fault isolation and service information
definition: Given an equipment symptom or fault code, retrieve the relevant service information, parts and known fixes, and guide the technician through tests to the cause.

name: Service and repair information retrieval
definition: Given equipment identity and a component or symptom, retrieve applicable repair procedures, specifications, wiring diagrams and service bulletins.
inputs: make, model, serial or VIN, query text or code
outputs: ranked procedures, specifications, diagrams and bulletins
benchmark_note: retrieval and question answering over a fixed manual corpus can be scored with held-out questions
state_of_art: ALLDATA Repair; Mitchell 1 ProDemand; Identifix; Boeing Toolbox; Airbus AirN@v

name: Guided symptom-based troubleshooting
definition: Given observed symptoms and test results, choose the next most informative test and converge on the faulty component.
inputs: symptoms, fault codes, test outcomes, system model or troubleshooting tree
outputs: ordered test sequence, diagnosed fault and confidence
benchmark_note: sequential diagnosis can be scored on simulated systems with known faults (expected tests to isolation)
state_of_art: CaseBank SpotLight; Bosch ESI[tronic] guided diagnostics; Snap-on SureTrack; Siemens Teamcenter diagnostics

name: Known-fix mining from repair histories
definition: Given a symptom or code and a corpus of past repair records, return the fixes that most often resolved it.
inputs: symptom or code, vehicle or equipment identity, repair-record corpus
outputs: ranked confirmed fixes with frequencies
benchmark_note: ranking can be scored on held-out repair records, but large corpora are proprietary
state_of_art: Identifix Direct-Hit; Snap-on SureTrack Real Fixes; Mitchell 1 SureTrack

name: Industrial controller fault interpretation
definition: Given the fault log or live status of an elevator, robot, drive or turbine controller, decode faults and give the likely causes and checks.
inputs: controller fault log, live I/O and status, controller documentation
outputs: decoded faults, probable causes, recommended checks
benchmark_note: code decoding is exact against documentation; cause ranking needs labeled events
state_of_art: FANUC ZDT (Zero Down Time); KONE 24/7 Connected Services; Otis ONE; Vestas remote operations

name: Illustrated parts identification
definition: Given equipment identity and a part description, location or photo, identify the exact part number, supersessions and interchangeable parts.
inputs: equipment identity, illustrated parts catalog, description or image
outputs: part number, supersession chain, alternates
benchmark_note: part-number lookup from descriptions or images can be scored on catalog test sets
state_of_art: Documoto; PartsTrader; ARI PartSmart

name: Condition monitoring and prognostics
definition: Given measurements taken on operating equipment and structures, detect and diagnose developing faults and estimate remaining useful life.

name: Rotating machinery vibration analysis
definition: Given vibration signals from rotating machines and their kinematics, compute spectra and envelopes, rate severity and diagnose faults such as imbalance, misalignment and bearing defects.
inputs: accelerometer or proximity probe signals, shaft speeds, bearing and gear geometry
outputs: spectra and severity levels, fault diagnosis per machine
benchmark_note: Case Western Reserve University and Paderborn bearing datasets have labeled faults
state_of_art: Emerson AMS Machinery Manager; SKF @ptitude Observer; Bently Nevada System 1

name: Lubricant and wear-debris analysis
definition: Given laboratory or online oil measurements (wear metals, viscosity, contamination, particle counts), set alarm limits and diagnose wear and lubricant condition.
inputs: sample results by component, oil type, history
outputs: alarm status, diagnosis and recommended action per sample
benchmark_note: alarm-limit calculations are exact; diagnoses need expert-labeled samples
state_of_art: Bureau Veritas LOAMS; Spectro Scientific SpectroTrack; Polaris Laboratories HORIZON

name: Transformer dissolved gas analysis
definition: Given dissolved gas concentrations in transformer oil over time, classify the fault type and severity.
inputs: gas concentrations (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, carbon oxides), sampling dates
outputs: fault class (partial discharge, thermal, arcing), severity status, trend
benchmark_note: the IEC TC10 fault database and Duval triangle reference cases give labeled examples
state_of_art: Doble TOA4; Hitachi Energy TXpert; Delta-X Research Transformer Oil Analyst

name: In-service nondestructive inspection evaluation
definition: Given ultrasonic, eddy-current or radiographic data from in-service components, size flaws or wall loss and compare with acceptance or fitness-for-service criteria.
inputs: scan data (A-, B-, C-scans, images), component geometry, acceptance criteria
outputs: flaw indications with size and location, thickness maps, accept or reject
benchmark_note: flaw sizing on reference blocks is scoreable; public labeled field data is scarce
state_of_art: Evident (Olympus) OmniPC; Eddyfi Technologies UltraVision; Waygate Technologies InspectionWorks

name: Inspection image defect detection
definition: Given visible or infrared images of equipment and infrastructure, detect and grade defects such as cracks, corrosion, hot spots and pipe deformations.
inputs: inspection photos, drone or crawler video, thermograms, asset context
outputs: defect locations, classes and severity grades
benchmark_note: CODEBRIM (bridge defects), Sewer-ML (sewer pipe defects) and road damage datasets are public
state_of_art: FLIR Thermal Studio; Fluke SmartView; WinCan; Bentley Asset Performance inspection

name: Operator rounds and inspection data
definition: Given streaming sensor values and manually collected operator readings, store, compress, trend and check them against operating limits.
inputs: tag values from control systems and meters, operator round readings
outputs: time-series archive, trends, limit excursions, shift logs
benchmark_note: compression error and query performance are measurable; there is no standard functional benchmark
state_of_art: AVEVA PI System; Honeywell PHD; GE Proficy Historian; Canary Historian

name: Equipment anomaly detection and diagnosis
definition: Given multivariate sensor or acoustic data from equipment, detect departures from normal behavior and classify the likely fault.
inputs: multivariate time series or sound recordings, operating context, normal-behavior history
outputs: anomaly scores and alerts, diagnosed fault class
benchmark_note: MIMII and the DCASE machine-sound anomaly tasks, and the Skoltech SKAB set, are public leaderboards or datasets
state_of_art: AVEVA PI Asset Analytics; GE Vernova SmartSignal; Aspen Mtell; Uptake

name: Remaining useful life prognostics
definition: Given degradation measurements and operating conditions for a unit, estimate its remaining useful life with uncertainty.
inputs: run-to-failure histories, current degradation signals, future load profile
outputs: remaining-life estimate with confidence bounds
benchmark_note: NASA C-MAPSS turbofan and PHM Society data challenges have scored test sets
state_of_art: Aspen Mtell; SparkCognition; GE Vernova APM Predict

name: Reliability and maintainability analysis
definition: Given failure and repair data or component models, estimate life distributions, system reliability, availability and maintainability.

name: Life data analysis
definition: Given failure and suspension times, fit life distributions (Weibull, lognormal, exponential) with confidence bounds and derive reliability metrics.
inputs: times to failure, censored times, grouping
outputs: distribution parameters with confidence bounds, B-lives, reliability and hazard curves
benchmark_note: IEC 61649 and textbook datasets have reference estimates
state_of_art: ReliaSoft Weibull++; Minitab Reliability; JMP Life Distribution

name: Accelerated life test analysis
definition: Given failure data at elevated stresses, fit a life-stress model and extrapolate life at use conditions.
inputs: failure and suspension times per stress level, stress variables, use conditions
outputs: life-stress model parameters, use-level life estimates with bounds
benchmark_note: published example datasets have reference fits
state_of_art: ReliaSoft ALTA; JMP Reliability

name: Parts-count reliability prediction
definition: Given a bill of materials with part types, quality levels and operating stresses, compute failure rates per a prediction handbook.
inputs: parts list, part parameters, stresses, environment, handbook choice
outputs: part and assembly failure rates, mean time between failures
benchmark_note: handbook formulas give exact answers for a defined parts list
state_of_art: ReliaSoft Lambda Predict; PTC Windchill Prediction; Isograph Reliability Workbench Prediction

name: System reliability and availability modeling
definition: Given a system structure as a reliability block diagram with component failure and repair models, compute or simulate system reliability, availability and throughput.
inputs: block diagram, component distributions, maintenance and spares policies
outputs: system reliability, availability, downtime contributors
benchmark_note: analytic block-diagram results and Monte Carlo reference cases can be compared
state_of_art: ReliaSoft BlockSim; Isograph Availability Workbench; Isograph Reliability Workbench

name: Markov reliability modeling
definition: Given system states and transition rates for failure and repair, solve for state probabilities, availability and mean time to failure.
inputs: state space, failure and repair rates, initial state
outputs: transient and steady-state probabilities, availability, mean time to failure
benchmark_note: closed-form and numerical solutions exist for defined chains
state_of_art: Isograph Reliability Workbench Markov; PTC Windchill Markov

name: Reliability growth analysis
definition: Given failure times from a test-fix-test program, fit a growth model and project reliability after corrective actions.
inputs: cumulative failure times, corrective action timing, test duration
outputs: growth model parameters, current and projected failure intensity
benchmark_note: Crow-AMSAA examples in IEC 61164 have reference estimates
state_of_art: ReliaSoft RGA

name: Maintainability prediction
definition: Given a system's maintenance tasks, fault-isolation design and task times, predict mean time to repair and related maintainability figures.
inputs: replaceable units, failure rates, task time elements, fault isolation design
outputs: mean time to repair, maximum corrective time, maintenance hours per operating hour
benchmark_note: handbook procedures give exact answers for defined inputs
state_of_art: Isograph Reliability Workbench Maintainability; PTC Windchill Maintainability

name: Failure, hazard and risk analysis
definition: Given a system, process or event, identify how it can fail or cause harm, quantify the risk where possible, and trace failures to root causes and corrective actions.

name: Failure modes and effects analysis
definition: Given a system structure and functions, enumerate failure modes, their effects and causes, and rank them by severity, occurrence and detection or criticality.
inputs: system or process structure, functions, failure mode libraries, rating scales
outputs: FMEA or FMECA worksheet with risk rankings and actions
benchmark_note: criticality numbers are exact given ratings, but completeness of failure modes needs expert-labeled systems
state_of_art: ReliaSoft XFMEA; APIS IQ-RM; PTC Windchill FMEA; Siemens Polarion FMEA

name: Fault tree analysis
definition: Given a fault tree of basic events and logic gates with probabilities, compute minimal cut sets, top-event probability and importance measures.
inputs: fault tree logic, basic event probabilities or rates, common-cause groups
outputs: minimal cut sets, top-event probability, importance measures
benchmark_note: the Open-PSA model exchange format has benchmark trees with known cut sets
state_of_art: Isograph FaultTree+; RiskSpectrum PSA; ReliaSoft BlockSim FTA

name: Probabilistic risk assessment
definition: Given initiating events, event trees and supporting fault trees, quantify accident sequence frequencies and plant risk, including online configuration risk.
inputs: initiating event frequencies, event trees, fault trees, equipment configuration
outputs: sequence and core-damage or release frequencies, risk importance, configuration risk profile
benchmark_note: Open-PSA reference models give known quantification results
state_of_art: SAPHIRE; RiskSpectrum PSA; CAFTA (EPRI); EPRI Phoenix

name: Process and machinery hazard studies
definition: Given process or machine design information, systematically identify deviations or hazards, their causes and consequences, existing safeguards and needed actions.
inputs: piping and instrument diagrams or machine design, guide words or hazard lists, operating modes
outputs: HAZOP, what-if or machinery risk assessment worksheets with risk rankings and actions
benchmark_note: completeness can be scored against expert HAZOP records for reference plants, but few are public
state_of_art: Sphera PHA-Pro; AcuTech PHA Works; Primatech PHAWorks; designsafe

name: Protection layer and safety integrity analysis
definition: Given hazard scenarios with initiating frequencies and independent protection layers, determine required risk reduction and the safety integrity level of instrumented functions, and verify a design meets it.
inputs: scenarios, initiating event frequencies, protection layers and their failure probabilities, tolerable risk, safety function architecture
outputs: required safety integrity levels, achieved probability of failure on demand, test intervals
benchmark_note: probability of failure on demand formulas in IEC 61508-6 give exact answers for defined architectures
state_of_art: exida exSILentia; Sphera PHA-Pro LOPA; Rockwell SIL Solver

name: Aircraft system safety assessment
definition: Given aircraft or system functions, assess failure conditions and their severity, allocate safety objectives and show the architecture meets them.
inputs: aircraft and system functions, failure conditions, architecture, fault trees
outputs: functional hazard assessment, preliminary and final system safety assessments
benchmark_note: the ARP4761 worked examples give reference outputs, but real assessments are proprietary
state_of_art: Isograph Reliability Workbench; Ansys medini analyze

name: Root cause analysis
definition: Given a failure or incident with its evidence and timeline, build a causal model and identify root causes and corrective actions.
inputs: event description, timeline, evidence, interviews
outputs: causal chart or tree, root causes, corrective actions
benchmark_note: cause extraction from published investigation reports (for example Chemical Safety Board) can be scored against their stated causes
state_of_art: TapRooT; Sologic Causelink; Reliability Center PROACT; ThinkReliability Cause Mapping

name: Failure reporting and corrective action
definition: Given failure reports from test or field use, classify, trend and track each failure through analysis to verified corrective action.
inputs: failure reports, part and configuration data, analysis results
outputs: failure classifications, Pareto and trend reports, corrective action status
benchmark_note: failure-report classification is scoreable; workflow tracking is not
state_of_art: ReliaSoft XFRACAS; PTC Windchill FRACAS; Relyence FRACAS

name: Occupational health and safety management
definition: Given workplace hazards, exposures, chemicals and incidents, record, assess and control risks to workers and produce the required safety records.

name: Injury and illness recordkeeping
definition: Given incident reports, decide recordability and classification under the regulation, code the case, and produce the required logs and summaries.
inputs: incident narratives, treatment and lost-time details, hours worked
outputs: recordability decision, coded cases, injury logs and annual summaries, incidence rates
benchmark_note: OSHA severe injury reports and BLS OIICS-coded narratives allow scored case classification
state_of_art: Cority; Intelex; VelocityEHS; Enablon

name: Incident and corrective action management
definition: Given reported incidents, near misses and observations, route investigations, assign corrective actions and track them to closure with trend reporting.
inputs: incident and near-miss reports, investigation findings, organizational structure
outputs: investigation records, corrective actions with status, leading and lagging indicators
benchmark_note: mostly workflow and record keeping with no defined correct output
state_of_art: Cority; Intelex; Enablon; Sphera; VelocityEHS

name: Chemical hazard classification and safety data sheets
definition: Given chemical products and mixture compositions, classify hazards, maintain safety data sheets and site chemical inventories, and generate labels.
inputs: product compositions, ingredient hazard data, site inventory
outputs: hazard classifications, 16-section safety data sheets, labels, inventory reports
benchmark_note: GHS mixture classification rules give exact classifications for defined compositions
state_of_art: VelocityEHS Chemical Management; Sphera SDS Authoring; 3E Protect; UL WERCS

name: Hazardous energy control procedures
definition: Given a machine's energy sources and isolation points, produce equipment-specific lockout and tagout procedures and track their application.
inputs: equipment energy sources, isolation devices and locations, photos
outputs: machine-specific lockout procedures, tags, permit and audit records
benchmark_note: completeness of isolation points can be checked against reference equipment, but no public set exists
state_of_art: Brady LINK360; Master Lock Safety Series procedure software; ProSafe eLOTO

name: Workplace exposure monitoring
definition: Given gas detector, noise dosimeter and air-sampling data, compute time-weighted exposures, compare with occupational limits, and manage detector fleets.
inputs: detector and dosimeter logs, sampling results, worker and task assignments, exposure limits
outputs: time-weighted averages and doses, exceedances, detector bump-test and calibration status
benchmark_note: time-weighted average and noise-dose formulas give exact answers
state_of_art: Industrial Scientific iNet Now; Honeywell Safety Suite; Blackline Safety Blackline Live; 3M Detection Management Software

name: Ergonomic job risk assessment
definition: Given a job's postures, loads, frequencies and durations, compute biomechanical and lifting risk indices and the share of workers capable of the task.
inputs: posture angles, hand loads, lift geometry and frequency, worker anthropometry
outputs: lifting index, compressive spinal forces, population strength capability, energy expenditure
benchmark_note: lifting-equation and static-strength calculations have reference examples; video pose-based scoring can be compared with expert ratings
state_of_art: University of Michigan 3DSSPP; Siemens Jack; TuMeke; VelocityEHS Industrial Ergonomics

name: Safety inspections and audits
definition: Given checklists and site observations, record findings, score compliance and assign corrective actions.
inputs: inspection checklists, observations and photos, locations
outputs: inspection reports, scores, findings with actions
benchmark_note: hazard detection in site photos can be scored on labeled images; checklist scoring is record keeping
state_of_art: SafetyCulture iAuditor; Intelex; Cority

name: Environmental compliance management
definition: Given a facility's emission sources, monitoring data, wastes and permits, calculate releases, track permit obligations and produce regulatory environmental reports.

name: Air emissions inventory calculation
definition: Given source activity data, fuels, throughputs and storage tank parameters, calculate emissions using emission factors and engineering methods.
inputs: source inventory, activity data, emission factors, tank and material properties
outputs: emissions by pollutant and source, permit-limit comparisons, inventory reports
benchmark_note: AP-42 and tank-loss equations give exact answers for defined inputs
state_of_art: Sphera Environmental; Enablon Air; Trinity Consultants TRAQER; Cority Air; EPA MOVES; CERC EMIT

name: Continuous emissions data reporting
definition: Given analyzer and flow readings from continuous emissions monitors, validate, substitute missing data, compute emission rates and produce regulatory reports.
inputs: minute and hourly analyzer data, calibration and quality-assurance test results, unit operating data
outputs: validated hourly emissions, substitute data, quarterly electronic reports
benchmark_note: EPA's ECMPS check engine defines correct calculations and substitutions
state_of_art: Emerson (Ovation) CEMS DAHS; ESC Spectrum StackVision; Teledyne CEMS

name: Fugitive leak detection and repair
definition: Given a component inventory and monitoring readings, schedule monitoring, flag leaks above thresholds, track repair deadlines and compute fugitive emissions.
inputs: component inventory with tags, monitoring readings, regulatory leak definitions
outputs: monitoring schedules, leak lists and repair deadlines, compliance reports
benchmark_note: schedule and deadline rules are exact; optical gas image detection can be scored on labeled video
state_of_art: Guideware LeakDAS; Sphera LDAR; Envirosuite

name: Greenhouse gas inventory accounting
definition: Given activity data for fuels, electricity, processes and refrigerants, compute greenhouse gas emissions by scope and gas using published factors.
inputs: activity data, emission factors, organizational boundary, global warming potentials
outputs: emissions by scope, source and gas, regulatory and voluntary reports
benchmark_note: GHG Protocol calculation tools give exact results for defined activity data
state_of_art: Persefoni; Watershed; Sphera Corporate Sustainability; Microsoft Sustainability Manager

name: Hazardous waste tracking and manifesting
definition: Given waste streams generated on site, characterize and code them, track accumulation limits and shipments, and produce manifests and reports.
inputs: waste stream profiles, container and accumulation records, transporter and facility data
outputs: waste codes, accumulation alerts, shipping manifests, biennial reports
benchmark_note: waste code assignment from profiles is scoreable; tracking is record keeping
state_of_art: Sphera Waste; Enablon Waste; VelocityEHS Waste

name: Water discharge permit compliance
definition: Given effluent sampling results and permit limits, compute averages and loads, flag exceedances and produce discharge monitoring reports.
inputs: sample results, flows, permit limits and averaging periods
outputs: computed concentrations and loads, exceedances, discharge monitoring reports
benchmark_note: averaging and load calculations under permit rules have exact answers
state_of_art: Hach WIMS; Aquatic Informatics Rio; EPA NetDMR

name: Permit obligation tracking
definition: Given environmental permits and regulations, extract each obligation and turn it into scheduled tasks, records and certifications.
inputs: permit documents, applicable regulations, facility equipment
outputs: obligation register, task calendar, compliance certifications
benchmark_note: obligation extraction from permit text can be scored against hand-built registers
state_of_art: Enablon Compliance; Intelex Environmental; Cority Environmental

name: Building automation and control
definition: Given a building's sensors, controllers and equipment, supervise and schedule heating, cooling, ventilation, lighting and access, detect faults, and verify control sequences.

name: Supervisory control and scheduling
definition: Given building controllers and occupancy schedules, read and command points, set schedules and setpoints, and trend values.
inputs: controller network and point lists, schedules, setpoints
outputs: commanded equipment states, schedules, trend logs, graphics
benchmark_note: protocol conformance has BACnet Testing Laboratories test plans; supervisory logic has no standard score
state_of_art: Niagara Framework; Johnson Controls Metasys; Siemens Desigo CC; Schneider EcoStruxure Building Operation; Honeywell WEBs
open_tools: VOLTTRON; BACnet Stack; BAC0; Home Assistant

name: Point tagging and semantic modeling
definition: Given raw controller point names and metadata, assign standard semantic classes and relationships so applications can find equipment and points.
inputs: point names, descriptions, units, controller structure
outputs: Brick or Haystack model of equipment, points and locations
benchmark_note: point-name-to-class mapping can be scored on labeled building point lists such as the Mortar testbed
state_of_art: SkyFoundry SkySpark; Mapped; Normal Software; J2 Innovations FIN

name: HVAC fault detection and diagnostics
definition: Given trended points from air handlers, terminal units and plants, apply rules or models to detect and diagnose faults and estimate their energy cost.
inputs: trend data, equipment semantics, fault rules or models
outputs: fault detections with diagnosis, priority and cost impact
benchmark_note: LBNL fault detection and diagnosis datasets and ASHRAE research project data have labeled faults
state_of_art: SkyFoundry SkySpark; Clockworks Analytics; CopperTree Kaizen; Cimetrics Analytika

name: Building alarm and event management
definition: Given point values and alarm definitions, raise, route, acknowledge and log alarms and events to the right people.
inputs: alarm limits and conditions, notification classes and recipients
outputs: alarm notifications, acknowledgment records, event history
benchmark_note: correctness depends on site-specific configuration
state_of_art: Niagara Framework alarm service; Johnson Controls Metasys; Siemens Desigo CC

name: Electronic access control and intrusion monitoring
definition: Given credentials, door hardware, schedules and alarm zones, grant or deny entry, monitor door and intrusion states, and log events.
inputs: credential holders, access rules and schedules, door and sensor states, camera feeds
outputs: access decisions, door and intrusion alarms, audit trails, associated video
benchmark_note: policy evaluation is simple and site-specific; there is no scored task
state_of_art: Genetec Security Center; Software House C-CURE 9000; Lenel OnGuard; Milestone XProtect

name: Control sequence verification and commissioning
definition: Given a specified control sequence and trend or test data from the installed system, verify the sequence behaves as specified and record functional test results.
inputs: sequence of operations, point mapping, trend or forced-test data
outputs: pass or fail per requirement, issues log, commissioning report
benchmark_note: Guideline 36 reference implementations allow automated verification against trended or simulated data
state_of_art: Facility Grid; CxAlloy; SkyFoundry SkySpark
open_tools: Modelica Buildings Library control description language (CDL) tools

name: Facility energy management
definition: Given meter readings, utility bills and facility data, track, benchmark and forecast energy use, verify savings and identify efficiency measures.

name: Utility bill tracking and allocation
definition: Given utility bills and submeter readings, validate charges, normalize for weather and allocate costs to buildings, tenants or departments.
inputs: utility bills, tariffs, submeter data, weather, floor areas
outputs: validated bills, cost allocations, normalized consumption reports
benchmark_note: bill error detection and tariff calculation are scoreable on constructed cases
state_of_art: EnergyCAP; Urjanet (Arcadia); Schneider EcoStruxure Resource Advisor

name: Building energy benchmarking
definition: Given a building's annual energy use and characteristics, compute normalized intensity and a peer score or rating.
inputs: annual energy by fuel, floor area, use type, operating characteristics, location
outputs: energy use intensity, 1-100 score or rating, peer comparison
benchmark_note: published ENERGY STAR regression models give exact scores for defined inputs
state_of_art: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager; Measurabl; Deepki

name: Energy baseline and savings verification
definition: Given pre- and post-retrofit interval or monthly meter data with weather, fit a baseline model, forecast counterfactual use and compute avoided energy with uncertainty.
inputs: metered energy, weather, operating schedule, retrofit dates
outputs: baseline model with fit statistics, avoided energy and its uncertainty
benchmark_note: CalTRACK test sets, ASHRAE Great Energy Predictor III and Building Data Genome 2 allow scored forecasts
state_of_art: OpenEEmeter (CalTRACK); Gridium; Schneider EcoStruxure Resource Advisor

name: Energy audit and measure screening
definition: Given site survey data and consumption, estimate end-use breakdowns and the savings and cost-effectiveness of candidate efficiency measures.
inputs: equipment inventory, operating hours, utility data, measure library, costs
outputs: end-use breakdown, measure list with savings, costs and payback, audit report
benchmark_note: savings estimates can be compared with measured post-retrofit results where available
state_of_art: DOE Audit Template; EnergyCAP; Snugg Pro; TREAT

name: Demand response and peak load management
definition: Given utility signals, tariffs and controllable loads, decide load reductions or shifts to cut peak demand or meet program commitments, and verify the response.
inputs: event or price signals, interval load data, controllable loads and constraints
outputs: load shed or shift schedule, dispatched commands, verified load reduction
benchmark_note: CityLearn challenge environments score demand-response control policies
state_of_art: Enel X demand response; CPower; Voltus

name: Facility and space management
definition: Given buildings, floor plans and an organization's needs, inventory and allocate space, schedule rooms and services, and assess facility condition.

name: Space inventory and area measurement
definition: Given floor plans or building models, delineate and classify rooms and compute floor areas under a measurement standard.
inputs: floor plans or BIM, space classification scheme, measurement standard
outputs: room inventory with classes and areas, area reports
benchmark_note: room segmentation and area from floor plan images can be scored on public floor plan datasets
state_of_art: Archibus; IBM TRIRIGA; Planon; FM:Systems

name: Space allocation and stacking
definition: Given space inventory, headcounts, adjacency needs and utilization data, assign groups to floors and rooms.
inputs: space inventory, group sizes and growth, adjacency matrix, utilization sensors
outputs: stack and block plan, utilization reports
benchmark_note: allocation instances can be scored on capacity and adjacency objectives
state_of_art: Archibus; Planon; Serraview; OfficeSpace

name: Room and resource reservation
definition: Given rooms, their features and booking requests, assign rooms to events without conflicts.
inputs: rooms with capacity and features, booking requests and rules
outputs: conflict-free room assignments, calendars, utilization
benchmark_note: room assignment is a constrained assignment problem with checkable feasibility
state_of_art: CollegeNET 25Live; EMS Software; Robin; Condeco

name: Custodial workload planning
definition: Given cleanable areas, space types and target cleanliness levels, compute staffing needs and assign cleaning routes.
inputs: areas by space type, cleaning frequencies and productivity rates, service levels
outputs: staffing requirement, route assignments, inspection scores
benchmark_note: staffing calculations from published productivity rates are exact
state_of_art: ISSA Cleaning Times workloading; Team Software; Swept

name: Facility condition assessment
definition: Given building systems surveyed with condition and age, estimate deferred maintenance and renewal needs and compute a facility condition index.
inputs: building system inventory, condition ratings, useful lives, replacement costs
outputs: deficiency list with costs, renewal forecast, facility condition index
benchmark_note: index calculations are exact once deficiencies and costs are set; surveys are judgment
state_of_art: Gordian VFA; AssetWorks AiM Capital Planning; Brightly Asset Essentials

name: Electric grid operations
definition: Given real-time measurements and a network model of an electric transmission or distribution system, monitor its state, dispatch generation, switch the network and restore outages.

name: State estimation and contingency monitoring
definition: Given redundant telemetry and a network topology model, estimate the system state, detect bad data and screen contingencies for limit violations.
inputs: telemetered flows, injections and voltages, breaker statuses, network model
outputs: estimated voltages and flows, bad-data flags, contingency violations
benchmark_note: IEEE test systems with synthetic noisy measurements give known true states
state_of_art: GE Vernova GridOS EMS; Siemens Spectrum Power; Hitachi Energy Network Manager; OSI monarch

name: Generation dispatch and frequency control
definition: Given load, interchange schedules, unit limits and costs, compute real-time economic dispatch and automatic generation control signals.
inputs: area control error, unit limits and ramp rates, cost curves, interchange schedules
outputs: unit base points and regulation signals, control performance metrics
benchmark_note: dispatch on PGLib or IEEE cases has verifiable optima; the L2RPN challenges score real-time operation
state_of_art: GE Vernova GridOS EMS; Siemens Spectrum Power; OSI monarch

name: Wide-area synchrophasor monitoring
definition: Given time-synchronized phasor measurements across the grid, detect oscillations, islanding and disturbances and estimate their source.
inputs: phasor measurement unit streams, network model
outputs: oscillation modes and damping, event detections and locations, alarms
benchmark_note: the IEEE-NASPI oscillation source location contest provides scored cases
state_of_art: GE Vernova PhasorPoint; Hitachi Energy PSGuard; Electric Power Group RTDMS

name: Distribution switching and fault restoration
definition: Given a distribution network model, telemetry and a fault, locate the fault, isolate it and compute a switching sequence that restores service within limits.
inputs: feeder model, switch states, fault indicator and relay data, loads
outputs: fault location, isolation and restoration switching plan, restored customers
benchmark_note: IEEE distribution test feeders with seeded faults give scoreable restoration plans
state_of_art: Schneider EcoStruxure ADMS; GE Vernova GridOS ADMS; Oracle Network Management System; Siemens Spectrum Power ADMS

name: Outage management
definition: Given customer calls, meter events and device operations, infer which protective device operated, group customers into outages, dispatch crews and compute reliability indices.
inputs: trouble calls, meter last-gasp events, network connectivity, device operations, crew status
outputs: predicted outage devices, outage records with restoration times, reliability indices
benchmark_note: outage-device prediction can be scored on simulated call patterns; reliability indices are exact
state_of_art: Oracle Network Management System; GE Vernova GridOS ADMS; Schneider EcoStruxure ADMS; Milsoft DisSPatch

name: Substation automation and monitoring
definition: Given intelligent electronic devices in a substation, configure and supervise their communication, control interlocks and equipment monitoring.
inputs: substation configuration description, device data models, measurements and statuses
outputs: station control and interlocking, alarms, equipment condition data
benchmark_note: configuration-file validation is exact; operational behavior has no shared benchmark
state_of_art: Hitachi Energy MicroSCADA X; SEL RTAC; Siemens SICAM; GE Vernova MCP

name: Meter data validation and estimation
definition: Given raw interval reads from utility meters, validate them, estimate missing or bad values and edit them into billing-quality data.
inputs: interval reads, meter events, validation rules, history and weather
outputs: validated and estimated interval data with quality flags
benchmark_note: imputation of masked intervals can be scored on public smart-meter datasets
state_of_art: Itron Enterprise Edition MDM; Oracle Utilities Meter Data Management; Siemens EnergyIP

name: Pipeline and water network operations
definition: Given telemetry and models of gas, liquid or water pipe networks, detect leaks, measure and balance flows, schedule pumping and assess pipe integrity.

name: Leak detection and localization
definition: Given flow, pressure and acoustic measurements from a pressurized network, detect leaks and estimate their location and size.
inputs: flow and pressure time series, network model, acoustic logger data
outputs: leak alarms, estimated location and leak rate
benchmark_note: the BattLeDIM 2020 competition and LeakDB give scored leak detection and localization
state_of_art: Atmos Pipe; Emerson (ROXAR) PipelineManager; Xylem (Pure Technologies); TaKaDu

name: Gas flow measurement and accounting
definition: Given meter readings, pressures, temperatures and gas composition, compute corrected volumes and energy, validate meters and balance receipts against deliveries.
inputs: differential pressure or meter pulses, pressure, temperature, gas analysis
outputs: corrected volumes and energy, lost-and-unaccounted-for gas, measurement exceptions
benchmark_note: AGA reports include verification cases with exact expected results
state_of_art: Quorum PGAS; Flowcal; Emerson FloBoss software

name: Water network pump scheduling
definition: Given demand forecasts, tank levels, tariffs and a network model, schedule pumps and valves to meet pressure and storage limits at least cost.
inputs: demand forecast, network hydraulic model, pump curves, tariffs, tank limits
outputs: pump and valve schedules, predicted levels and pressures, energy cost
benchmark_note: published benchmark networks (for example the Anytown and Richmond networks) with pump-scheduling objectives allow comparison
state_of_art: Xylem (Innovyze) Info360; Bentley OpenFlows WaterSight; Schneider AVEVA Water

name: Pipeline integrity assessment
definition: Given in-line inspection anomalies and pipe properties, compute remaining strength and safe operating pressure and prioritize digs and repairs.
inputs: anomaly lists (depth, length, orientation), pipe grade and geometry, operating pressure
outputs: failure pressure and safe pressure per anomaly, repair priorities, reassessment intervals
benchmark_note: B31G and modified B31G formulas give exact failure pressures for defined anomalies
state_of_art: ROSEN Integrity Data Management; Dynamic Risk IRAS; Baker Hughes Pipeline Integrity

name: Telecom and broadcast plant operations
definition: Given installed cable, radio and transmitter plant, keep records of it, test it and monitor it so circuits and broadcasts stay in service.

name: Outside plant records
definition: Given cables, conduits, splices, poles and their connectivity, maintain a spatial and logical record that traces any circuit end to end.
inputs: as-built drawings, splice and pair or fiber assignments, field updates
outputs: connected plant record, circuit traces, capacity reports
benchmark_note: circuit tracing over a defined plant record is exact; capturing records is not
state_of_art: Mapcom M4; IQGeo Network Manager; Bentley Fiber; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network for telecom

name: Copper and fiber cable test analysis
definition: Given optical time-domain reflectometer traces or copper test results, locate events and faults and certify links against standards.
inputs: reflectometer traces, loss and length measurements, copper pair tests, standards limits
outputs: event tables with distance and loss, fault location, pass or fail certification
benchmark_note: event detection on synthetic reflectometer traces is scoreable; few labeled field traces are public
state_of_art: EXFO FastReporter; VIAVI FiberTrace; Fluke Networks LinkWare

name: Antenna and feed line sweep testing
definition: Given swept return-loss or reflection measurements of antenna systems, compute distance-to-fault and pass or fail against limits.
inputs: frequency-domain reflection data, cable type and velocity factor, limits
outputs: return loss and voltage standing wave ratio, distance-to-fault plot, pass or fail
benchmark_note: distance-to-fault from reflection data is a defined transform with exact answers on synthetic lines
state_of_art: Anritsu Line Sweep Tools; VIAVI CellAdvisor

name: Cell site and tower management
definition: Given towers, shelters and the equipment and leases on them, track site configuration, structural loading records, access and maintenance.
inputs: site inventory, mounted equipment, tenant and lease data, inspection records
outputs: site configuration records, inspection and maintenance status, capacity on structures
benchmark_note: record keeping without a defined correct output
state_of_art: Sitetracker; Tillman Infrastructure systems; AmeriTower

name: Transmitter remote monitoring and control
definition: Given metering and status from unattended broadcast or radio transmitter sites, log readings, raise alarms and execute remote control actions.
inputs: power, reflected power and status telemetry, alarm limits, control commands
outputs: logged readings, alarms, executed control actions
benchmark_note: site-specific supervision without a defined scored task
state_of_art: Burk ARC Plus; Davicom Comlab; Sine Systems

name: Map, survey and model earth, land and living resources
definition: Measuring and modeling the natural world and land use: mapping and GIS, surveying and positioning, remote sensing, the subsurface, natural water and atmosphere, and the management of farms, forests and fisheries.

name: Geographic information systems
definition: Given vector and raster geodata with attributes, store, query, transform and combine them to produce derived layers and answers to spatial questions.

name: Geodata storage and translation
definition: Given geodata in mixed formats and coordinate systems, validate, reproject and load it into a managed spatial store or another format without losing geometry or attributes.
inputs: vector and raster files or services, coordinate reference systems, schema mappings
outputs: spatial database tables or files in the target format and projection; validation reports
benchmark_note: round-trip fidelity and OGC conformance tests are scoreable; schema mapping is case-specific
state_of_art: ArcGIS Pro; FME; Oracle Spatial

name: Vector overlay and geoprocessing
definition: Given point, line and polygon layers, compute buffers, clips, intersections, unions, dissolves and spatial joins.
inputs: vector layers with attributes, tolerances, operation parameters
outputs: derived vector layers with combined attributes
benchmark_note: results are exact geometry, and robustness suites such as the JTS/GEOS test cases exist
state_of_art: ArcGIS Pro; FME

name: Raster and terrain analysis
definition: Given elevation and other raster layers, compute map-algebra results and terrain derivatives such as slope, aspect, viewshed, cost distance, flow direction and catchments.
inputs: digital elevation models and raster layers, analysis parameters
outputs: derived rasters, viewsheds, least-cost paths, drainage networks and basins
benchmark_note: derivatives on synthetic surfaces have analytic answers and drainage extraction can be scored against mapped streams
state_of_art: ArcGIS Spatial Analyst; Global Mapper
open_tools: GRASS GIS; WhiteboxTools; SAGA GIS; TauDEM

name: Spatial interpolation and geostatistics
definition: Given measurements at scattered locations, model spatial dependence and predict values and uncertainty on a grid, or test for clustering and hot spots.
inputs: point samples with values, optional covariates and boundaries
outputs: variograms, interpolated grids, prediction variance, conditional simulations, cluster statistics
benchmark_note: held-out cross-validation error, as in the Spatial Interpolation Comparison exercises
state_of_art: ArcGIS Geostatistical Analyst; Surfer; Isatis
open_tools: gstat; GSLIB; SGeMS; PyKrige; GeoDa; PySAL

name: Land suitability and site selection
definition: Given criteria layers, weights and constraints, rank locations or allocate land uses and compare planning scenarios.
inputs: criteria rasters or polygons, weights, constraints, demand targets
outputs: suitability surfaces, selected sites or corridors, scenario indicators
benchmark_note: reserve-selection objectives are scoreable on shared problem sets; criteria weights are a value judgment
state_of_art: ArcGIS Pro suitability modeler; CommunityViz; Marxan with Zones

name: Mobile field data capture
definition: Given a data schema and a GNSS-enabled device, record attributed features and observations in the field and synchronize them with a spatial database.
inputs: form schemas, basemaps, device positions
outputs: georeferenced feature records and photos synchronized to a geodatabase
benchmark_note: a workflow tool whose quality is usability and sync reliability
state_of_art: ArcGIS Field Maps; ArcGIS Survey123; Trimble TerraFlex

name: Geocoding and address matching
definition: Given postal addresses or place names, return coordinates with match quality, and the reverse.
inputs: address strings, reference street and address-point data
outputs: coordinates, match scores, standardized addresses
benchmark_note: match rate and positional error against authoritative address points
state_of_art: ArcGIS World Geocoding Service; Precisely Spectrum Geocoding

name: Web map and feature services
definition: Given spatial layers, publish them as standard map, tile, feature and processing services that remote clients can query.
inputs: spatial layers, styles, service configuration
outputs: map images, tiles, feature responses and processing results over standard protocols
benchmark_note: OGC conformance suites test correctness; performance depends on deployment
state_of_art: ArcGIS Enterprise

name: Cartography and map production
definition: Given geodata and a purpose and scale, design and render maps, charts and 3D views that communicate it correctly.

name: Thematic map design
definition: Given attribute data joined to geography, classify and symbolize it as choropleth, proportional-symbol, dot or flow maps with legends and layout.
inputs: attribute data, boundaries, classification and symbol choices
outputs: symbolized map layouts and legends
benchmark_note: rule checks (class breaks, color legibility) are scoreable; overall design quality needs human judgment
state_of_art: ArcGIS Pro; Mapbox Studio

name: Automated label placement
definition: Given features, label text and placement rules, place labels without overlap and in preferred positions.
inputs: features, label strings, fonts, priorities and rules
outputs: label positions and a list of unplaced labels
benchmark_note: labels placed, conflicts and rule violations are countable on shared datasets
state_of_art: ArcGIS Maplex label engine

name: Map projection design
definition: Given a region and a map purpose, choose and parameterize a projection and report its area, shape and distance distortion.
inputs: geographic extent, purpose, candidate projections
outputs: projection definition, distortion statistics, reprojected graticules
benchmark_note: distortion measures are computable exactly
state_of_art: Geocart; Projection Wizard

name: Map generalization
definition: Given detailed geodata and a target scale, simplify, aggregate, displace and select features so the map stays legible.
inputs: large-scale vector data, target scale, constraints
outputs: generalized vector data
benchmark_note: constraint violations are measurable; agreement with human-generalized maps is subjective
state_of_art: ArcGIS Pro cartography toolset; 1Spatial 1Generalise

name: Topographic and thematic base mapping
definition: Given surveys, imagery and elevation data, compile standard map sheets with contours, hillshade, geology or soil units and standard symbology.
inputs: survey data, orthoimagery, elevation models, thematic field maps, product specification
outputs: map sheets and base-map databases
benchmark_note: completeness and positional accuracy against specification are checkable; symbol design is not
state_of_art: ArcGIS Production Mapping; Global Mapper

name: 3D terrain and globe visualization
definition: Given elevation models, imagery and features, render interactive 3D scenes, virtual globes and fly-throughs.
inputs: elevation models, imagery, vector features, camera paths
outputs: interactive 3D scenes, rendered views and animations
benchmark_note: visual quality and interactivity have no reference answer
state_of_art: Google Earth Pro; ArcGIS Pro scenes; Cesium ion

name: Nautical chart compilation
definition: Given validated bathymetry and maritime features, compile electronic and paper navigational charts to the hydrographic product specification.
inputs: bathymetric surfaces, soundings, aids to navigation, coastline, product specification
outputs: electronic navigational chart cells and paper charts, validation reports
benchmark_note: product validation checks (S-58) are scoreable; generalization of soundings needs review
state_of_art: Teledyne CARIS HPD; ESRI ArcGIS Maritime

name: Land and hydrographic surveying
definition: Given field measurements of angles, distances, satellite signals or sonar returns, compute positions, boundaries and surfaces of land and seafloor with stated accuracy.

name: Survey field data collection
definition: Given an instrument connection and a job file, record coded total-station and GNSS observations and stake out design points.
inputs: instrument observations, control points, point codes, stakeout coordinates
outputs: raw observation files, coded points, stakeout reports
benchmark_note: an instrument-control and logging workflow
state_of_art: Trimble Access; Leica Captivate; Carlson SurvPC

name: GNSS post-processing
definition: Given raw satellite-positioning observations and reference data, compute corrected positions by baseline, differential, kinematic or precise-point processing.
inputs: raw GNSS observations, base-station or network data, orbits and clocks
outputs: baseline vectors, corrected coordinates and their precision
benchmark_note: position error against known stations such as IGS and CORS sites
state_of_art: Trimble Business Center; Leica Infinity; NovAtel Inertial Explorer

name: Least-squares network adjustment
definition: Given redundant angle, distance, height and GNSS-vector observations and control, compute adjusted coordinates, error ellipses and blunder tests.
inputs: observations with standard errors, control coordinates
outputs: adjusted coordinates, residuals, error ellipses, statistical test results
benchmark_note: published test networks have reference adjusted solutions
state_of_art: STAR*NET; Trimble Business Center; Columbus

name: Coordinate geometry and boundaries
definition: Given bearings, distances, curves and legal descriptions, compute coordinates, misclosure, areas and parcel plats.
inputs: traverse or deed calls, curve data, control points
outputs: parcel coordinates, closure reports, areas, plat drawings
benchmark_note: closure and area from a set of calls are exactly computable
state_of_art: Carlson Survey; Civil 3D survey tools

name: Geodetic datum transformation
definition: Given coordinates in one horizontal or vertical reference frame and projection, convert them to another and report transformation uncertainty.
inputs: coordinates, source and target reference frames, epochs, geoid and grid models
outputs: transformed coordinates and heights with uncertainty
benchmark_note: agency test points give reference results
state_of_art: NGS NCAT; Blue Marble Geographic Calculator

name: Survey drafting and existing surface
definition: Given coded survey points, build linework, a triangulated existing-ground surface, contours and the survey drawing.
inputs: coded points, breaklines, drafting standards
outputs: survey linework, surface model, contours, survey plans
benchmark_note: the surface and contours from given points are deterministic; linework from codes follows local conventions
state_of_art: Autodesk Civil 3D; Carlson Survey; Trimble Business Center

name: Hydrographic survey and bathymetry processing
definition: Given planned lines and vessel sensor records (positioning, motion, sound velocity, echo sounder or multibeam), produce cleaned soundings and depth surfaces that meet a survey order.
inputs: survey lines, raw sonar, positioning, motion and sound-velocity records, tides
outputs: cleaned soundings, bathymetric grids, uncertainty surfaces, survey reports
benchmark_note: reference surfaces and IHO total vertical uncertainty limits make results scoreable
state_of_art: Teledyne CARIS HIPS and SIPS; QPS Qimera; HYPACK

name: Side-scan mosaicking and seabed classification
definition: Given side-scan or backscatter records, build georeferenced mosaics, pick targets and classify seabed type.
inputs: side-scan or multibeam backscatter, navigation, ground-truth samples
outputs: mosaics, target lists, seabed class maps
benchmark_note: labeled seabed and target datasets exist but are few
state_of_art: Chesapeake SonarWiz; QPS FMGT; Teledyne CARIS SIPS

name: Remote sensing image analysis
definition: Given satellite or airborne imagery from optical, thermal or radar sensors, extract calibrated physical quantities, classes, objects and changes.

name: Radiometric and atmospheric correction
definition: Given raw image digital numbers and sensor metadata, compute top-of-atmosphere and surface reflectance or brightness temperature, with cloud and shadow masks.
inputs: raw imagery, calibration coefficients, atmospheric data, acquisition geometry
outputs: surface reflectance or temperature images, quality masks
benchmark_note: atmospheric correction intercomparisons score against ground-measured reflectance
state_of_art: ENVI FLAASH; ERDAS IMAGINE ATCOR; Sen2Cor; LaSRC

name: Land cover classification
definition: Given multispectral imagery and training samples, assign each pixel a land-cover class and assess accuracy.
inputs: image stacks, training and validation samples, class legend
outputs: class maps, confusion matrices, area estimates
benchmark_note: labeled datasets such as EuroSAT and BigEarthNet
state_of_art: Google Earth Engine; ENVI; ERDAS IMAGINE

name: Object-based feature extraction
definition: Given high-resolution imagery, segment it and extract objects such as buildings, roads, tree crowns or water bodies.
inputs: high-resolution imagery, optional elevation and training labels, rule sets
outputs: object polygons or lines with class and attributes
benchmark_note: SpaceNet building and road challenges
state_of_art: Trimble eCognition; ArcGIS Pro deep learning tools

name: Change detection and image time series
definition: Given co-registered images over time, map where and when the surface changed and characterize trends and seasonal cycles.
inputs: multi-date image stacks, masks, change legend
outputs: change maps, disturbance dates, trend and phenology metrics
benchmark_note: labeled change datasets such as OSCD and xView2
state_of_art: Google Earth Engine (LandTrendr, CCDC); TerrSet Land Change Modeler

name: Hyperspectral and spectral analysis
definition: Given spectral image cubes and spectral libraries, identify materials and estimate their abundance per pixel.
inputs: hyperspectral or multispectral cubes, spectral libraries
outputs: material and abundance maps, anomaly and target detections
benchmark_note: standard scenes (Indian Pines, Pavia) have ground truth but are small
state_of_art: ENVI

name: Radar imaging and interferometry
definition: Given synthetic-aperture radar acquisitions, produce calibrated backscatter, coherence, interferograms and surface-deformation time series.
inputs: SAR single-look complex or detected images, orbits, elevation model
outputs: backscatter images, interferograms, displacement maps and time series
benchmark_note: deformation estimates can be scored against GNSS stations
state_of_art: GAMMA; SARscape; SNAP

name: Image interpretation and mensuration
definition: Given georeferenced imagery, let an analyst view, measure, annotate and report on features and activity.
inputs: imagery with sensor models, reference data
outputs: measurements, annotated products, reports
benchmark_note: mensuration accuracy is scoreable; interpretation is analyst judgment
state_of_art: SOCET GXP; RemoteView

name: Photogrammetry, lidar and aerial mapping
definition: Given overlapping images or laser scans from aircraft, drones or ground vehicles, reconstruct accurate 3D geometry: orientations, point clouds, elevation models and orthoimages.

name: Aerial mapping mission planning
definition: Given an area, a sensor and an accuracy target, compute flight lines, altitude, overlap and waypoints that achieve the required coverage and ground sample distance.
inputs: area of interest, camera or lidar specification, terrain, accuracy and overlap requirements
outputs: flight plan, waypoints, predicted coverage and resolution
benchmark_note: coverage and resolution are computable; feasibility depends on airspace and aircraft
state_of_art: DJI Pilot 2; UgCS; Leica MissionPro

name: Aerial triangulation and bundle adjustment
definition: Given overlapping images, approximate positions and ground control, solve camera orientations and tie-point coordinates by least-squares bundle adjustment.
inputs: images, camera calibration, GNSS/IMU data, ground control points
outputs: exterior and interior orientations, tie points, accuracy report
benchmark_note: ISPRS and EuroSDR benchmark blocks have independent checkpoints
state_of_art: Trimble Inpho MATCH-AT; Hexagon HxMap; Pix4Dmatic

name: Structure from motion and dense matching
definition: Given unordered overlapping photographs, recover camera poses and a dense 3D point cloud or mesh.
inputs: photographs, optional positions and control
outputs: camera poses, sparse and dense point clouds, textured meshes
benchmark_note: ETH3D and Tanks and Temples score reconstructions against laser-scanned ground truth
state_of_art: Pix4Dmapper; Agisoft Metashape; Bentley iTwin Capture (ContextCapture); RealityCapture

name: Orthorectification and mosaicking
definition: Given oriented images and an elevation model, remove relief and tilt displacement and blend the images into a seamless orthomosaic.
inputs: images, orientations or sensor models, elevation model
outputs: orthoimages, seamlines, mosaics, accuracy report
benchmark_note: checkpoint error under the ASPRS positional accuracy standard
state_of_art: PCI Geomatica OrthoEngine; Trimble Inpho OrthoVista; Pix4Dmapper

name: Stereo feature compilation
definition: Given oriented stereo pairs, digitize 3D features such as breaklines, buildings, roads and hydrography.
inputs: oriented stereo models, feature specification
outputs: 3D vector features
benchmark_note: positional accuracy is scoreable against checkpoints; completeness depends on the specification
state_of_art: DAT/EM Summit Evolution; SOCET GXP; Hexagon ImageStation

name: Lidar point cloud classification
definition: Given georeferenced lidar or image-derived points, label them as ground, vegetation, buildings, water and other standard classes.
inputs: point clouds with intensity and returns, trajectories, class scheme
outputs: classified point clouds, strip-alignment and accuracy reports
benchmark_note: ISPRS filter test, DALES and Semantic3D have labeled points
state_of_art: Terrasolid TerraScan; LP360; Global Mapper Lidar Module

name: Elevation model generation
definition: Given classified points or stereo matches, interpolate bare-earth and surface elevation models with breaklines and contours.
inputs: classified point clouds or stereo matches, breaklines
outputs: digital terrain and surface models, contours, vertical accuracy report
benchmark_note: vertical error against surveyed checkpoints
state_of_art: Terrasolid TerraModeler; Global Mapper; LP360

name: Mobile mapping and SLAM
definition: Given lidar, camera and inertial streams from a moving platform, estimate its trajectory and build a consistent georeferenced map.
inputs: lidar scans, images, IMU and GNSS streams
outputs: trajectory, registered point cloud or map
benchmark_note: KITTI odometry and Hilti SLAM challenge score trajectory error
state_of_art: GeoSLAM Connect; Leica Cyclone; NavVis IVION

name: Subsurface imaging and geological modeling
definition: Given seismic, potential-field, electrical and well measurements, image the subsurface and build interpreted 3D geological models.

name: Seismic data processing and imaging
definition: Given field seismic records and acquisition geometry, apply corrections, velocity analysis, stacking and migration to produce subsurface images.
inputs: shot records, geometry, velocity models
outputs: stacked and migrated volumes, velocity models
benchmark_note: synthetic models such as Marmousi and the SEG/EAGE salt model have known truth
state_of_art: SLB Omega; Halliburton SeisSpace ProMAX; CGG Geovation; Shearwater Reveal

name: Seismic interpretation
definition: Given migrated seismic volumes and well ties, pick horizons and faults, compute attributes and convert time to depth.
inputs: seismic volumes, well logs and tops, velocity data
outputs: horizon and fault surfaces, attribute volumes, time and depth maps
benchmark_note: labeled fault and facies volumes such as the F3 Netherlands facies benchmark
state_of_art: SLB Petrel; S&P Global Kingdom; Halliburton DecisionSpace

name: Seismic inversion and rock physics
definition: Given seismic data and well logs, estimate elastic properties, run amplitude-versus-offset analysis and relate them to lithology and fluids.
inputs: pre- or post-stack seismic, wavelets, well logs, rock physics models
outputs: impedance and elastic property volumes, synthetic seismograms, lithology and fluid probability
benchmark_note: synthetic earth models with known properties allow exact scoring
state_of_art: GeoSoftware HampsonRussell; Ikon Science RokDoc; Jason

name: Potential-field and near-surface geophysics
definition: Given gravity, magnetic, electrical, electromagnetic or refraction measurements, produce anomaly maps and forward or inverted earth models.
inputs: survey readings, station positions, terrain, starting models
outputs: corrected anomaly grids, 2D and 3D property models, depth-to-source estimates
benchmark_note: synthetic models with known structure
state_of_art: Seequent Oasis montaj; Seequent VOXI; Res2DInv

name: Well log analysis and petrophysics
definition: Given wireline or drilling logs and core data, compute porosity, water saturation, lithology and net pay.
inputs: log curves, core measurements, formation tops, parameters
outputs: petrophysical curves, zone summaries, net-pay reports
benchmark_note: FORCE 2020 lithology and SPWLA prediction contests
state_of_art: SLB Techlog; Halliburton DecisionSpace Petrophysics; Interactive Petrophysics

name: Borehole logs and stratigraphic correlation
definition: Given borehole descriptions, samples and logs, draft log plots and correlate units into cross sections and fence diagrams.
inputs: lithology descriptions, sample and test results, downhole logs, locations
outputs: borehole log plots, correlated cross sections, fence diagrams
benchmark_note: drafting and interpretive correlation without a reference answer
state_of_art: Bentley OpenGround; Golden Software Strater; RockWorks

name: Structural and 3D geological modeling
definition: Given horizons, faults, well tops and outcrop data, build a consistent 3D structural framework, restore sections and populate property grids.
inputs: interpreted surfaces, fault sticks, well tops, orientation data, property data
outputs: 3D structural models, restored sections, gridded property models
benchmark_note: synthetic models test reproduction of known structure; interpretation is non-unique
state_of_art: SLB Petrel; Emerson SKUA-GOCAD; Seequent Leapfrog Geo; Petroleum Experts Move

name: Basin and petroleum system modeling
definition: Given stratigraphy, lithology and heat-flow history, simulate burial, temperature, maturity and hydrocarbon generation and migration.
inputs: layer ages and thicknesses, lithologies, heat flow, source-rock kinetics
outputs: burial and thermal histories, maturity maps, charge and migration estimates
benchmark_note: calibration to measured temperature and vitrinite reflectance in wells
state_of_art: SLB PetroMod; Zetaware Trinity; BasinMod

name: Reservoir and well performance engineering
definition: Given a reservoir description, fluid properties and well data, predict flow, pressure and recoverable volumes over time.

name: Reservoir flow simulation
definition: Given a gridded reservoir model, fluid and rock properties and well controls, simulate multiphase flow and forecast production and pressure.
inputs: property grids, relative permeability and capillary data, fluid model, well schedules
outputs: pressure and saturation fields, well rates, forecasts
benchmark_note: SPE Comparative Solution Projects provide shared problems and reference results
state_of_art: SLB ECLIPSE and INTERSECT; CMG IMEX/GEM/STARS; Stone Ridge Echelon

name: Reservoir fluid characterization
definition: Given laboratory pressure-volume-temperature data, tune an equation-of-state or black-oil model of the reservoir fluid.
inputs: fluid composition, lab experiments (constant composition expansion, differential liberation, separator tests)
outputs: tuned equation-of-state model, black-oil tables
benchmark_note: error against measured lab properties on public fluid datasets
state_of_art: SLB PVTi; Calsep PVTsim; Petroleum Experts PVTP

name: Well inflow and lift performance
definition: Given reservoir, completion and tubing data, compute inflow and vertical-lift curves, operating rates and artificial-lift designs.
inputs: reservoir pressure and productivity, completion and tubing geometry, fluid model
outputs: inflow and outflow curves, operating point, lift design
benchmark_note: correlations can be scored against measured well tests
state_of_art: SLB PIPESIM; Petroleum Experts PROSPER

name: Pressure transient analysis
