definition: Given flow-rate and pressure records from a well test, estimate permeability, skin, boundaries and reservoir pressure.
inputs: rate and pressure history, well and fluid properties
outputs: diagnostic plots, model match, reservoir parameters
benchmark_note: synthetic tests with known parameters
state_of_art: KAPPA Saphir; Weatherford PanSystem

name: Decline analysis and reserves evaluation
definition: Given production history and economics, forecast rates, estimate ultimate recovery and classify reserves.
inputs: monthly production, prices, costs, ownership
outputs: rate forecasts, estimated ultimate recovery, reserves and cash-flow reports
benchmark_note: hindcasts on public state production data are scoreable
state_of_art: Halliburton ARIES; PHDWin; Enverus PRISM

name: Mineral resource and mine planning
definition: Given drillhole data, a geological model and economic parameters, estimate the mineral resource and design and schedule its extraction.

name: Drillhole data management and compositing
definition: Given collars, downhole surveys, assays and geology logs, validate them into a drillhole database and produce composites.
inputs: collar, survey, assay and lithology tables
outputs: validated drillhole database, 3D traces, composites
benchmark_note: data management without a reference answer
state_of_art: Seequent MX Deposit; Datamine Fusion; acQuire

name: Block modeling and resource estimation
definition: Given composites and geological domains, estimate grades into a block model and classify the resource by confidence.
inputs: composites, domain wireframes, variograms, estimation parameters
outputs: block model with grades and classification, grade-tonnage curves
benchmark_note: synthetic and exhaustive datasets (Walker Lake) allow scoring estimates against truth
state_of_art: Datamine Studio RM; Maptek Vulcan; Seequent Leapfrog Edge; Deswik

name: Open-pit limit optimization
definition: Given block economic values and slope constraints, find the ultimate pit and nested shells that maximize value.
inputs: block model with values, slope angles, prices and costs
outputs: ultimate pit, nested shells, pushback candidates
benchmark_note: MineLib instances have known optima
state_of_art: Dassault GEOVIA Whittle; Deswik.GO; MiningMath

name: Mine layout design
definition: Given an optimal shell or stope envelope, design practical benches, ramps, stopes and development openings.
inputs: pit shells or stope shapes, design parameters, topography
outputs: pit and underground designs, reserve volumes
benchmark_note: designs can be checked against constraints and shell volume; practicality needs review
state_of_art: Deswik.CAD; Maptek Vulcan; GEOVIA Surpac

name: Mine production scheduling
definition: Given a reserve model, precedences and capacities, schedule extraction by period to maximize net present value.
inputs: mining blocks or solids, precedences, equipment and plant capacities, economics
outputs: period schedules, stockpile plans, NPV
benchmark_note: MineLib scheduling instances have best known solutions
state_of_art: Deswik.Sched; Minemax Scheduler; Epiroc XPAC

name: Surface water hydrology and hydraulics
definition: Given precipitation, terrain, land cover, soils and channel geometry, predict runoff, river flows, water levels, floods, erosion and water quality in natural waters.

name: Rainfall-runoff and watershed modeling
definition: Given precipitation, basin geometry, land cover and soils, compute infiltration, runoff hydrographs and continuous streamflow.
inputs: rainfall or meteorological series, subbasin parameters, loss and routing methods
outputs: runoff hydrographs, peak flows, water balances
benchmark_note: CAMELS catchments give observed streamflow for scoring
state_of_art: HEC-HMS; DHI MIKE SHE; PCSWMM

name: Open-channel and river hydraulics
definition: Given channel and floodplain geometry, roughness, structures and flows, compute water-surface profiles, velocities and shear in one or two dimensions.
inputs: cross sections or terrain mesh, roughness, bridges and culverts, boundary flows
outputs: water-surface elevations, velocities, depths, hydraulic tables
benchmark_note: the UK Environment Agency 2D hydraulic benchmark tests
state_of_art: HEC-RAS; TUFLOW; DHI MIKE 21

name: Flood inundation and hazard mapping
definition: Given design or observed flows and terrain, map flood extent, depth and hazard zones.
inputs: flow frequencies or hydraulic results, terrain models, structures
outputs: inundation extents, depth grids, flood-zone maps
benchmark_note: observed flood extents from imagery give a reference
state_of_art: HEC-RAS Mapper; TUFLOW; JBA Flood Modeller; Fathom Global

name: Hydrologic data and frequency analysis
definition: Given gauge and logger records, quality-control the series, build rating curves and estimate flow and rainfall frequency.
inputs: stage, discharge and rainfall records, field measurements
outputs: cleaned series, rating curves, frequency curves and design values
benchmark_note: published frequency estimates for test sites
state_of_art: Aquatic Informatics AQUARIUS; USGS PeakFQ; HEC-SSP

name: Surface water quality and loading
definition: Given pollutant sources, flows and kinetics, simulate nutrient, sediment and contaminant concentrations in streams and lakes and allocate loads.
inputs: point and nonpoint loads, flows, reaction rates, temperatures
outputs: concentration series, load budgets, load allocations
benchmark_note: monitored concentrations exist but calibration data are sparse
state_of_art: EPA WASP; DHI MIKE ECO Lab; HSPF

name: Soil erosion and sediment yield
definition: Given rainfall, soils, slopes, cover and practices, estimate soil loss, sediment delivery and pond trapping.
inputs: rainfall erosivity, soil erodibility, slope, cover and practice factors or process parameters
outputs: soil loss rates, sediment yields, basin trap efficiency
benchmark_note: plot-scale erosion datasets exist
state_of_art: RUSLE2; WEPP

name: Coastal and estuarine hydrodynamics
definition: Given bathymetry, tides, winds and river inflows, simulate water levels, currents, waves, storm surge and salinity.
inputs: bathymetric mesh, tidal and meteorological forcing, river inflows
outputs: water levels, currents, wave fields, surge and salinity
benchmark_note: hindcasts scored against tide gauges and wave buoys
state_of_art: DHI MIKE 21; Delft3D FM; ADCIRC

name: Groundwater and vadose zone modeling
definition: Given aquifer and soil geometry, properties, boundaries and stresses, predict groundwater flow, unsaturated moisture, and solute and contaminant transport and chemistry.

name: Groundwater flow modeling
definition: Given aquifer layers, hydraulic properties, boundaries and pumping or recharge, compute heads, drawdowns and water budgets.
inputs: layer geometry, conductivity and storage, boundary conditions, stresses
outputs: head fields, drawdowns, budgets, capture zones
benchmark_note: analytic solutions and the MODFLOW test problems
state_of_art: MODFLOW 6 via GMS or Groundwater Vistas; DHI FEFLOW; Visual MODFLOW Flex

name: Solute transport and particle tracking
definition: Given a flow field, sources and reaction parameters, compute plume concentrations, travel paths and times.
inputs: velocity field, porosity, dispersivity, source terms, decay and sorption
outputs: concentration fields over time, pathlines, travel times
benchmark_note: analytic solutions and published field tracer tests
state_of_art: MT3D-USGS; FEFLOW; MODPATH 7

name: Aquifer and slug test analysis
definition: Given drawdown or recovery records from pumping or slug tests, estimate transmissivity, storativity and leakage.
inputs: time-drawdown data, well geometry, pumping rates
outputs: aquifer parameters, curve matches
benchmark_note: synthetic and textbook tests with known parameters
state_of_art: AQTESOLV; AquiferTest Pro

name: Unsaturated zone flow and leaching
definition: Given soil hydraulic properties, climate and surface loads, simulate infiltration, soil moisture, recharge and leaching through the unsaturated zone.
inputs: soil water-retention and conductivity functions, weather, crop or surface conditions, solute loads
outputs: moisture profiles, fluxes, recharge, leachate concentrations
benchmark_note: analytic infiltration solutions and lysimeter data
state_of_art: HYDRUS; SVFlux; FEFLOW

name: Aqueous geochemical modeling
definition: Given water analyses and mineral data, compute speciation, saturation indices and reaction paths and classify water types.
inputs: major and trace ion analyses, temperature, mineral assemblages, thermodynamic database
outputs: species distributions, saturation indices, reaction-path results, water-type diagrams
benchmark_note: reference speciation problems with published answers
state_of_art: Geochemist's Workbench; PHREEQC; AquaChem

name: Free-product and multiphase flow
definition: Given spilled hydrocarbon or other non-aqueous liquid data, estimate its volume, spread and recovery by pumping or vapor extraction.
inputs: well product thickness, soil properties, fluid properties, recovery system design
outputs: free-product volume, plume extent, recovery rates
benchmark_note: laboratory column and tank experiments provide references
state_of_art: API LNAPL Distribution and Recovery Model; TOUGH3

name: Weather, climate and air quality
definition: Given atmospheric observations, model fields and emissions, analyze and forecast weather, project climate and predict pollutant concentrations and wind resources.

name: Weather data analysis and display
definition: Given surface, upper-air, satellite and model data, decode, analyze and display weather maps, soundings and diagnostics.
inputs: observation feeds, gridded model output, satellite imagery
outputs: analyzed charts, soundings and stability indices, diagnostic fields
benchmark_note: display and diagnosis tools without a reference answer
state_of_art: AWIPS; IBM Weather Operations Center (WSI); Unidata IDV

name: Weather radar analysis
definition: Given radar volume scans, produce quality-controlled reflectivity and velocity products, precipitation estimates and storm identification.
inputs: radar volume scans, calibration, gauge data
outputs: mosaics, rainfall estimates, hydrometeor classes, storm cells
benchmark_note: radar rainfall estimates scored against gauges
state_of_art: Baron Lynx; GR2Analyst; MRMS

name: Numerical weather prediction
definition: Given initial and boundary conditions, forecast the atmospheric state at global or mesoscale resolution.
inputs: analyses and observations, boundary conditions, terrain and land surface
outputs: forecast fields of wind, temperature, humidity and precipitation
benchmark_note: WeatherBench 2 scores forecasts against reanalysis
state_of_art: ECMWF IFS; NOAA GFS and HRRR; GraphCast

name: Tropical cyclone and severe storm tracking
definition: Given forecasts and observations, track hurricanes and severe storms and estimate their paths, intensity and local threat.
inputs: advisories, model tracks, radar and observations, site locations
outputs: tracks, wind swaths, arrival times, site threat assessments
benchmark_note: track and intensity error against best-track records
state_of_art: HURRTRAK; Baron Threat Net

name: Climate modeling and downscaling
definition: Given forcing scenarios, simulate the coupled climate system and downscale results to regional scale.
inputs: greenhouse gas and aerosol scenarios, boundary data, model configuration
outputs: long-term climate fields, regional projections
benchmark_note: model evaluation against observations (PCMDI metrics) but no single correct projection
state_of_art: CESM; E3SM; EC-Earth

name: Air pollutant dispersion modeling
definition: Given emission sources, meteorology and terrain, compute downwind concentrations and deposition of pollutants or accidental releases.
inputs: source parameters, meteorological data, terrain and receptors
outputs: concentration and deposition fields, design values, plume footprints
benchmark_note: field tracer studies used in EPA model evaluation
state_of_art: AERMOD; CALPUFF; CERC ADMS; HYSPLIT

name: Wind and solar resource assessment
definition: Given measured wind or irradiance data and terrain, estimate the long-term resource across a site and expected energy yield.
inputs: met mast, lidar or irradiance measurements, reference data, terrain and roughness
outputs: wind or solar resource maps, long-term corrected statistics, energy yield estimates
benchmark_note: flow benchmarks such as Askervein and Bolund hills and operating-farm yields
state_of_art: WAsP; windPRO; Meteodyn WT; Solargis

name: Environmental sampling and site assessment
definition: Given a potentially contaminated site, plan sampling, manage monitoring results, and assess risk and remedies.

name: Environmental sampling design
definition: Given decision objectives, site layout and prior data, compute how many samples to take and where, with the probability of detecting a hot spot.
inputs: data quality objectives, site boundaries, prior concentrations, error tolerances
outputs: sample counts and locations, detection probabilities
benchmark_note: detection probabilities and sample sizes are analytically checkable
state_of_art: Visual Sample Plan; SADA

name: Environmental monitoring data management
definition: Given field measurements and laboratory results, validate them into a site database and report exceedances against standards.
inputs: electronic lab deliverables, field logs, logger feeds, regulatory limits
outputs: validated database, exceedance tables, maps and charts
benchmark_note: data management without a reference answer
state_of_art: EarthSoft EQuIS; Locus EIM; Esdat

name: Monitoring statistics and trends
definition: Given monitoring results over time and space, compute background levels, upper confidence limits, trends and plume stability.
inputs: concentration series by well or station, nondetects, background data
outputs: statistical limits, trend tests, plume stability metrics
benchmark_note: statistical outputs are reproducible against reference datasets
state_of_art: EPA ProUCL; Sanitas; MAROS

name: Human health and ecological risk assessment
definition: Given concentrations, exposure pathways and toxicity values, compute risks and hazard indices and derive cleanup levels.
inputs: media concentrations, receptor and exposure assumptions, toxicity data
outputs: risk and hazard estimates, risk-based cleanup levels, site rankings
benchmark_note: deterministic calculations are checkable against agency calculators; assumptions are site-specific
state_of_art: EPA Regional Screening Levels calculator; RISC

name: Remediation design and optimization
definition: Given plume data and remedial options, compare alternatives, estimate mass flux and optimize remediation and monitoring networks.
inputs: plume extents, mass estimates, remedy options and costs, monitoring network
outputs: ranked alternatives, mass-flux estimates, optimized well networks
benchmark_note: network optimization objectives are scoreable; remedy selection is judgment
state_of_art: MAROS; SiteWise

name: Crop, soil and livestock management
definition: Given fields, soils, weather, crops and animals, record operations, analyze spatial field data, prescribe inputs, simulate crop growth and formulate livestock feeding and breeding.

name: Field operations records
definition: Given fields, crops and applied inputs, record planting, spraying, fertilizing and harvest operations and produce field histories and compliance reports.
inputs: field boundaries, crop plans, operation logs, product labels
outputs: field histories, input-use and compliance reports
benchmark_note: record keeping without a reference answer
state_of_art: John Deere Operations Center; Climate FieldView; Trimble Ag Software

name: Yield mapping and variable-rate prescriptions
definition: Given yield-monitor, soil-sample and imagery data for a field, clean and map it, delineate management zones and write variable-rate application maps.
inputs: yield monitor logs, soil test points, imagery, agronomic rules
outputs: cleaned yield maps, management zones, prescription files for machine controllers
benchmark_note: yield cleaning can be scored on data with planted errors; prescription value needs field trials
state_of_art: Ag Leader SMS; Climate FieldView; John Deere Operations Center

name: Crop growth and irrigation simulation
definition: Given weather, soils, cultivar and management, simulate crop development, yield, water and nitrogen balance and irrigation needs.
inputs: daily weather, soil profile, cultivar parameters, management schedule
outputs: growth stages, biomass and yield, soil water and nitrogen, irrigation schedules
benchmark_note: AgMIP intercomparisons score simulated against observed yields
state_of_art: DSSAT; APSIM; AquaCrop

name: Soil survey and soil interpretation
definition: Given pedon descriptions, lab data and soil maps, describe soils, map their properties and derive suitability and limitation ratings.
inputs: pedon descriptions, laboratory analyses, map units, interpretation criteria
outputs: soil property maps, map-unit descriptions, interpretation ratings
benchmark_note: digital soil mapping scored against held-out profiles
state_of_art: NRCS Web Soil Survey; SoilGrids

name: Livestock herd records
definition: Given animal identities and events (breeding, birth, health, milk, weights), maintain herd records and report performance and action lists.
inputs: animal IDs, pedigrees, event records, milk and weight tests
outputs: herd registers, performance reports, action lists
benchmark_note: record keeping without a reference answer
state_of_art: VAS DairyComp; DeLaval DelPro; CattleMax

name: Feed ration formulation
definition: Given animal requirements, available feeds with composition and price, formulate a least-cost ration that meets nutrient constraints.
inputs: animal class and production level, feed analyses, prices, constraints
outputs: ration composition, predicted nutrient supply and performance, cost
benchmark_note: nutrient-requirement models give reference outputs and least-cost solutions are checkable
state_of_art: AMTS.Cattle; NDS Professional; Format Solutions

name: Genetic evaluation and mating
definition: Given pedigrees, performance records and genotypes, estimate breeding values and plan matings.
inputs: pedigrees, phenotypes, genotypes, model specification
outputs: estimated breeding values, accuracies, mating recommendations
benchmark_note: Interbull test runs and simulated populations with known true breeding values
state_of_art: BLUPF90 family; ASReml; MiXBLUP

name: Forests, rangelands, wildlife and fire
definition: Given measurements of vegetation, fuels, weather and animal populations, inventory and project forests and rangelands, plan harvests, predict wildland fire, and estimate wildlife and fish populations.

name: Forest inventory and timber cruising
definition: Given plot and tree measurements and a sampling design, compute stand tables, volumes, values and sampling error.
inputs: tree species, diameters, heights, plot design, volume equations
outputs: stand and stock tables, volume and value estimates, sampling statistics
benchmark_note: volumes and estimates are reproducible from published equations and FIA reference estimates
state_of_art: Two Dog; SuperACE; FIA EVALIDator

name: Forest growth and yield projection
definition: Given tree lists or stand data, site and treatments, project stand development and landscape change over time.
inputs: tree lists, site index, management prescriptions, disturbance regimes
outputs: projected stand attributes, yields, landscape states
benchmark_note: remeasured permanent plots give observed growth
state_of_art: Forest Vegetation Simulator; LANDIS-II; 3-PG

name: Harvest scheduling and forest planning
definition: Given stands, growth projections and constraints, schedule treatments and harvests over a planning horizon to meet value and sustainability goals.
inputs: stand inventory and yields, adjacency and flow constraints, prices and costs
outputs: harvest schedules, spatial patterns, projected flows and values
benchmark_note: optimization objectives are scoreable on shared forest planning instances, though few are public
state_of_art: Remsoft Woodstock; Spatial Woodstock

name: Wildland fire behavior prediction
definition: Given fuels, weather and terrain, predict fire spread rate, intensity, perimeter growth and burn probability.
inputs: fuel models, fuel moisture, wind and weather, terrain, ignitions
outputs: spread rates, flame lengths, perimeters over time, burn probability maps
benchmark_note: observed fire perimeters provide ground truth
state_of_art: FlamMap; WFDSS FSPro; Prometheus; Technosylva Wildfire Analyst

name: Fuels and fire effects
definition: Given stand and fuel measurements, characterize fuelbeds and estimate fuel consumption, emissions and fire effects, and track monitoring plots.
inputs: fuel inventory, vegetation plots, burn conditions
outputs: fuelbed characteristics, consumption and emissions, effects summaries
benchmark_note: consumption can be scored against measured burns
state_of_art: FCCS; Consume; FOFEM

name: Rangeland and vegetation monitoring
definition: Given transect, plot and photo data, compute vegetation cover and composition, ecological site condition and grazing capacity.
inputs: line-point intercept, gap and plot data, photos, ecological site descriptions
outputs: cover and composition indicators, condition assessments, stocking rates
benchmark_note: cover estimates can be scored against plot data
state_of_art: DIMA / LandscapeDataCommons; Rangeland Analysis Platform

name: Wildlife population and habitat analysis
definition: Given counts, captures, telemetry and habitat layers, estimate abundance, survival, home ranges and habitat suitability.
inputs: survey counts, capture histories, telemetry fixes, habitat covariates
outputs: abundance and survival estimates, home ranges, habitat suitability maps
benchmark_note: simulated populations with known abundance
state_of_art: Program MARK; Distance; Maxent

name: Fish stock assessment and catch records
definition: Given catch logbooks, survey indices and biology, record catch and stocking and estimate stock size and sustainable harvest.
inputs: catch and effort logs, survey indices, age and length data, stocking records
outputs: catch records, biomass and fishing-mortality estimates, reference points
benchmark_note: simulation-tested assessments with known true stocks
state_of_art: Stock Synthesis; NOAA Fisheries Integrated Toolbox

name: Compute, analyze and discover
definition: General methods of quantitative work and laboratory science: numerical and symbolic computing, statistics, machine learning, optimization, visualization, and the informatics of laboratories, molecules and genomes.

name: Numerical computing
definition: Given a mathematical problem stated as matrices, functions or differential equations, compute a floating-point approximate solution with error control.

name: Dense matrix computations
definition: Given a dense matrix (and right-hand sides), compute a factorization, solution, eigen-decomposition or singular value decomposition.
inputs: dense real or complex matrix; right-hand side vectors
outputs: solution vectors, LU/QR/Cholesky factors, eigenvalues and vectors, singular values, condition estimates
benchmark_note: HPL/LINPACK for speed; residual and backward-error checks against known matrices for accuracy
state_of_art: Intel oneMKL; NAG Library; MATLAB

name: Sparse linear systems
definition: Given a large sparse matrix and right-hand side, compute the solution by direct factorization or preconditioned iteration.
inputs: sparse matrix in compressed format; right-hand side; tolerance
outputs: solution vector; residual history; factor or preconditioner
benchmark_note: SuiteSparse Matrix Collection and HPCG give standard problems with checkable residuals
state_of_art: Intel oneMKL PARDISO; MUMPS; NVIDIA cuSPARSE

name: Ordinary differential equation integration
definition: Given a system of ordinary or differential-algebraic equations with initial or boundary conditions, compute the trajectory to a stated tolerance.
inputs: right-hand-side function, initial or boundary values, time span, tolerances
outputs: solution trajectory; error estimates; event times
benchmark_note: published stiff and non-stiff test sets (e.g. the Bari IVP test set) have reference solutions
state_of_art: MATLAB ode suite; Mathematica NDSolve; NAG Library

name: General partial differential equation solution
definition: Given a user-stated partial differential equation, domain and boundary conditions, discretize and solve it without a physics-specific front end.
inputs: equation in weak or strong form, domain or mesh, boundary and initial conditions
outputs: field solution on a grid or mesh; error estimates
benchmark_note: method-of-manufactured-solutions problems give exact errors
state_of_art: MATLAB PDE Toolbox; Mathematica finite element methods; COMSOL equation-based modeling

name: Numerical integration and differentiation
definition: Given a function or tabulated data and a region, compute definite integrals or derivatives to a requested accuracy.
inputs: integrand function or samples, limits or region, tolerance
outputs: integral or derivative value with error estimate
benchmark_note: integrals with closed forms (Genz test families) give exact errors
state_of_art: Mathematica NIntegrate; NAG Library

name: Nonlinear equation solving
definition: Given a system of nonlinear algebraic equations and a starting point or bounds, find roots or certify that none exist.
inputs: residual function, Jacobian (optional), initial guess or interval box
outputs: roots; convergence status; enclosure intervals for verified methods
benchmark_note: standard nonlinear test problems (Moré-Garbow-Hillstrom) have known roots
state_of_art: MATLAB fsolve; Mathcad solve blocks; TK Solver

name: Interpolation and function approximation
definition: Given sampled data or an expensive function, construct an interpolant, spline or approximant and evaluate it.
inputs: data points or function handle, approximation family, tolerance
outputs: interpolant coefficients; evaluated values; error bounds
benchmark_note: approximation error on known functions is exactly measurable
state_of_art: MATLAB Curve Fitting Toolbox; NAG Library

name: Special functions and extended precision
definition: Given arguments and a requested precision, evaluate special functions or carry out arithmetic beyond hardware floating point.
inputs: arguments, function or operation, precision
outputs: values with guaranteed or estimated error
benchmark_note: correctly rounded reference values exist for most functions
state_of_art: Mathematica; Maple

name: Symbolic and exact mathematics
definition: Given mathematical expressions, structures or conjectures, compute exact symbolic results or machine-checked proofs.

name: Symbolic algebra and calculus
definition: Given symbolic expressions, simplify, factor, differentiate, integrate, solve or expand them in closed form.
inputs: symbolic expressions, equations, assumptions
outputs: closed-form results, simplified expressions, symbolic solutions
benchmark_note: integration and simplification test suites (e.g. the Rubi integration tests) have known answers
state_of_art: Mathematica; Maple; Magma

name: Computational algebra and number theory
definition: Given algebraic structures (groups, rings, polynomial ideals, number fields), compute invariants, decompositions or arithmetic facts exactly.
inputs: group presentations, polynomial systems, number fields, integers
outputs: Gröbner bases, class groups, factorizations, character tables
benchmark_note: exact answers are checkable; databases such as LMFDB give reference values
state_of_art: Magma; Mathematica

name: Automated and interactive theorem proving
definition: Given a formal statement and axioms, search for or check a machine-verifiable proof.
inputs: formal statements, theories, proof scripts
outputs: proofs or counterexamples; verification status
benchmark_note: TPTP and miniF2F are standard problem sets with pass/fail scoring
state_of_art: Lean; Isabelle; Vampire
open_tools: Lean; Isabelle; Rocq (Coq); E prover; Vampire; Z3

name: Interactive geometry and graphing
definition: Given geometric constructions or functions, render them and update dependent objects as inputs are dragged or changed.
inputs: constructions, function definitions, parameters
outputs: interactive figures, graphs, loci, measurements
benchmark_note: an exploratory tool; quality is usability, not a computed answer
state_of_art: GeoGebra; Desmos; Cabri
open_tools: GeoGebra (open-source core); KSEG; Geomview; Kig; Dr. Geo

name: Statistical modeling and inference
definition: Given data and a statistical question, fit models, estimate quantities and test hypotheses with stated uncertainty.

name: Hypothesis tests and descriptive statistics
definition: Given samples, compute summaries and run parametric, nonparametric or exact tests and analysis of variance.
inputs: data table, grouping variables, test choice
outputs: summary statistics, test statistics, p-values, confidence intervals, ANOVA tables
benchmark_note: NIST Statistical Reference Datasets give certified results
state_of_art: SAS/STAT; Stata; JMP; SPSS

name: Regression and generalized linear models
definition: Given a response and predictors, fit linear, nonlinear or generalized linear models and report estimates and diagnostics.
inputs: data table, model formula, link and error family
outputs: coefficients, standard errors, fitted values, diagnostics
benchmark_note: NIST StRD linear and nonlinear regression datasets have certified values
state_of_art: SAS/STAT; Stata; R

name: Mixed and multilevel models
definition: Given clustered, repeated or pedigree-structured data, fit models with random effects and estimate variance components.
inputs: data with grouping structure, fixed and random effect terms, covariance structures
outputs: fixed effects, variance components, predicted random effects (BLUPs)
benchmark_note: simulation studies with known variance components; no single standard suite
state_of_art: SAS PROC MIXED; ASReml; HLM

name: Structural equation and latent variable models
definition: Given observed indicators and a hypothesized structure, estimate latent factors, paths and fit indices.
inputs: covariance matrix or raw data, path or measurement model
outputs: loadings, path coefficients, fit indices, factor scores
benchmark_note: parameter recovery on simulated data; published reference models
state_of_art: Mplus; LISREL; Amos

name: Bayesian inference
definition: Given a probabilistic model and data, compute or sample the posterior distribution of the parameters.
inputs: model specification, priors, data
outputs: posterior samples or approximations, credible intervals, convergence diagnostics
benchmark_note: posteriordb gives reference posteriors for accuracy and speed comparison
state_of_art: Stan; PyMC; SAS PROC MCMC

name: Multivariate and exploratory analysis
definition: Given a multivariate data matrix, reduce, ordinate, cluster or classify it with classical methods (PCA, factor, cluster, discriminant, scaling).
inputs: data matrix or distance matrix
outputs: components, factor loadings, clusters, discriminant functions, ordination plots
benchmark_note: results are deterministic for classical methods but quality of exploratory output is judged
state_of_art: SAS; SPSS; PRIMER

name: Survival and time-to-event analysis
definition: Given event times with censoring and covariates, estimate survival curves and hazard models.
inputs: event or censoring times, covariates
outputs: Kaplan-Meier curves, hazard ratios, life tables
benchmark_note: reference datasets with published estimates; simulation with known hazards
state_of_art: SAS PROC PHREG; Stata st

name: Missing data imputation
definition: Given a dataset with missing values and an assumed missingness mechanism, produce imputations and pooled estimates.
inputs: incomplete data table, imputation model
outputs: imputed datasets; pooled estimates with combined variance
benchmark_note: masking known values gives exact imputation error
state_of_art: SAS PROC MI; SPSS Missing Values

name: Experimental and sampling design
definition: Given study goals and constraints, choose the runs, sample sizes or sampling locations that will answer the question efficiently.

name: Factorial and response surface designs
definition: Given factors, levels and run budget, generate a factorial, fractional, mixture or response surface design and analyze its results.
inputs: factors, ranges, constraints, run budget
outputs: design matrix; fitted response surface; optimal settings
benchmark_note: design efficiency (D, I criteria) is computable; usefulness depends on the experiment
state_of_art: JMP; Design-Expert; Minitab

name: Optimal and computer-experiment designs
definition: Given a model and candidate region, construct designs that optimize an information criterion or fill the space for simulation experiments.
inputs: model terms, candidate set or region, criterion
outputs: design points; efficiency values
benchmark_note: criteria values (D-efficiency, discrepancy) compare designs exactly
state_of_art: JMP custom design; Design-Expert

name: Power and sample size
definition: Given a planned test, effect size and error rates, compute the required sample size or achieved power.
inputs: test type, effect size, alpha, variance assumptions
outputs: sample size or power; power curves
benchmark_note: closed-form and simulated reference values
state_of_art: PASS; nQuery

name: Statistical sampling plans
definition: Given a population or site and a decision rule, determine how many units or locations to sample and where.
inputs: population or area, decision error limits, variance estimates
outputs: sample size, sample locations or unit selections
benchmark_note: decision error rates can be simulated
state_of_art: Visual Sample Plan; RAT-STATS

name: Signal and time-series analysis
definition: Given sampled signals or time-indexed series, transform, filter, decompose, model and forecast them.

name: Spectral and Fourier analysis
definition: Given a sampled signal, compute its Fourier transform, power spectrum or time-frequency representation.
inputs: sampled signal, sample rate, window
outputs: spectra, spectrograms, peak frequencies
benchmark_note: transforms of known signals have exact answers; FFT speed is benchmarked (benchFFT)
state_of_art: MATLAB Signal Processing Toolbox; DADiSP

name: Digital filter design and filtering
definition: Given a frequency specification or a noisy signal, design filters and apply them.
inputs: passband and stopband specs or signal plus filter
outputs: filter coefficients; filtered signal; frequency response
benchmark_note: filter responses are checkable against specifications
state_of_art: MATLAB Filter Designer

name: Wavelet and multiresolution analysis
definition: Given a signal or image, compute wavelet decompositions for denoising, compression or feature extraction.
inputs: signal or image, wavelet family, levels
outputs: coefficients; denoised or compressed signal
benchmark_note: denoising error on synthetic signals is measurable
state_of_art: MATLAB Wavelet Toolbox

name: Time-series forecasting
definition: Given a univariate or hierarchical series, fit time-series models (ARIMA, exponential smoothing, state space) and forecast with intervals.
inputs: time-indexed series, horizon, exogenous regressors
outputs: forecasts with prediction intervals; fitted model
benchmark_note: M3, M4 and M5 forecasting competitions give scored datasets
state_of_art: SAS Forecast Server; Autobox; EViews

name: Econometric estimation
definition: Given economic panel or time-series data, estimate structural, panel, instrumental-variable or vector-autoregressive models.
inputs: panel or time-series data, model specification, instruments
outputs: estimates, tests (unit root, cointegration), impulse responses
benchmark_note: published replication datasets with reference estimates
state_of_art: EViews; Stata; OxMetrics

name: Acoustic and speech signal analysis
definition: Given recorded speech or sound, measure pitch, formants, intensity and spectral features.
inputs: audio recordings, analysis settings
outputs: pitch and formant tracks, spectrograms, acoustic measures
benchmark_note: pitch and formant trackers can be scored against annotated corpora
state_of_art: Praat; KayPENTAX CSL

name: Machine learning and data mining
definition: Given example data, learn models that predict, group, generate or find patterns, and apply them to new data.

name: Supervised learning on tabular data
definition: Given labeled feature tables, train classifiers or regressors (trees, ensembles, kernels) and predict labels for new rows.
inputs: feature table with labels; validation scheme
outputs: trained model, predictions, accuracy metrics, feature importance
benchmark_note: OpenML benchmark suites (e.g. OpenML-CC18) and the AutoML Benchmark
state_of_art: XGBoost; LightGBM; DataRobot; H2O Driverless AI

name: Clustering and representation learning
definition: Given unlabeled data, find clusters, low-dimensional embeddings or anomalies.
inputs: feature table or similarity matrix
outputs: cluster labels, embeddings, anomaly scores
benchmark_note: labeled clustering benchmarks and ADBench for anomaly detection; unsupervised quality is otherwise judged
state_of_art: scikit-learn; SAS Enterprise Miner

name: Association rule and pattern mining
definition: Given transactions or event sequences, find frequent itemsets, association rules or sequential patterns.
inputs: transaction or sequence database, support and confidence thresholds
outputs: frequent patterns, rules with support and confidence
benchmark_note: FIMI repository datasets; outputs are exact for given thresholds
state_of_art: SAS Enterprise Miner

name: Neural network training
definition: Given a network architecture, data and loss, train weights by gradient methods and evaluate the trained network.
inputs: architecture, training data, loss, optimizer settings
outputs: trained weights, learning curves, evaluation metrics
benchmark_note: MLPerf Training measures time to a target quality on fixed tasks
state_of_art: PyTorch; JAX; TensorFlow

name: Natural language processing
definition: Given text, tag, parse, classify, extract, embed or generate language with statistical or neural models.
inputs: text corpora, task labels or prompts
outputs: annotations, entities, classes, embeddings, generated text
benchmark_note: GLUE, SuperGLUE, HELM and task-specific shared tasks
state_of_art: GPT and Claude model families; spaCy
open_tools: Hugging Face Transformers; spaCy; NLTK; Stanza

name: Image recognition and detection
definition: Given images or video frames, classify them, detect and segment objects, or estimate pose with learned models.
inputs: labeled or unlabeled images
outputs: class labels, bounding boxes, masks, keypoints
benchmark_note: ImageNet, COCO and similar leaderboards
state_of_art: Segment Anything; YOLO family; Detectron2

name: Mathematical optimization
definition: Given decision variables, an objective and constraints, find optimal or near-optimal values with bounds on the gap.

name: Linear programming
definition: Given a linear objective and linear constraints over continuous variables, compute an optimal basis or certify infeasibility.
inputs: LP model (MPS or modeling-language form)
outputs: optimal solution, duals, reduced costs, status
benchmark_note: Mittelmann benchmarks and Netlib LP set
state_of_art: Gurobi; CPLEX; FICO Xpress; COPT

name: Mixed-integer programming
definition: Given a linear or quadratic model with integer variables, find a proven-optimal or best-found solution and bound.
inputs: MIP model with integrality restrictions
outputs: incumbent solution, best bound, optimality gap
benchmark_note: MIPLIB 2017 with time-to-optimal and gap scoring
state_of_art: Gurobi; CPLEX; FICO Xpress

name: Nonlinear programming
definition: Given smooth nonlinear objectives and constraints, find local or global optima.
inputs: objective and constraint functions, derivatives, bounds
outputs: optimal point, multipliers, convergence status
benchmark_note: CUTEst and MINLPLib problem sets
state_of_art: Knitro; SNOPT; BARON

name: Constraint programming
definition: Given discrete variables with logical and combinatorial constraints, find feasible or optimal assignments by propagation and search.
inputs: variables, domains, global constraints, objective
outputs: assignments, proof of infeasibility or optimality
benchmark_note: the annual MiniZinc Challenge and SAT competitions
state_of_art: IBM CP Optimizer; OR-Tools CP-SAT

name: Derivative-free and evolutionary search
definition: Given a black-box objective, search for good solutions with genetic, evolutionary, swarm or surrogate methods.
inputs: objective function, variable bounds, evaluation budget
outputs: best solutions found, convergence history, Pareto fronts
benchmark_note: BBOB/COCO benchmark functions with anytime performance scoring
state_of_art: Optuna; modeFRONTIER

name: Algebraic optimization modeling
definition: Given an optimization model written in algebraic notation plus data, generate the solver instance, call a solver and report results.
inputs: model file, data tables, solver choice
outputs: solver instance, solution reports, sensitivity data
benchmark_note: model generation time on large instances is measurable; expressiveness is not
state_of_art: AMPL; GAMS; AIMMS

name: Model calibration and parameter estimation
definition: Given a forward model and observations, estimate the parameters that best fit, with uncertainty.
inputs: forward model, observations, parameter bounds, weights
outputs: calibrated parameters, residuals, parameter uncertainty
benchmark_note: synthetic problems with known parameters; NIST StRD nonlinear regression
state_of_art: PEST; MATLAB lsqnonlin

name: General-purpose stochastic simulation
definition: Given a model with random inputs or discrete events, simulate many realizations and summarize the distribution of outcomes.

name: Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation
definition: Given a model with uncertain inputs as distributions, sample them, propagate through the model and report output distributions and sensitivities.
inputs: model (often a spreadsheet), input distributions, correlations
outputs: output distributions, percentiles, sensitivity rankings
benchmark_note: analytic test functions (Ishigami, Sobol g) have known moments and sensitivity indices
state_of_art: @Risk; Crystal Ball; Analytica

name: Discrete-event simulation
definition: Given entities, resources, queues and event logic, simulate system behavior over time and report throughput, waits and utilization.
inputs: process logic, arrival and service distributions, resources
outputs: time series of state, queue statistics, utilization, confidence intervals
benchmark_note: queueing models with analytic solutions (M/M/c, Jackson networks) check correctness
state_of_art: Arena; AnyLogic; Simio; ExtendSim

name: Agent-based and cellular automaton simulation
definition: Given agent or cell rules and an initial population or lattice, simulate the emergent collective dynamics.
inputs: agent rules, interaction topology, initial state
outputs: population trajectories, spatial patterns, summary statistics
benchmark_note: reference models (e.g. Game of Life, Schelling) reproduce known behavior; validity is otherwise domain-specific
state_of_art: AnyLogic; NetLogo

name: Decision tree and Markov model analysis
definition: Given decisions, chance nodes, probabilities and payoffs or a state-transition model, compute expected values and optimal policies.
inputs: decision tree or Markov states, transition probabilities, costs and utilities
outputs: expected values, optimal strategy, cost-effectiveness, sensitivity results
benchmark_note: expected values are exactly computable for given trees and chains
state_of_art: TreeAge Pro; Analytica

name: Scientific visualization and image analysis
definition: Given numerical data or scientific images, render them as plots or 3D views, or extract quantitative measurements from them.

name: Scientific charts and plots
definition: Given numeric data, produce publication-quality 2D and 3D plots, histograms and fitted curves.
inputs: data tables, plot specification
outputs: figures (vector or raster), fitted curves
benchmark_note: plot-generation benchmarks (e.g. MatPlotBench) score code-to-figure tasks; visual quality is judged
state_of_art: Origin; Prism; MATLAB graphics

name: Volume and field visualization
definition: Given gridded or meshed scalar and vector fields, render isosurfaces, slices, streamlines and volume renderings.
inputs: structured or unstructured grids with field values
outputs: interactive 3D views, images, animations
benchmark_note: rendering throughput is measurable; insight is not
state_of_art: Tecplot 360; Avizo; EnSight

name: Interactive exploratory data graphics
definition: Given a multivariate dataset, provide linked, brushable views for exploring structure before modeling.
inputs: data table
outputs: linked interactive plots, selections, saved views
benchmark_note: usefulness is a matter of user judgment
state_of_art: JMP; Tableau

name: Microscopy image quantification
definition: Given light, fluorescence or scanning-probe microscope images, segment objects and measure counts, sizes, intensities and tracks.
inputs: 2D or 3D image stacks, calibration
outputs: segmentation masks, object measurements, tracks
benchmark_note: Cell Tracking Challenge and the Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection
state_of_art: Imaris; NIS-Elements; ZEN; Aivia
open_tools: Fiji; CellProfiler; QuPath; napari; ilastik; Gwyddion

name: Chromosome and cytogenetic image analysis
definition: Given metaphase or interphase cell images, locate, classify and pair chromosomes or score FISH, CGH and comet assay signals.
inputs: stained or hybridized cell images
outputs: karyograms, signal counts, DNA damage scores
benchmark_note: annotated karyotype image sets exist for classification accuracy
state_of_art: MetaSystems Ikaros and Isis; Leica CytoVision

name: Astronomical image reduction
definition: Given raw telescope frames or interferometer visibilities, calibrate, stack, image and extract sources and photometry.
inputs: raw frames, calibration frames, visibilities
outputs: calibrated images, source catalogs, photometry and astrometry
benchmark_note: simulated images with known sources score detection and photometry
state_of_art: CASA; PixInsight; MaxIm DL

name: Video motion tracking
definition: Given video or marker data of moving subjects, track points, reconstruct 3D trajectories and compute kinematics.
inputs: video or marker streams, camera calibration
outputs: point trajectories, joint angles, velocities
benchmark_note: pose-estimation datasets with ground truth (e.g. Human3.6M)
state_of_art: Vicon Nexus; Qualisys Track Manager; Dartfish

name: Instrument control and data acquisition
definition: Given laboratory instruments and sensors, configure them, run measurement sequences and record time-stamped data.

name: Sensor data acquisition and logging
definition: Given sensors on acquisition hardware, configure channels and sampling, acquire, scale and store the signals.
inputs: channel configuration, sample rates, triggers, sensor calibrations
outputs: time-stamped data files; live displays
benchmark_note: throughput and timing jitter are measurable but tied to hardware
state_of_art: LabVIEW with NI-DAQmx; DEWESoft; LabChart

name: Bench instrument control
definition: Given programmable instruments (meters, sources, analyzers), script their settings and readings into an automated measurement.
inputs: instrument drivers or command sets, measurement procedure
outputs: measurement data, instrument state logs
benchmark_note: success depends on the hardware attached
state_of_art: LabVIEW; Keysight PathWave BenchVue

name: Automated test sequencing
definition: Given a test plan of measurement steps and limits, execute it against a device under test and report pass/fail results.
inputs: test sequence, limits, device under test
outputs: test reports, pass/fail logs, measurement records
benchmark_note: depends on hardware under test
state_of_art: NI TestStand; Keysight PathWave Test Executive

name: Large experiment control systems
definition: Given the devices of an accelerator, telescope or beamline, provide distributed process variables, sequencing, archiving and alarms.
inputs: device drivers, process variable database, sequences
outputs: live process variables, archived data, alarms
benchmark_note: facility-specific
state_of_art: EPICS; Tango Controls

name: Analytical instrument data processing
definition: Given raw output from analytical instruments, process it into identified and quantified components.

name: Chromatogram processing and quantitation
definition: Given chromatograms, detect and integrate peaks, identify them against standards and compute concentrations.
inputs: detector traces, method, calibration standards
outputs: peak tables, concentrations, system-suitability results
benchmark_note: simulated and reference chromatograms test integration accuracy
state_of_art: Waters Empower; Thermo Chromeleon; Agilent OpenLab

name: Mass spectrometry data analysis
definition: Given mass spectra or LC-MS runs, detect features, identify compounds or peptides and quantify them.
inputs: raw spectra, databases or libraries, search parameters
outputs: feature tables, identifications with scores, quantities
benchmark_note: CASMI contest and proteomics benchmark datasets
state_of_art: Thermo Proteome Discoverer; Spectronaut; Agilent MassHunter

name: Optical and X-ray spectroscopy analysis
definition: Given infrared, Raman, UV-visible or X-ray fluorescence spectra, correct baselines, identify materials and quantify components.
inputs: spectra, reference libraries, calibration sets
outputs: identified compounds, concentrations, chemometric models
benchmark_note: library-search accuracy and chemometric prediction error on reference sets
state_of_art: Bruker OPUS; Thermo OMNIC; GRAMS

name: Nuclear magnetic resonance processing
definition: Given free induction decays, transform, phase and assign spectra and derive structures or quantities.
inputs: FIDs, acquisition parameters, molecule hypotheses
outputs: processed spectra, peak lists, assignments, concentrations
benchmark_note: chemical-shift prediction and assignment have reference datasets
state_of_art: TopSpin; Mnova; ACD/NMR Workbook

name: Powder diffraction phase analysis
definition: Given X-ray powder patterns, identify phases, refine structures by the Rietveld method and quantify phase fractions.
inputs: diffraction patterns, phase databases, instrument profile
outputs: phase identifications, refined lattice parameters, phase fractions
benchmark_note: IUCr round-robin samples have known compositions
state_of_art: TOPAS; HighScore Plus; Jade

name: Flow cytometry analysis
definition: Given per-cell fluorescence events, compensate, gate populations and report frequencies and cell-cycle fits.
inputs: FCS event files, panel definitions, gating strategy
outputs: gated populations, frequencies, DNA content models
benchmark_note: FlowCAP challenges score automated gating against expert gates
state_of_art: FlowJo; FCS Express; OMIQ

name: Microplate assay and dose-response analysis
definition: Given plate-reader readings and a plate layout, fit standard curves and dose-response models and report potencies.
inputs: plate reads, layout, concentrations
outputs: standard curves, EC50/IC50 values, toxicity endpoints
benchmark_note: dose-response fits are checkable against reference fits
state_of_art: SoftMax Pro; Prism; Genedata Screener

name: Laboratory informatics
definition: Given the samples, methods and observations of a research or testing laboratory, record, track and report them with an audit trail.

name: Laboratory sample and test management
definition: Given incoming samples and test requests, register, assign, track results through review and issue certificates of analysis.
inputs: sample registrations, test methods, specifications, results
outputs: sample status, approved results, certificates, audit trail
benchmark_note: a records workflow, judged by requirements coverage (the ASTM E1578 checklist), not a computed answer
state_of_art: LabWare LIMS; LabVantage; STARLIMS; Thermo SampleManager

name: Electronic laboratory notebooks
definition: Given experiments as they happen, capture protocols, observations, data files and sign-offs in a searchable, time-stamped record.
inputs: protocols, observations, attached data, signatures
outputs: notebook entries, witnessed records, searchable archive
benchmark_note: a records tool
state_of_art: Benchling; Revvity Signals Notebook; LabArchives

name: Research data capture
definition: Given a study instrument, build validated data-entry forms and collect, clean and export study records.
inputs: form definitions, validation rules, participants or field sites
outputs: validated datasets, audit logs, exports to statistics packages
benchmark_note: a data-collection workflow
state_of_art: REDCap; Medidata Rave

name: Survey and behavioral research methods
definition: Given research questions about people, collect responses, observations and experimental behavior and turn them into analyzable data.

name: Questionnaire design and fielding
definition: Given a questionnaire with routing logic, field it online or by interviewer and collect responses.
inputs: questions, skip logic, sample lists, quotas
outputs: response datasets, paradata, completion reports
benchmark_note: a data-collection workflow
state_of_art: Qualtrics; Forsta (Confirmit); Voxco

name: Survey tabulation and weighting
definition: Given survey responses and a sample design, weight to population totals, produce cross-tabulations and design-based variances.
inputs: response data, design variables, population margins
outputs: weights, banner tables, estimates with design-based standard errors
benchmark_note: design-based variance estimates can be checked against published reference computations
state_of_art: SUDAAN; WinCross; Stata svy

name: Qualitative data coding
definition: Given interview transcripts, field notes or media, apply and organize codes and retrieve coded segments for interpretation.
inputs: transcripts, documents, media, code book
outputs: coded segments, code co-occurrence, memos
benchmark_note: coder agreement against a gold-coded corpus is measurable
state_of_art: NVivo; ATLAS.ti; MAXQDA

name: Behavioral experiment presentation
definition: Given an experimental design, present stimuli or economic games to participants and record responses with precise timing.
inputs: stimulus lists, trial structure, game rules
outputs: trial-level response and reaction-time data
benchmark_note: stimulus-timing accuracy is measurable (published timing mega-studies)
state_of_art: E-Prime; Inquisit; Gorilla

name: Behavioral observation coding
definition: Given live sessions or video, code behavioral events and states on a timeline and compute frequencies, durations and sequences.
inputs: video or live session, ethogram or coding scheme
outputs: event logs, durations, sequential statistics, inter-observer reliability
benchmark_note: automated coders can be scored against human-coded video
state_of_art: Noldus Observer XT; Mangold INTERACT

name: Social network analysis
definition: Given relational data among actors, compute centrality, communities and network models.
inputs: edge lists or adjacency matrices with attributes
outputs: centrality scores, communities, fitted network models
benchmark_note: algorithms are exact; model fit on reference networks is comparable
state_of_art: UCINET; Gephi

name: Biological sequence analysis
definition: Given DNA, RNA or protein sequences, compare, align, annotate, design and relate them.

name: Sequence similarity search
definition: Given a query sequence and a database, find similar sequences with alignment scores and significance.
inputs: query sequences, sequence databases
outputs: ranked hits, local alignments, E-values
benchmark_note: SCOP- and Pfam-based homology benchmarks score sensitivity and speed
state_of_art: NCBI BLAST; DIAMOND; MMseqs2

name: Multiple sequence alignment
definition: Given a set of related sequences, align them column by column for comparison.
inputs: unaligned sequences
outputs: multiple alignment, conservation scores
benchmark_note: BAliBASE and HomFam reference alignments
state_of_art: MAFFT; Clustal Omega

name: Phylogenetic inference
definition: Given aligned sequences or characters, infer evolutionary trees with branch support and divergence times.
inputs: alignment or character matrix, substitution model
outputs: trees with branch lengths and support values
benchmark_note: simulated alignments on known trees score topology accuracy
state_of_art: IQ-TREE; RAxML-NG; BEAST

name: Gene prediction and genome annotation
definition: Given genomic sequence, locate genes, repeats, operons and regulatory elements and assign functions.
inputs: assembled genome or contigs, evidence (transcripts, proteins)
outputs: gene models, repeat masks, functional annotations
benchmark_note: reference annotations (e.g. GENCODE) and BUSCO completeness
state_of_art: BRAKER; NCBI PGAP

name: Sequence editing, cloning and primer design
definition: Given DNA sequences and an experimental goal, design primers and probes, simulate digests and assemble cloning constructs.
inputs: template sequences, design constraints, enzymes and vectors
outputs: primers and probes, construct maps, digest predictions
benchmark_note: in-silico checks (specificity, melting temperature) are computable; wet-lab success is not
state_of_art: Benchling; SnapGene; Geneious Prime

name: Protein sequence property analysis
definition: Given protein sequences, compute physicochemical properties and predict domains, secondary structure and localization.
inputs: protein sequences
outputs: property profiles, domain and motif annotations, secondary-structure predictions
benchmark_note: CAFA function prediction and secondary-structure test sets
state_of_art: InterProScan; PredictProtein

name: High-throughput genomic data analysis
definition: Given sequencing reads or array data from many molecules, reconstruct genomes, find variants and measure expression.

name: Sequence read mapping
definition: Given short or long sequencing reads and a reference genome or transcriptome, place each read with an alignment and mapping quality.
inputs: FASTQ reads, reference sequence and index
outputs: BAM/SAM alignments, mapping statistics
benchmark_note: simulated reads and GIAB truth sets score accuracy and speed
state_of_art: DRAGEN; BWA-MEM2; minimap2

name: Genome assembly and base calling
definition: Given raw sequencing traces or reads, call bases and assemble them into contigs and scaffolds.
inputs: raw traces or reads, optional long-range data
outputs: base calls with qualities, contigs, scaffolds, assembly metrics
benchmark_note: Assemblathon, QUAST and reference genomes score contiguity and correctness
state_of_art: hifiasm; Verkko; Dorado

name: Variant calling and genotyping
definition: Given aligned reads or genotyping signals, identify sequence variants and assign genotypes with quality scores.
inputs: alignments or intensity/fragment data, reference
outputs: VCF variant calls, genotypes, quality metrics
benchmark_note: Genome in a Bottle truth sets and precisionFDA challenges
state_of_art: DRAGEN; DeepVariant; GATK

name: Gene expression quantification
definition: Given RNA-seq reads or microarray intensities, quantify expression per gene or transcript and test differential expression.
inputs: reads or array images/intensities, annotation, sample design
outputs: expression matrices, differential expression results, clusters
benchmark_note: SEQC/MAQC consortium datasets with known ratios
state_of_art: Partek Flow; Qiagen CLC Genomics

name: Linkage and association mapping
definition: Given genotypes and phenotypes of related or unrelated individuals, locate loci linked to or associated with traits.
inputs: genotype matrices, pedigrees, phenotypes, covariates
outputs: LOD scores or association statistics, genetic maps, candidate loci
benchmark_note: simulated traits with planted loci score power and false-positive rate
state_of_art: Golden Helix SVS; REGENIE

name: Biochemical and physiological systems modeling
definition: Given biological pathways or mechanisms, build quantitative models of their dynamics or test data against known networks.

name: Pathway and network enrichment
definition: Given a list of genes, proteins or metabolites with measurements, map them to known pathways and test for enrichment.
inputs: gene or metabolite lists with statistics, pathway databases
outputs: enriched pathways, network views, upstream regulators
benchmark_note: benchmark gene sets with known perturbed pathways exist
state_of_art: QIAGEN IPA; MetaCore

name: Reaction network kinetics
definition: Given reactions, rate laws and parameters, simulate concentrations over time, find steady states and estimate parameters.
inputs: reaction network (often SBML), rate laws, initial conditions
outputs: concentration time courses, steady states, sensitivities
benchmark_note: SBML Test Suite and curated BioModels give reference trajectories
state_of_art: SimBiology; COPASI

name: Neuron and membrane models
definition: Given membrane channel kinetics and morphology, simulate membrane potentials and spiking of cells and networks.
inputs: channel models, morphology, stimuli
outputs: voltage traces, spike times, currents
benchmark_note: reference simulations and model-database reproductions
state_of_art: NEURON; Brian 2

name: Predictive microbial growth
definition: Given organism, temperature, pH, water activity and other factors, predict microbial growth or inactivation over time.
inputs: organism, environmental conditions, initial load
outputs: growth or decline curves, lag times, generation times
benchmark_note: ComBase observations allow prediction-error scoring
state_of_art: ComBase Predictor; Pathogen Modeling Program

name: Molecular modeling and structural biology
definition: Given atoms, molecules or experimental structure data, compute energies, motions, binding and three-dimensional structures.

name: Electronic structure calculation
definition: Given atomic positions (molecules or periodic cells) and a level of theory, compute energies, geometries, spectra and properties from quantum mechanics.
inputs: geometry, charge and spin, basis set or plane-wave cutoff, method
outputs: energies, optimized geometries, orbitals, vibrational and electronic spectra
benchmark_note: GMTKN55 and the solid-state Delta test give reference energies
state_of_art: Gaussian; VASP; ORCA; Q-Chem
open_tools: Quantum ESPRESSO; CP2K; NWChem; Psi4; PySCF; GAMESS (free)

name: Molecular dynamics and mechanics
definition: Given a molecular system, force field and conditions, integrate atomic motion and compute ensembles, free energies and transport properties.
inputs: coordinates, topology, force field, thermostat and barostat settings
outputs: trajectories, energies, free energies, structural statistics
benchmark_note: free-energy benchmark sets (e.g. FreeSolv) and throughput benchmarks
state_of_art: AMBER; Desmond; GROMACS

name: Docking and virtual screening
definition: Given a target structure and candidate ligands, predict binding poses and rank ligands by estimated affinity.
inputs: receptor structure, binding site, ligand library
outputs: poses, docking scores, ranked hit lists
benchmark_note: PDBbind/CASF, DUD-E and PoseBusters
state_of_art: Schrödinger Glide; CCDC GOLD; OpenEye FRED

name: Protein structure prediction and design
definition: Given an amino-acid sequence (or a target fold), predict its 3D structure, or design sequences and assess stability changes.
inputs: sequences or target backbone, templates or alignments
outputs: 3D models with confidence, designed sequences, stability estimates
benchmark_note: CASP and CAMEO blind assessments
state_of_art: AlphaFold 3; RoseTTAFold; ESMFold

name: Experimental structure determination
definition: Given X-ray diffraction images or electron micrographs, index, phase and reconstruct maps and refine an atomic model.
inputs: diffraction images or micrographs, sequence, symmetry
outputs: electron-density or cryo-EM maps, refined atomic models, validation reports
benchmark_note: EMDB/PDB deposits with validation metrics allow map-model comparison
state_of_art: Phenix; cryoSPARC; RELION

name: Molecular visualization and building
definition: Given molecular or crystal structures, render, inspect, edit and build them interactively.
inputs: coordinate files, crystal data
outputs: rendered views, measurements, edited or built structures
benchmark_note: interactive viewing; judged by users
state_of_art: PyMOL; ChimeraX; Maestro

name: Cheminformatics
definition: Given chemical structures as data, draw, store, search and model them to predict properties and plan syntheses.

name: Chemical structure drawing and search
definition: Given structures drawn or imported, store them and search collections by exact, substructure or similarity match.
inputs: drawings, SMILES or molfiles, query structures
outputs: canonical structures, names, search hits
benchmark_note: name-to-structure and image-to-structure sets score conversion; search is exact
state_of_art: ChemDraw; BIOVIA Pipeline Pilot; ChemAxon Marvin
open_tools: RDKit; Open Babel; CDK; Ketcher; OPSIN

name: Molecular property and toxicity prediction
definition: Given molecular structures, predict physicochemical properties, activities or toxicity from structure-activity models.
inputs: structures, training data with measured endpoints
outputs: predicted properties with applicability domain
benchmark_note: MoleculeNet, Tox21 and TDC leaderboards
state_of_art: Simulations Plus ADMET Predictor; Derek Nexus; Chemprop

name: Synthesis route planning
definition: Given a target molecule and available building blocks, propose retrosynthetic routes and reaction conditions.
inputs: target structure, stock compounds, reaction templates or models
outputs: ranked synthetic routes, predicted conditions
benchmark_note: USPTO-50k single-step accuracy and route-finding benchmarks
state_of_art: Synthia; Reaxys Predictive Retrosynthesis; CAS SciFinder retrosynthesis

name: Move goods and people
definition: Planning and running the movement and storage of things and travelers: supply-chain planning, warehousing, transport management, routing and dispatch, and the operation of vehicles, aircraft, ships and trains.

name: Supply chain planning
definition: Given demand history, the network of sites and lanes, lead times and costs, decide how much to stock, make and move where and when, and where facilities should be.

name: Demand forecasting for replenishment
definition: Given sales or shipment history by item and location with calendar and promotion data, produce forecasts at the levels planners use.
inputs: item-location demand history, hierarchy, calendar, prices and promotions
outputs: point and quantile forecasts by item, location and period
benchmark_note: the M5 competition (Walmart hierarchical unit sales) has public data and scoring
state_of_art: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; SAP Integrated Business Planning; o9 Solutions; Oracle Demantra; RELEX Solutions; Blue Yonder Luminate Demand; SAP Unified Demand Forecast

name: Multi-site supply planning
definition: Given net demand, sourcing rules, site capacities and lead times across a network, decide production, transfer and purchase quantities by period.
inputs: demand plan, bills of distribution, capacities, lead times, costs
outputs: time-phased supply plan by site and lane; capacity and shortage exceptions
benchmark_note: formulations are standard linear and mixed-integer programs, but there is no shared instance set
state_of_art: Kinaxis RapidResponse; SAP Integrated Business Planning; Blue Yonder Supply Planning; o9 Solutions

name: Inventory policy optimization
definition: Given demand distributions, lead times, costs and service targets for one or many echelons, set safety stocks, reorder points and order quantities.
inputs: demand and lead-time distributions, holding and shortage costs, network structure, service targets
outputs: safety stock, reorder point and order-up-to levels by item and location; expected service and cost
benchmark_note: Willems (2008) published 38 real multi-echelon supply chains for safety-stock placement, with reference solutions
state_of_art: SAP Integrated Business Planning for Inventory; ToolsGroup SO99+; Logility

name: Supply chain network design
definition: Given candidate facility sites, demand points, flows and costs, choose which facilities to open and how to assign flows to minimize cost under capacity limits.
inputs: customer demand, candidate sites and capacities, fixed and variable costs, transport costs
outputs: facilities to open, flow assignment, total cost and service levels
benchmark_note: OR-Library capacitated warehouse location instances (Beasley) and the Holmberg capacitated facility location set
state_of_art: Coupa Supply Chain Modeler; AIMMS SC Navigator; anyLogistix; Optilogic Cosmic Frog

name: Warehouse and inventory control
definition: Given stock, storage locations, orders and identification events, keep an accurate record of what is where and direct the work of storing, picking and packing it.

name: Storage location assignment
definition: Given items, their demand and dimensions, and a warehouse layout, assign items to storage locations (slotting and putaway) to reduce travel and respect constraints.
inputs: SKU velocity and dimensions, location dimensions, layout, compatibility rules
outputs: item-to-location assignment; expected pick travel
benchmark_note: slotting is a quadratic assignment problem with QAPLIB instances, but no warehouse-specific shared set
state_of_art: Manhattan Active Warehouse Management; Blue Yonder Warehouse Management; SAP Extended Warehouse Management; Körber WMS

name: Order batching and picker routing
definition: Given open orders, item locations and the warehouse layout, group orders into pick batches or waves and sequence each picker's route.
inputs: order lines, item locations, aisle layout, picker and cart capacity
outputs: batches or waves, pick lists in route sequence, travel distance
benchmark_note: picker routing in rectangular warehouses has exact algorithms (Ratliff and Rosenthal) and published batching instances, but no single standard set
state_of_art: Manhattan Active Warehouse Management; Blue Yonder Warehouse Management; SAP Extended Warehouse Management

name: Cartonization and pack planning
definition: Given the items of an order and the available box sizes, choose boxes and item placements that minimize shipped volume or cost.
inputs: item dimensions and weights, box catalogue, carrier dimensional-weight rules
outputs: boxes per order with item assignments and placements
benchmark_note: three-dimensional bin packing instance classes of Martello, Pisinger and Vigo
state_of_art: Paccurate; Manhattan Active Warehouse Management

name: Stock records and cycle counting
definition: Given receipts, issues, transfers and counts, maintain on-hand balances by item, lot and location, and schedule counts to find and correct discrepancies.
inputs: inventory transactions, count results, item and location master data
outputs: on-hand balances, custody history, count schedules and variance adjustments
benchmark_note: record keeping is transactional; correctness is a matter of tests, not a leaderboard
state_of_art: SAP S/4HANA Inventory Management; NetSuite; Fishbowl

name: Barcode and logistics label generation
definition: Given identifiers and shipment data, encode them in linear or two-dimensional symbols and lay out a compliant label for printing.
inputs: identifiers (item number, serial shipping container code, lot, dates), label template, printer
outputs: printable label with conformant barcode symbols
benchmark_note: generated symbols can be graded against ISO/IEC 15415 and 15416 and GS1 application-identifier rules
state_of_art: Seagull BarTender; Loftware NiceLabel; ZebraDesigner

name: Barcode decoding from images
definition: Given a camera or scanner image, locate and decode every linear and two-dimensional symbol in it.
inputs: image or scan line
outputs: decoded symbol data, symbology and position
benchmark_note: public barcode image datasets (Muenster BarcodeDB, ArTe-Lab 1D barcode collections) give decode-rate benchmarks
state_of_art: Scandit; Dynamsoft Barcode Reader; Cognex

name: RFID and identification event capture
definition: Given raw tag reads from readers and portals, filter and translate them into business events saying what was observed where, when and why.
inputs: raw tag reads, reader and location configuration, tag data encoding
outputs: standard visibility events (object, aggregation, transaction) in a repository
benchmark_note: EPCIS conformance can be tested; read filtering lacks shared datasets
state_of_art: Zebra; Impinj ItemSense; SAP Advanced Track and Trace

name: Lot traceability
definition: Given recorded transformation and shipment events, trace a lot forward to everyone who received it and backward to every input it came from.
inputs: lot-level receipt, transformation and shipment events
outputs: forward and backward trace graphs; recall lists
benchmark_note: answers are exact given the events, so synthetic event sets can score completeness, but none are shared
state_of_art: TraceLink; SAP Advanced Track and Trace; rfxcel

name: Freight transportation management
definition: Given shipments to move, carriers, rates and equipment, decide how to consolidate, load, price, book and follow them to delivery.

name: Freight rating and carrier selection
definition: Given a shipment and carriers' contracts and tariffs, compute each carrier's charges with accessorials and choose the carrier and service.
inputs: origin, destination, freight class, weight, dimensions, service, tariffs and contracts
outputs: rated quotes by carrier and service; selected carrier
benchmark_note: rating is deterministic given tariffs, but tariffs are proprietary
state_of_art: Oracle Transportation Management; Blue Yonder Transportation Management; SAP Transportation Management; MercuryGate; SMC3 CzarLite

name: Freight lane procurement
definition: Given lanes, volumes and carrier bids, including package bids, award lanes to carriers to minimize cost subject to capacity and business rules.
inputs: lane volumes, carrier bids and package bids, capacity and award rules
outputs: lane awards by carrier; expected cost
benchmark_note: winner determination instances from the Combinatorial Auction Test Suite include a transport-like 'paths' distribution
state_of_art: Keelvar; Coupa Sourcing Optimization; Blue Yonder Transportation Procurement

name: Shipment consolidation and load building
definition: Given orders with dates, sizes and destinations, group them into truckloads, multi-stop loads or less-than-truckload shipments and choose the mode.
inputs: orders, ship windows, equipment, rates by mode
outputs: planned loads with stops and modes; cost
benchmark_note: modeled as vehicle routing with split deliveries; no consolidation-specific instance set
state_of_art: Oracle Transportation Management; Blue Yonder Transportation Management; SAP Transportation Management

name: Container and truck load planning
definition: Given cargo items and a container, trailer or aircraft hold, place the items in three dimensions to maximize utilization while meeting weight, axle, stacking and stability limits.
inputs: item dimensions, weights, orientations, stacking rules; container dimensions and weight limits
outputs: three-dimensional placement and load sequence; utilization and weight distribution
benchmark_note: Bischoff and Ratcliff container loading classes BR1 to BR15 in OR-Library
state_of_art: EasyCargo; Logen CubeMaster; TOPS Pro

name: Pallet and case pattern design
definition: Given a case size and pallet, or a product and candidate cases, find stacking patterns that maximize cases per pallet within height and weight limits.
inputs: product or case dimensions, pallet size, height and weight limits
outputs: layer patterns and stack; cases per pallet
benchmark_note: the manufacturer's pallet loading problem has standard Cover I and Cover II instance sets
state_of_art: CAPE PACK; TOPS Pro

name: Shipment tracking and arrival prediction
definition: Given carrier status messages, positions and proof-of-delivery records, keep each shipment's status current and predict its arrival time.
inputs: status messages, positions, schedules, delivery confirmations
outputs: shipment status, predicted arrival with uncertainty, exceptions
benchmark_note: arrival-time error can be scored on public vessel AIS and trip data, but no shared freight set
state_of_art: project44; FourKites; Descartes MacroPoint

name: Freight forwarding and consolidation
definition: Given a customer's shipment, book multi-leg, multi-modal carriage, consolidate it into master shipments and produce house and master documents.
inputs: shipment details, routings, carrier schedules and space
outputs: bookings, house and master bills, consolidated manifests
benchmark_note: transactional workflow without an optimization or prediction target
state_of_art: CargoWise; Magaya; Riege Scope

name: Parcel and mail processing
definition: Given packages and mail pieces with addresses, validate the addresses, rate, label and presort the pieces, and read and sort them in the postal network.

name: Multi-carrier parcel rating and labeling
definition: Given a package and destination, rate it across parcel carriers and services, then produce the carrier label, manifest and tracking number.
inputs: package weight and dimensions, addresses, service requirements, carrier accounts
outputs: rates by carrier, chosen service, carrier label, manifest, tracking number
benchmark_note: carrier rate tables are public, so rating is checkable, but label conformance is carrier-certified
state_of_art: ShipStation; ProShip; UPS WorldShip

name: Postal address validation
definition: Given a free-text or fielded address, parse and standardize it and match it to the postal authority's deliverable-address file.
inputs: address text or fields
outputs: standardized address, delivery point code, match confidence
benchmark_note: USPS CASS certification test files have reference answers
state_of_art: Smarty; Loqate; Melissa

name: Mail presort and postage calculation
definition: Given a mailing list and mail class, sort pieces into the trays, sacks and pallets the postal rules define and compute the discounted postage.
inputs: addresses, mail class and shape, postal sortation rules and rates
outputs: presorted list, container labels, postage statement
benchmark_note: USPS PAVE certification checks presort output against rules, but test sets are not public
state_of_art: BCC Mail Manager; Satori Bulk Mailer; Window Book DAT-MAIL

name: Address recognition and sortation
definition: Given images of mail pieces or parcels, read the destination address and barcode and assign each piece to a sort destination.
inputs: piece images, address directory, sort plan
outputs: recognized address, delivery point, sort bin
