benchmark_note: in-between frame generation is scored on ATD-12K; full animation is judged
state_of_art: Toon Boom Harmony; Moho; TVPaint; Adobe Animate

name: Screen recording and capture
definition: Given a computer display and narration, capture, annotate and lightly edit a screen recording or screenshot.
inputs: display output, microphone and webcam, annotations
outputs: screencast video or annotated screenshots
benchmark_note: device capture and simple editing; nothing to score beyond performance
state_of_art: TechSmith Camtasia; Loom; TechSmith Snagit

name: Video generation from text
definition: Given a text description and optional images or clips, synthesize a new video clip that matches the description.
inputs: text prompt, optional reference images or video
outputs: generated video clips
benchmark_note: VBench scores prompt adherence, temporal consistency and quality on a fixed prompt set
state_of_art: Google Veo; OpenAI Sora; Runway Gen-4; Kling

name: 3D modeling and character animation
definition: Given concept art, references or captured motion, build 3D surface models, materials and rigs and animate them.

name: Polygon and subdivision modeling
definition: Given references or a brief, build a polygon or subdivision-surface mesh of an object, character or set.
inputs: concept art, reference images, scale
outputs: polygon or subdivision meshes (FBX, OBJ, glTF, USD)
benchmark_note: text-to-3D and image-to-3D generation are scored on Objaverse-derived sets and GPTEval3D; hand modeling is judged
state_of_art: Autodesk Maya; Autodesk 3ds Max; Blender; Maxon Cinema 4D

name: Digital sculpting
definition: Given a base mesh, sculpt high-resolution organic detail with brush tools and bake it to displacement or normal maps.
inputs: base mesh, brush strokes, alphas
outputs: high-resolution sculpted mesh, displacement and normal maps
benchmark_note: artistic output; only map baking accuracy is measurable
state_of_art: Maxon ZBrush; Autodesk Mudbox; Nomad Sculpt

name: UV mapping, texturing and look development
definition: Given a mesh, unwrap UVs and paint or procedurally generate physically based material maps.
inputs: mesh, reference photographs, material definitions
outputs: UV layouts, PBR texture maps, shader networks
benchmark_note: UV distortion and material capture from photos (SVBRDF estimation) are measurable
state_of_art: Adobe Substance 3D Painter; Adobe Substance 3D Designer; Foundry Mari

name: Procedural terrain and environments
definition: Given rules and parameters, generate natural landscapes, vegetation and skies for film or games.
inputs: height or noise parameters, erosion settings, ecosystem rules
outputs: terrain meshes or heightfields, scattered vegetation, atmosphere settings
benchmark_note: visual plausibility is judged
state_of_art: World Machine; Gaea; Terragen; SpeedTree

name: Character rigging and skinning
definition: Given a character mesh, build a skeleton, controls and deformation weights so it can be posed and animated.
inputs: character mesh, joint placement, deformation requirements
outputs: rigged character with skin weights and controls
benchmark_note: automatic rigging is scored on joint and skin-weight error (RigNet dataset)
state_of_art: Autodesk Maya; AccuRIG; Mixamo auto-rigger

name: Keyframe character animation
definition: Given a rigged character and performance direction, set and interpolate poses over time to produce an animated performance.
inputs: rigged characters, timing, audio, choreography
outputs: animation curves, animated scenes
benchmark_note: motion in-betweening and text-to-motion are scored on HumanML3D and LaFAN1; hand animation is judged
state_of_art: Autodesk Maya; Autodesk MotionBuilder; Cascadeur

name: Motion capture processing and retargeting
definition: Given marker, sensor or video recordings of a performer, solve a skeleton motion, clean it and retarget it to a character.
inputs: optical marker data, inertial data or video; performer and target skeletons
outputs: cleaned skeletal animation on the target rig
benchmark_note: 3D pose estimation error is scored on Human3.6M and AMASS
state_of_art: Vicon Shogun; Autodesk MotionBuilder; Move AI

name: Rendering and effects simulation
definition: Given 3D scenes, materials, lights and simulation setups, compute images and visually plausible physical effects.

name: Offline physically based rendering
definition: Given a scene description with geometry, materials, lights and camera, compute a photorealistic image by path tracing or similar light transport.
inputs: scene geometry, materials, lights, camera, render settings (USD, RIB)
outputs: rendered images and passes (OpenEXR)
benchmark_note: error against converged reference images versus render time on standard scenes
state_of_art: Pixar RenderMan; Chaos V-Ray; Autodesk Arnold; Redshift
open_tools: Blender Cycles; LuxCoreRender; Mitsuba; pbrt; appleseed

name: Real-time rasterized rendering
definition: Given scene data and shaders, draw frames on a graphics processor at interactive rates.
inputs: meshes, textures, shader programs, scene graph
outputs: frames at interactive rates
benchmark_note: frame time and image error against path-traced references on fixed scenes
state_of_art: Unreal Engine renderer; Unity HDRP; NVIDIA RTX path

name: Fluid, particle and destruction effects
definition: Given emitters, colliders and solver settings, simulate smoke, fire, liquids, particles and fracture for visual effects.
inputs: scene geometry, emitters, forces, solver parameters
outputs: cached simulations (VDB volumes, particle and mesh sequences)
benchmark_note: solver speed and stability are measurable; visual plausibility is judged
state_of_art: SideFX Houdini; JangaFX EmberGen; Autodesk Bifrost

name: Crowd simulation
definition: Given agent behaviors and an environment, simulate and animate large numbers of characters moving as a crowd.
inputs: agent rules, motion clips, environment layout
outputs: animated crowd caches
benchmark_note: collision counts and trajectory error against recorded crowds are measurable
state_of_art: Massive; Golaem; Houdini crowds

name: Image-based novel view synthesis
definition: Given photographs or video of a real scene, reconstruct a renderable representation and synthesize views from new camera positions.
inputs: multi-view images, camera poses
outputs: radiance field or Gaussian splat scene, rendered novel views
benchmark_note: PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS on held-out views of Mip-NeRF 360 and Tanks and Temples
state_of_art: Luma AI; Polycam; Postshot

name: Audio recording, editing and mixing
definition: Given recorded or synthesized sound, edit, process, sequence, mix and master it into finished audio.

name: Multitrack recording and mixing
definition: Given live inputs and audio tracks, record, arrange, apply effects and balance them to a stereo or surround mix.
inputs: audio inputs and tracks, plug-in effects, automation
outputs: multitrack session, mixed stems and master
benchmark_note: automatic mixing can be compared with reference mixes on multitrack datasets, but mix quality is judged by listeners
state_of_art: Avid Pro Tools; Apple Logic Pro; Ableton Live; Steinberg Cubase

name: Waveform editing and audio restoration
definition: Given a recording, cut, splice and remove noise, clicks, hum and clipping to produce a clean edited file.
inputs: audio files, noise profiles, edit points
outputs: edited and restored audio
benchmark_note: speech and audio enhancement are scored on VoiceBank-DEMAND and the DNS Challenge with PESQ and DNSMOS
state_of_art: iZotope RX; Adobe Audition; Steinberg SpectraLayers

name: Mastering and loudness normalization
definition: Given a final mix, apply equalization, dynamics and limiting and measure loudness to meet a delivery specification.
inputs: stereo or multichannel mix, target loudness and true-peak limits
outputs: mastered audio, loudness report
benchmark_note: loudness meters are tested against EBU Tech 3341 signals; automatic mastering can be scored against reference masters
state_of_art: iZotope Ozone; LANDR; Steinberg WaveLab

name: Sound synthesis and virtual instruments
definition: Given note events and a patch, generate instrument sound by synthesis or sample playback.
inputs: MIDI or note events, synthesis patches, sample libraries
outputs: audio signal, instrument presets
benchmark_note: synthesizer sound matching and neural timbre models have datasets (NSynth), but instrument quality is judged
state_of_art: Native Instruments Kontakt; Xfer Serum; Spectrasonics Omnisphere
open_tools: ZynAddSubFX; Surge XT; Pure Data; SuperCollider; Csound

name: MIDI sequencing and pattern tracking
definition: Given musical ideas, enter and edit note, drum and controller events on a piano roll, step grid or tracker and play them through instruments.
inputs: note and controller events, tempo map, instrument assignments
outputs: MIDI sequences or tracker modules
benchmark_note: editing environment with no defined correct output
state_of_art: Ableton Live; Image-Line FL Studio; Renoise

name: Music source separation
definition: Given a mixed recording, estimate the separate stems such as vocals, drums and bass.
inputs: mixed audio
outputs: separated stem audio
benchmark_note: signal-to-distortion ratio on MUSDB18
state_of_art: iZotope RX Music Rebalance; AudioShake; LALAL.AI

name: Music and sound generation from text
definition: Given a text description and optional melody or audio prompt, synthesize music or sound effects.
inputs: text prompt, optional melody, audio or duration
outputs: generated audio
benchmark_note: Frechet Audio Distance and text-audio similarity on MusicCaps and AudioCaps, with listening tests
state_of_art: Suno; Udio; ElevenLabs Sound Effects

name: Music notation and composition
definition: Given musical ideas, audio or printed scores, produce, recognize, analyze or generate symbolic music.

name: Score notation and engraving
definition: Given musical content entered by hand, MIDI or import, lay out and engrave a printed score and parts.
inputs: note entry, MIDI or MusicXML, instrumentation, layout settings
outputs: engraved scores and parts (PDF, MusicXML)
benchmark_note: MIDI-to-score conversion is measurable against reference scores; engraving quality is judged
state_of_art: Avid Sibelius; Steinberg Dorico; MuseScore Studio

name: Fretted-instrument tablature editing
definition: Given a melody or part for a fretted instrument, write and play back tablature with string and fret positions.
inputs: notes or audio, instrument tuning
outputs: tablature files and playback
benchmark_note: automatic tablature transcription and fingering are scored on GuitarSet
state_of_art: Guitar Pro; Songsterr

name: Optical music recognition
definition: Given an image of printed or handwritten music, recognize the symbols and output an editable score.
inputs: score images or PDFs
outputs: MusicXML or MEI score
benchmark_note: symbol detection and end-to-end recognition are scored on DeepScores and MUSCIMA++
state_of_art: Neuratron PhotoScore; Newzik; ScanScore

name: Automatic music transcription
definition: Given audio of a performance, detect pitches, onsets and durations and output notes or a score.
inputs: audio recordings
outputs: MIDI notes or notated score
benchmark_note: note-level F1 on MAESTRO and MAPS
state_of_art: Melodyne; AnthemScore; Klangio

name: Accompaniment and algorithmic composition
definition: Given a chord progression, style or seed melody, generate accompaniment parts or new symbolic music.
inputs: chords, style, seed melody, rules
outputs: generated MIDI or notation
benchmark_note: symbolic generation is scored by likelihood and style metrics on Lakh MIDI, with listening tests
state_of_art: PG Music Band-in-a-Box; Orb Producer Suite; Scaler

name: Harmony and music theory analysis
definition: Given a score or chord sequence, label keys, chords, functions, voice-leading errors or tone-row forms.
inputs: symbolic score, chord sequence or tone row
outputs: harmonic labels, error reports, row matrices
benchmark_note: functional harmony and chord recognition are scored on BPS-FH and MIREX chord sets
state_of_art: Hookpad; Chordify

name: Game engines and interactive media
definition: Given assets, rules and scripts, assemble and run interactive experiences such as games, interactive stories and virtual tours.

name: Game engine scene and level authoring
definition: Given models, textures, audio and scripts, assemble levels, behaviors and physics in an engine and build a runnable game or real-time experience.
inputs: 3D and 2D assets, scripts, level layouts, target platforms
outputs: playable builds for target platforms
benchmark_note: frame time and build size on fixed sample projects are measurable; game quality is not
state_of_art: Unreal Engine; Unity

name: Interactive narrative and multimedia authoring
definition: Given text, media and branching logic, author a hypermedia piece or branching story without general-purpose programming.
inputs: story text, media assets, branching rules, variables
outputs: playable interactive story or multimedia title
benchmark_note: story-graph consistency checks are automatic; narrative quality is judged
state_of_art: articy:draft; Ren'Py; Yarn Spinner

name: Interactive game audio integration
definition: Given sound assets and game events, define adaptive playback, mixing and spatialization rules that run inside the game.
inputs: sound assets, game parameters and events
outputs: runtime sound banks and event mappings
benchmark_note: integration tooling with no defined correct output
state_of_art: Audiokinetic Wwise; FMOD Studio

name: Panoramic virtual tours
definition: Given stitched panoramas and floor plans, link them with hotspots into a navigable 360-degree tour.
inputs: panoramic images, floor plans, hotspot links
outputs: web-viewable 360-degree tour
benchmark_note: authoring and viewing; nothing to score
state_of_art: Matterport; 3DVista; Kuula

name: Procedural game content generation
definition: Given constraints and a style, generate playable levels, maps, items or quests.
inputs: tile sets or grammars, constraints, playability requirements
outputs: generated levels or content
benchmark_note: playability, diversity and constraint satisfaction metrics exist, but no single standard suite
state_of_art: Houdini Engine for games; Unity procedural toolkits

name: Web page creation and content management
definition: Given content and a design, author web pages and sites and manage their content for publication.

name: HTML and CSS page authoring
definition: Given content and a visual design, write or visually edit HTML and CSS to produce standards-conforming web pages.
inputs: text, images, design mockups, style rules
outputs: HTML, CSS and asset files
benchmark_note: screenshot-to-code benchmarks (Design2Code, WebSight) and W3C validator conformance
state_of_art: Adobe Dreamweaver; Webflow; Visual Studio Code

name: Template-based site building
definition: Given a template and content, assemble a website through a visual builder without writing markup.
inputs: site template, pages and content blocks, media
outputs: hosted website
benchmark_note: generated sites can be checked for validity, accessibility and fidelity to a brief
state_of_art: Squarespace; Wix; Webflow; Google Sites

name: Web content management
definition: Given content items, users and workflows, store, edit, approve and publish content to a website through templates.
inputs: content items, templates, roles, approval workflow
outputs: published pages, content repository, revision history
benchmark_note: platform function; performance benchmarks exist but not task correctness
state_of_art: Adobe Experience Manager; WordPress VIP; Contentful; Sitecore

name: Static site generation
definition: Given content files in markup and templates, build a complete static website.
inputs: Markdown or other content files, templates, configuration
outputs: static HTML site
benchmark_note: build correctness and speed on fixed content sets are measurable
state_of_art: Hugo; Astro; Next.js static export

name: Web accessibility evaluation
definition: Given a web page or site, test it against accessibility success criteria and report failures with fixes.
inputs: rendered web pages, DOM, styles
outputs: list of accessibility violations by criterion, suggested fixes
benchmark_note: W3C ACT Rules test cases give expected pass or fail outcomes for each rule
state_of_art: Deque axe DevTools; Siteimprove; WAVE

name: User-interface and experience prototyping
definition: Given product requirements and users, design, prototype and test the screens and flows of a digital interface.

name: Wireframing
definition: Given requirements and content, sketch low-fidelity screen layouts and navigation.
inputs: requirements, content inventory, user flows
outputs: wireframes and flow diagrams
benchmark_note: layout generation from requirements can be compared with reference screens (Rico, RICO-derived sets)
state_of_art: Balsamiq; Figma; Whimsical

name: Visual interface design
definition: Given wireframes and a design system, produce high-fidelity screen designs with components, styles and specifications for developers.
inputs: wireframes, design system components, brand styles
outputs: high-fidelity screens, component libraries, developer specs
benchmark_note: UI generation from text or screenshot is scored on Design2Code-style sets; visual quality is judged
state_of_art: Figma; Sketch; Framer

name: Interactive prototyping
definition: Given screen designs, link them with interactions and transitions into a clickable prototype for review and testing.
inputs: screen designs, interaction rules, transitions
outputs: clickable prototype
benchmark_note: authoring environment with no defined correct output
state_of_art: Figma prototyping; ProtoPie; Axure RP

name: Remote usability testing
definition: Given a prototype or live product and test tasks, run sessions with participants and report task success, time and issues.
inputs: prototype or product, tasks, participant pool
outputs: recordings, task metrics, issue lists
benchmark_note: automated usability issue detection can be scored against expert-labelled sessions; studies themselves are not benchmarks
state_of_art: UserTesting; Maze; Lookback

name: Broadcast, streaming and live production
definition: Given finished and live media, encode, schedule, switch, play out and deliver it to audiences over air, cable or the internet.

name: Video and audio encoding
definition: Given a master file, compress it to one or more delivery codecs and bitrates, or author it to disc.
inputs: mezzanine video and audio, codec and bitrate ladder, packaging format
outputs: encoded renditions, disc images
benchmark_note: rate-distortion (BD-rate with VMAF or PSNR) on standard test sequences
state_of_art: AWS Elemental MediaConvert; Harmonic; Telestream Vantage

name: Live and on-demand streaming delivery
definition: Given encoded media, package it into adaptive streaming formats, protect it and deliver it to players.
inputs: encoded renditions or live feed, DRM keys, manifest settings
outputs: HLS or DASH streams, hosted video players
benchmark_note: startup time, rebuffering and quality under emulated networks are measurable
state_of_art: Brightcove; Mux; AWS Elemental MediaPackage; Wowza

name: Live switching and on-air graphics
definition: Given live camera, replay and graphics sources, switch, mix and overlay them into a program feed in real time.
inputs: live video sources, graphics templates, data feeds
outputs: program output with character-generator graphics
benchmark_note: real-time operator tooling; only latency is measurable
state_of_art: Ross Video XPression; Vizrt Viz Engine; NewTek TriCaster; vMix

name: Playout and radio automation
definition: Given a schedule and media library, play out programs, commercials and music to air automatically with live overrides.
inputs: daily log or playlist, media files, live events
outputs: on-air output, as-run log
benchmark_note: operational automation with no defined correct output beyond schedule adherence
state_of_art: Imagine Communications Versio; Grass Valley iTX; RCS Zetta; WideOrbit Automation for Radio

name: Program, music and commercial scheduling
definition: Given a library, rotation rules and sold spots, build the daily program and music log and the commercial traffic log.
inputs: music or program library with attributes, rotation and separation rules, ad orders
outputs: scheduled music logs, traffic logs, program logs
benchmark_note: rule violations and fill rate of a generated log are countable, so a constraint-satisfaction benchmark could be built
state_of_art: RCS GSelector; MusicMaster; WideOrbit Traffic

name: Newsroom rundown and story management
definition: Given wire copy, assignments and scripts, build and update the running order of a news program and drive prompters and playout from it.
inputs: wire feeds, story scripts, media references, timing
outputs: program rundown, prompter scripts, device control commands
benchmark_note: coordination tooling with no defined correct output
state_of_art: AP ENPS; Avid iNEWS; Dalet Galaxy

name: Media asset management and archive
definition: Given ingested media, index it with technical and descriptive metadata, manage proxies and versions, and retrieve or archive it.
inputs: media files, metadata, rights, storage tiers
outputs: searchable media catalogue, proxies, archived essence
benchmark_note: automatic tagging and shot retrieval are scored on video retrieval sets such as MSR-VTT
state_of_art: Avid MediaCentral; Dalet Flex; Iconik

name: Live show cue control
definition: Given a cue list for a performance, trigger sound, video and lighting cues in sequence during the show.
inputs: cue list, media files, lighting fixtures and patches
outputs: timed audio, video and lighting output
benchmark_note: real-time operator tooling
state_of_art: Figure 53 QLab; ETC Eos; MA Lighting grandMA3

name: Translation, captioning and speech
definition: Given text or speech in one form or language, render it in another: translated text, localized software, captions, transcripts or synthesized speech.
see_also: enterprise.documents; health.clinical_record; govern.legal_practice; learn.assistive_access; learn.scholarly_information; learn.adaptive_practice

name: Machine translation
definition: Given text in a source language, produce text with the same meaning in a target language.
inputs: source text, language pair, optional glossary
outputs: translated text
benchmark_note: WMT shared tasks and FLORES-200 with COMET, chrF and human evaluation
state_of_art: DeepL; Google Translate; large language models
open_tools: OpenNMT; Marian NMT; Argos Translate; Apertium

name: Computer-assisted translation and localization
definition: Given source documents or software strings, segment them and help a translator reuse translation memory and terminology to produce localized files.
inputs: source files or resource strings, translation memories, term bases
outputs: translated files in original format, updated translation memory
benchmark_note: fuzzy-match retrieval and terminology consistency are measurable; overall translator productivity is not
state_of_art: RWS Trados Studio; memoQ; Phrase; Smartling

name: Speech recognition and transcription
definition: Given recorded or live speech, produce a written transcript with speaker turns and timing.
inputs: audio of speech, language, optional vocabulary
outputs: time-aligned transcript
benchmark_note: word error rate on LibriSpeech, Common Voice and the Open ASR Leaderboard
state_of_art: OpenAI Whisper large; Deepgram; Google Chirp; Nuance Dragon; Nuance Dragon Professional; Microsoft Dictate; Google Docs voice typing; Otter.ai
open_tools: Whisper; whisper.cpp; Kaldi; Vosk; NVIDIA NeMo

name: Stenographic realtime transcription
definition: Given chorded keystrokes from a stenotype machine, translate them through a steno dictionary into English text in real time.
inputs: steno keystroke stream, personal steno dictionary
outputs: realtime text feed, edited transcript
benchmark_note: translation accuracy against reference transcripts given steno input is measurable, but public steno corpora are scarce
state_of_art: Stenograph Case CATalyst; Advantage Software Eclipse

name: Caption and subtitle authoring
definition: Given video and a transcript or translation, segment, time and position caption text and export it in a delivery format.
inputs: video, transcript or translation, style rules
outputs: caption files (SCC, WebVTT, TTML, SRT) or burned-in subtitles
benchmark_note: segmentation and timing can be scored against reference subtitles (SubER metric) on sets such as MuST-Cinema
state_of_art: Ooona; EZTitles; Rev; Verbit

name: Text-to-speech synthesis
definition: Given text and a voice, produce natural-sounding speech audio.
inputs: text or SSML, voice model, prosody controls
outputs: speech audio
benchmark_note: MOS listening tests (Blizzard Challenge) plus automatic intelligibility via ASR word error rate and UTMOS
state_of_art: ElevenLabs; Microsoft Azure Neural TTS; Google Cloud Text-to-Speech
open_tools: Piper; Coqui TTS; eSpeak NG; Festival

name: Optical character recognition
definition: Given a scanned or photographed page, locate and recognize the text and output it with layout.
inputs: page images or image-only PDFs, language
outputs: text with coordinates, searchable PDF, structured layout
benchmark_note: character and word error rate on ICDAR competition sets and OmniDocBench
state_of_art: ABBYY FineReader; Google Document AI; Azure AI Document Intelligence

name: Social media and public communication
definition: Given content and an audience, publish it to social, video and syndication channels and monitor coverage and audience response.

name: Social network publishing and scheduling
definition: Given posts and media, publish or schedule them across social networks and manage replies from one place.
inputs: post text, images and video, channel accounts, schedule
outputs: published posts, engagement queue
benchmark_note: publishing tool; engagement outcomes depend on the audience, not the software
state_of_art: Hootsuite; Sprout Social; Buffer

name: Online video channel publishing
definition: Given finished videos and metadata, upload, describe and organize them on a video-sharing channel for public viewing.
inputs: video files, titles, descriptions, thumbnails, captions
outputs: published videos and playlists
benchmark_note: platform function
state_of_art: YouTube Studio; Vimeo; TikTok

name: Blog and podcast syndication
definition: Given posts or audio episodes, publish them with feeds so subscribers and directories receive new items.
inputs: posts or episode audio, show metadata
outputs: published entries and RSS or Atom feeds
benchmark_note: feed validity is checkable; nothing else is
state_of_art: Substack; WordPress.com; Spotify for Creators; Buzzsprout

name: Media monitoring and media relations
definition: Given topics and outlets, track news and social coverage, classify its sentiment and reach, and manage journalist contacts and press releases.
inputs: keywords and entities, news and social feeds, media contact lists
outputs: coverage reports, sentiment and share-of-voice measures, distribution lists
benchmark_note: topic classification, stance and sentiment are scored on SemEval tasks; coverage completeness is not
state_of_art: Cision; Meltwater; Muck Rack; Brandwatch

name: Audience measurement and analytics
definition: Given ratings panels or platform data, estimate audience size, reach and engagement for programs and posts.
inputs: panel or platform viewing and engagement data, schedules
outputs: ratings, reach and engagement reports
benchmark_note: audience estimates can be compared with census data where it exists
state_of_art: Nielsen; Comscore; YouTube Analytics

name: Build and run computing itself
definition: The capabilities software and IT work depend on: programming languages and tools, embedded toolchains, data management, operating systems and cloud, networks, security, and IT service operations.

name: Programming languages and compilers
definition: Given source code in a programming language, translate it into executable form and run it with the semantics the language defines.

name: Ahead-of-time native compilation
definition: Given source in a compiled systems language, produce optimized machine code for a target processor that preserves program semantics.
inputs: source code, target architecture, optimization settings
outputs: object code, executables, diagnostics
benchmark_note: SPEC CPU and LLVM test-suite measure generated-code speed; Csmith-style random programs test correctness
state_of_art: GCC; Clang/LLVM; Microsoft Visual C++; Intel oneAPI DPC++/C++ Compiler; rustc
open_tools: GCC; LLVM/Clang; rustc; Go toolchain; GNAT; GnuCOBOL

name: Managed bytecode runtimes
definition: Given programs compiled to a portable bytecode, execute them with just-in-time compilation, garbage collection and runtime type safety.
inputs: bytecode or intermediate language, runtime configuration
outputs: running program, throughput and pause-time profile
benchmark_note: DaCapo, Renaissance and SPECjbb measure JIT and garbage-collector performance
state_of_art: Oracle HotSpot JVM; GraalVM; Microsoft .NET runtime; Azul Zing
open_tools: OpenJDK; .NET runtime; Eclipse OpenJ9; GraalVM Community Edition

name: Dynamic language interpreters
definition: Given source in a dynamically typed scripting language, parse and execute it interactively or as a program.
inputs: script source, libraries, interpreter options
outputs: program output, runtime errors
benchmark_note: pyperformance, JetStream and similar suites measure interpreter speed; conformance suites such as test262 check semantics
state_of_art: CPython; PyPy; V8; Node.js; Ruby (MRI/YJIT)
open_tools: CPython; PyPy; V8; SpiderMonkey; LuaJIT; SWI-Prolog; Racket

name: Parallel and accelerator programming
definition: Given a computation, express it for multicore, distributed-memory or GPU execution and generate efficient parallel code.
inputs: sequential or annotated source, target hardware
outputs: parallel kernels or programs, scaling and throughput figures
benchmark_note: NAS Parallel Benchmarks and KernelBench give reference kernels with correctness checks and speed targets
state_of_art: NVIDIA CUDA; Intel oneAPI; AMD ROCm/HIP
open_tools: OpenMP (GCC, LLVM); Open MPI; MPICH; OpenAI Triton; Kokkos; Charm++

name: Interface definition and code generation
definition: Given an interface or schema definition, generate client, server and serialization code in one or more languages.
inputs: interface definition (IDL, protocol schema, WSDL)
outputs: generated stubs, serializers and type definitions
benchmark_note: conformance suites (for example the Protocol Buffers conformance tests) check generated code, but quality beyond correctness is hard to score
state_of_art: Protocol Buffers compiler; Apache Thrift; OpenAPI Generator
open_tools: Protocol Buffers; Apache Thrift; OpenAPI Generator; Apache Avro

name: Source-to-source translation and migration
definition: Given a program in one language or platform version, produce an equivalent program in another.
inputs: legacy source code, target language or platform
outputs: translated source, equivalence test results
benchmark_note: parallel corpora with unit tests (CodeXGLUE code-to-code, TransCoder test sets) score functional equivalence
state_of_art: IBM watsonx Code Assistant for Z; Micro Focus (OpenText) Enterprise Analyzer; AWS Mainframe Modernization

name: Software development tooling
definition: Given a codebase and a change to make, provide the editing, generation, versioning, review, build and delivery machinery that turns the change into a released artifact.

name: Code editing and refactoring
definition: Given a codebase, let a developer navigate, edit and apply semantics-preserving refactorings with language-aware assistance.
inputs: source tree, language server or index
outputs: edited source, refactoring diffs
benchmark_note: automated refactorings can be checked for behavior preservation with tests, but editor productivity is not directly scorable
state_of_art: JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA; Visual Studio; Visual Studio Code; Xcode
open_tools: Eclipse IDE; Code - OSS (VS Code); Vim; GNU Emacs; JupyterLab; clangd; rust-analyzer

name: Code generation from natural language
definition: Given a natural-language task and a codebase or function signature, produce a code change that makes the specified tests pass.
inputs: task description, repository or signature, tests
outputs: patch or function body
benchmark_note: HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench score generated code against hidden tests
state_of_art: Claude Code; GitHub Copilot; OpenAI Codex; Cursor

name: Version control and merging
definition: Given a sequence of edits by many authors, record history, branch, and merge concurrent changes with conflict detection.
inputs: working tree changes, branches
outputs: commit history, merged trees, conflict reports
benchmark_note: historical merge commits give ground-truth resolutions to score automatic merge-conflict resolution
state_of_art: Git; Perforce Helix Core; Plastic SCM (Unity Version Control)

name: Code hosting and review
definition: Given proposed changes to a shared repository, host them, run review discussion and gate merges on approvals and checks.
inputs: repositories, pull or merge requests
outputs: review comments, approvals, merged changes
benchmark_note: datasets of real review comments (for example Microsoft CodeReviewer) score automated review, but review value is partly subjective
state_of_art: GitHub; GitLab; Atlassian Bitbucket; Gerrit
open_tools: GitLab Community Edition; Gitea; Forgejo; Gerrit

name: Build automation and dependency management
definition: Given source, build scripts and declared dependencies, resolve versions, fetch packages and produce build artifacts incrementally and reproducibly.
inputs: source, build files, dependency manifests, package repositories
outputs: binaries, packages, lock files
benchmark_note: build time, incremental rebuild cost and bit-for-bit reproducibility are measurable, but no shared suite exists
state_of_art: Bazel; Gradle; JFrog Artifactory; Sonatype Nexus Repository
open_tools: Apache Maven; Gradle; Bazel; CMake; Ninja; pip/uv; Sonatype Nexus Repository OSS

name: Continuous integration and delivery
definition: Given commits to a repository, automatically build, test and promote them through environments to release.
inputs: repository events, pipeline definitions, environments
outputs: build and test results, deployed releases
benchmark_note: pipeline latency and flaky-test handling can be measured on fixed repositories, but no standard suite exists
state_of_art: GitHub Actions; GitLab CI/CD; Jenkins; CircleCI; Argo CD
open_tools: Jenkins; Tekton; Argo CD; Flux; Woodpecker CI

name: Issue and defect tracking
definition: Given bug reports and work items, record, deduplicate, triage and track them to resolution.
inputs: reports, work items, triage rules
outputs: prioritized backlog, assignment, status history
benchmark_note: public bug trackers give ground truth for duplicate detection and triage assignment; the workflow itself is not scorable
state_of_art: Atlassian Jira; Linear; GitHub Issues

name: API documentation generation
definition: Given annotated source code, extract and render reference documentation for its interfaces.
inputs: source with doc comments
outputs: browsable API reference
benchmark_note: code-summarization datasets (CodeSearchNet) score generated descriptions, extraction itself is deterministic
state_of_art: Doxygen; Sphinx; Javadoc

name: Software testing and verification
definition: Given a program and its specification or tests, find defects, show the absence of classes of defects, or locate their cause.

name: Unit test authoring and execution
definition: Given a unit of code, write and run tests that check its behavior and measure coverage and fault detection.
inputs: source code, specification or existing tests
outputs: test cases, pass/fail results, coverage and mutation scores
benchmark_note: Defects4J and TestGenEval score generated tests by coverage and by real faults detected
state_of_art: JUnit; pytest; Diffblue Cover; Parasoft Jtest
open_tools: JUnit; pytest; Jest; GoogleTest; EvoSuite; Randoop; PIT

name: User interface test automation
definition: Given a web, desktop or mobile application, drive its user interface through scripted scenarios and check expected states.
inputs: application under test, test scripts or scenarios
outputs: pass/fail results, screenshots, traces
benchmark_note: suites of instrumented apps with seeded faults can score fault detection, but scenarios are application-specific
state_of_art: Playwright; Selenium; Tricentis Tosca; OpenText UFT One
open_tools: Selenium; Playwright; Appium; Cypress; Robot Framework

name: Service interface testing
definition: Given an API specification and a running service, generate and send requests and check responses against the specification.
inputs: API specification (OpenAPI, WSDL), service endpoint
outputs: request sequences, failures, coverage
benchmark_note: open REST services with known faults (the EvoMaster benchmark corpus) score coverage and faults found
state_of_art: Postman; Parasoft SOAtest; ReadyAPI
open_tools: REST Assured; Schemathesis; EvoMaster; RESTler; Karate

name: Load and performance testing
definition: Given a system and a workload model, generate concurrent load and measure throughput, latency and failure points.
inputs: workload profile, target system
outputs: throughput, latency percentiles, saturation point
benchmark_note: generator accuracy can be checked against a reference service, but the target system is the variable
state_of_art: OpenText LoadRunner; Gatling Enterprise; k6 Cloud

name: Static code analysis
definition: Given source code, find defects and rule violations without executing it.
inputs: source code, rule set
outputs: findings with locations, severities and traces
benchmark_note: the NIST Juliet test suite and OWASP Benchmark have labeled true and false positives
state_of_art: Coverity; CodeQL; SonarQube; Fortify Static Code Analyzer
open_tools: Clang Static Analyzer; Infer; Semgrep; SpotBugs; cppcheck; SonarQube Community Build

name: Formal software verification
definition: Given a program and a formal specification, prove that the program meets it or produce a counterexample.
inputs: program, specification or assertions
outputs: proof, verified properties, counterexample trace
benchmark_note: SV-COMP publishes verification tasks with known verdicts
state_of_art: Atelier B; AbsInt Astrée; TrustInSoft Analyzer
open_tools: CBMC; Frama-C; Dafny; TLA+ tools; Coq (Rocq); Isabelle; Kani

name: Debugging and fault localization
definition: Given a failing program and a failure, locate the faulty code and, where possible, propose a repair.
inputs: program, failing input or test, execution
outputs: suspicious locations, root cause, candidate patch
benchmark_note: Defects4J and BugsInPy give real bugs with developer fixes to score localization and repair
state_of_art: Visual Studio debugger; WinDbg; Undo LiveRecorder

name: Performance and memory profiling
definition: Given a running program, attribute time, memory and resource use to code locations and detect leaks.
inputs: instrumented or sampled execution
outputs: profiles, hot paths, leak reports
benchmark_note: programs with planted hot spots and leaks can score attribution accuracy, but no standard suite exists
state_of_art: Intel VTune Profiler; YourKit; JProfiler; Datadog Continuous Profiler

name: Requirements and software architecture
definition: Given stakeholder needs, produce traceable requirements, design models and architecture descriptions, and estimate the effort to build them.

name: Requirements capture and traceability
definition: Given stakeholder statements and design artifacts, record requirements, classify them and maintain trace links to design and tests.
inputs: stakeholder statements, documents, existing artifacts
outputs: requirement set, trace matrix, change impact
benchmark_note: the PROMISE NFR dataset and trace-link recovery datasets score classification and tracing
state_of_art: IBM DOORS Next; Jama Connect; Polarion Requirements

name: Software design modeling
definition: Given requirements, build structural and behavioral models (classes, components, states, sequences) and generate or check code against them.
inputs: requirements, domain concepts
outputs: UML or similar models, generated code skeletons
benchmark_note: model-to-code consistency can be checked, but design quality is judged, not computed
state_of_art: Sparx Enterprise Architect; IBM Rhapsody; MagicDraw (Cameo)

name: Architecture description and analysis
definition: Given a system's components and connectors, describe its architecture and analyze qualities such as dependency structure and performance.
inputs: component and connector descriptions, quality scenarios
outputs: architecture views, analysis results
benchmark_note: architecture quality has no agreed ground truth beyond specific metrics
state_of_art: Sparx Enterprise Architect; Structurizr; Lattix

name: Software effort estimation
definition: Given the size and characteristics of a planned software project, estimate effort, duration and staffing.
inputs: size measures (function points, lines of code), project factors
outputs: effort and schedule estimates with uncertainty
benchmark_note: PROMISE and ISBSG project datasets with actual effort allow error scoring
state_of_art: QSM SLIM; Galorath SEER-SEM; Galorath SEER; PRICE TruePlanning

name: Embedded and real-time toolchains
definition: Given firmware for a microcontroller, signal processor or real-time computer, compile, configure, load, debug and verify it on the target hardware.

name: Cross-compilation for embedded targets
definition: Given firmware source and a microcontroller or DSP target, produce a size- and speed-optimized image that fits the target's memory map.
inputs: C, C++ or assembly source, linker script, target device
outputs: firmware image, memory map, size report
benchmark_note: Embench and EEMBC CoreMark measure code size and speed on fixed reference programs
state_of_art: IAR Embedded Workbench; Arm Keil MDK; Green Hills MULTI; Arm Compiler for Embedded
open_tools: GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain (GCC); LLVM/Clang; SDCC; PlatformIO

name: Real-time operating system configuration
definition: Given tasks with priorities and deadlines, configure and run a real-time kernel that schedules them deterministically.
inputs: task set, timing requirements, board support package
outputs: configured kernel image, scheduling and latency behavior
benchmark_note: Thread-Metric and interrupt-latency tests give comparable kernel timings on a fixed board
state_of_art: Wind River VxWorks; QNX Neutrino; Green Hills INTEGRITY; SafeRTOS
open_tools: FreeRTOS; Zephyr; Apache NuttX; RTEMS; Eclipse ThreadX

name: On-target debugging and trace
definition: Given a running embedded target, halt, step, inspect memory and registers, and capture execution trace through a debug probe.
inputs: target board, debug probe, symbol files
outputs: breakpoints, register and memory views, trace logs
benchmark_note: tool quality depends on hardware support and workflow, not a scorable output
state_of_art: Lauterbach TRACE32; SEGGER J-Link and Ozone; Arm Development Studio

name: Model-based embedded code generation
definition: Given a block diagram or state-machine model of controller behavior, generate production embedded code equivalent to the model.
inputs: controller model, target and data-type settings
outputs: embedded C code, equivalence test results
benchmark_note: back-to-back testing of model against generated code checks equivalence; code efficiency is measurable per target
state_of_art: MathWorks Embedded Coder; dSPACE TargetLink; Ansys SCADE Suite

name: Embedded unit and hardware-in-the-loop testing
definition: Given firmware and a simulated or real plant and bus environment, run unit, integration and hardware-in-the-loop tests and report coverage.
inputs: firmware, test cases, plant or bus simulation
outputs: test results, structural coverage, bus traces
benchmark_note: coverage on reference firmware is measurable; hardware-in-the-loop setups are rig-specific
state_of_art: VectorCAST; LDRA tool suite; dSPACE SCALEXIO; Vector CANoe

name: Embedded coding-standard and runtime-error verification
definition: Given embedded C or C++ source, check compliance with coding standards such as MISRA and prove the absence of runtime errors.
inputs: embedded source, coding standard, target configuration
outputs: violations, proven-safe and unproven operations
benchmark_note: the Juliet suite and SV-COMP embedded tasks give labeled defects
state_of_art: MathWorks Polyspace; AbsInt Astrée; LDRA TBvision; Perforce Helix QAC

name: Embedded Linux image building
definition: Given a board definition and package selection, build a bootable root file system, kernel and bootloader for an embedded processor.
inputs: board support layers, package recipes, configuration
outputs: bootable image, software bill of materials
benchmark_note: build time and bit-for-bit reproducibility are measurable
state_of_art: Wind River Linux; Siemens Embedded (Mentor) Linux

name: Application frameworks and servers
definition: Given application logic, provide the frameworks, runtimes and servers that turn it into a web, mobile or desktop application serving users.

name: Server-side web frameworks
definition: Given routes, data models and business logic, handle HTTP requests and render responses or API payloads.
inputs: application code, routes, templates, data models
outputs: running web application or API
benchmark_note: TechEmpower Framework Benchmarks measure throughput on fixed request types; app-generation benchmarks score functional correctness
state_of_art: Spring Boot; ASP.NET Core; Django; Ruby on Rails; Express
open_tools: Django; Ruby on Rails; Spring Boot; Express; FastAPI; Laravel

name: Browser user-interface frameworks
definition: Given component definitions and application state, render and update an interactive user interface in the browser.
inputs: components, state, events
outputs: rendered and reactive DOM
benchmark_note: js-framework-benchmark measures render and update cost on fixed operations
state_of_art: React; Angular; Vue.js; Svelte

name: Web browser engines
definition: Given HTML, CSS and JavaScript from the web, fetch, lay out, render and execute the page securely.
inputs: web resources (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, media)
outputs: rendered interactive page
benchmark_note: Web Platform Tests score standards conformance; Speedometer and JetStream score speed
state_of_art: Chromium/Blink; WebKit; Gecko

name: Mobile application frameworks
definition: Given app logic and screens, build a native or cross-platform app for phone and tablet operating systems.
inputs: app code, UI definitions, device capabilities
outputs: installable mobile app
benchmark_note: startup time, frame rate and size are measurable on fixed apps
state_of_art: SwiftUI and Xcode; Jetpack Compose and Android Studio; Flutter
open_tools: Flutter; React Native; Apache Cordova; Kotlin Multiplatform

name: Desktop graphical interface construction
definition: Given a layout and event handlers, build a native desktop user interface, by hand or in a visual builder.
inputs: layout definitions, event handlers
outputs: desktop application windows and controls
benchmark_note: screenshot-to-code benchmarks (Design2Code) score generated interfaces; builder usability is not scorable
state_of_art: Qt; Windows Presentation Foundation and WinUI; Electron
open_tools: Qt; GTK; wxWidgets; Lazarus; Avalonia; Tauri

name: Low-code application building
definition: Given forms, tables and workflow rules defined visually, generate a working data-entry application without conventional programming.
inputs: data model, forms, rules
outputs: deployed business application
benchmark_note: output quality depends on the application specified, with no shared reference tasks
state_of_art: Microsoft Power Apps; OutSystems; Mendix; Oracle APEX
open_tools: Budibase; Appsmith; Oracle APEX (free to use, not open)

name: Web service and remote call interfaces
definition: Given service operations, expose and call them across processes or machines through REST, GraphQL, RPC or distributed-object protocols.
inputs: service contract, endpoints
outputs: callable remote interfaces, client libraries
benchmark_note: latency and throughput suites exist per protocol; interface design quality is not scorable
state_of_art: gRPC; Apollo GraphQL; Kong Gateway
open_tools: gRPC; Apache Thrift; GraphQL reference implementation; omniORB

name: HTTP serving and reverse proxying
definition: Given web content and upstream services, accept HTTP connections, serve static content, terminate TLS and proxy requests.
inputs: site content, virtual host and proxy configuration
outputs: HTTP responses, access logs
benchmark_note: h2spec checks protocol conformance; wrk-style load tests measure throughput and tail latency
state_of_art: nginx; Apache HTTP Server; Microsoft IIS; Envoy
open_tools: nginx; Apache HTTP Server; Caddy; HAProxy; Envoy

name: Application and transaction servers
definition: Given deployed application components, host them with managed transactions, connection pools, security and clustering.
inputs: deployable application archives, resource configuration
outputs: running managed applications, transaction logs
benchmark_note: SPECjEnterprise and transaction-throughput tests compare servers on a fixed application
state_of_art: IBM CICS; Oracle WebLogic; IBM WebSphere Liberty; Red Hat JBoss EAP
open_tools: Apache Tomcat; WildFly; Open Liberty; Payara; Apache TomEE

name: Database management and query
definition: Given data and queries in a declared model (relational, document, graph, text, vector), store the data durably and answer the queries correctly and fast.

name: Transactional relational processing
definition: Given a relational schema and concurrent SQL transactions, execute them with ACID guarantees and recover after failure.
inputs: schema, SQL transactions, isolation level
outputs: committed state, query results, recovery logs
benchmark_note: TPC-C measures transaction throughput; sqllogictest and Jepsen check correctness and isolation
state_of_art: Oracle Database; Microsoft SQL Server; IBM Db2; Amazon Aurora
open_tools: PostgreSQL; MySQL; MariaDB; SQLite; CockroachDB; YugabyteDB

name: Analytical query processing
definition: Given large fact and dimension tables and analytical SQL, execute scans, joins and aggregations over columnar or massively parallel storage.
inputs: warehouse tables, analytical SQL
outputs: query results, execution plans
benchmark_note: TPC-H, TPC-DS, ClickBench and the Join Order Benchmark give fixed queries and data at known scales
state_of_art: Snowflake; Google BigQuery; Amazon Redshift; Teradata Vantage; Databricks SQL
open_tools: DuckDB; ClickHouse; Apache Doris; Trino; Apache Druid

name: Key-value, document and wide-column storage
definition: Given records addressed by key or document, store and retrieve them at scale with partitioning, replication and tunable consistency.
inputs: records or documents, access patterns, consistency settings
outputs: reads and writes with latency and consistency guarantees
benchmark_note: YCSB defines standard workloads; Jepsen tests consistency claims
state_of_art: Amazon DynamoDB; MongoDB Atlas; Redis Enterprise; Azure Cosmos DB
open_tools: Apache Cassandra; MongoDB Community Server; Valkey; Apache HBase; ScyllaDB; FoundationDB

name: Graph database query
definition: Given a property graph or RDF data, answer pattern-matching and traversal queries.
inputs: nodes, edges, properties; Cypher, GQL or SPARQL queries
outputs: matched subgraphs, paths, aggregates
benchmark_note: the LDBC Social Network Benchmark gives audited workloads and reference results
state_of_art: Neo4j; TigerGraph; Amazon Neptune
open_tools: Neo4j Community Edition; JanusGraph; Apache AGE; Apache Jena; Memgraph

name: Full-text search indexing
definition: Given a document collection and text queries, build inverted indexes and return ranked matches.
inputs: documents, analyzers, queries
outputs: ranked hits, facets, highlights
benchmark_note: MS MARCO and BEIR score ranking quality; Rally-style suites measure indexing and query speed
state_of_art: Elasticsearch; OpenSearch; Algolia
open_tools: Apache Lucene; Apache Solr; OpenSearch; Tantivy

name: Vector similarity search
definition: Given high-dimensional embeddings and query vectors, return approximate nearest neighbors quickly at a target recall.
inputs: embedding vectors, index parameters, query vectors
outputs: nearest neighbors with distances
benchmark_note: ann-benchmarks and big-ann-benchmarks report recall against queries per second
state_of_art: Pinecone; Milvus (Zilliz Cloud); Elasticsearch kNN

name: Query authoring and text-to-SQL
definition: Given a database schema and a question in natural language or a visual query builder, produce a correct query and its results.
inputs: schema, question or query-builder selections
outputs: SQL query, result set
benchmark_note: Spider and BIRD score text-to-SQL by execution accuracy
state_of_art: DataGrip; Toad; Snowflake Cortex Analyst

name: Database administration and tuning
definition: Given a running database and its workload, choose indexes, configuration and query plans that meet performance targets and keep the instance healthy.
inputs: workload traces, schema, configuration
outputs: index and configuration recommendations, health alerts
benchmark_note: index and knob tuners can be scored on TPC-H and Join Order Benchmark workloads, as in published tuning studies
state_of_art: Oracle Autonomous Database; SolarWinds Database Performance Analyzer; OtterTune (defunct)

name: Desktop and end-user databases
definition: Given a small data model defined by a non-programmer, create tables, forms, queries and reports in a single-file or hosted database.
inputs: tables, forms, simple queries
outputs: working database with forms and reports
benchmark_note: value depends on the user's application; there is no reference task set
state_of_art: Microsoft Access; Claris FileMaker; Airtable; Quickbase; Smartsheet; Microsoft Power Apps; Notion databases
open_tools: LibreOffice Base; NocoDB; Baserow; Budibase; Appsmith

name: Data integration and pipelines
definition: Given data spread across systems and formats, move, transform, reconcile and describe it so that downstream systems can use it.

name: Extract, transform and load
definition: Given source systems and target schemas, extract records, apply transformations and quality rules, and load the target incrementally.
inputs: source connections, mappings, transformation rules
outputs: loaded target tables, rejected records, run logs
benchmark_note: TPC-DI defines a reference data-integration workload with validation
state_of_art: Informatica PowerCenter and IDMC; Fivetran; Azure Data Factory; IBM DataStage
open_tools: Apache Hop; Airbyte; dbt Core; Apache NiFi; Singer

name: Data pipeline orchestration
definition: Given a graph of dependent jobs and their schedules, run them in order, retry failures and record lineage of each run.
inputs: job definitions, dependencies, schedules
outputs: executed runs, status, retries, run history
benchmark_note: scheduler overhead and failure recovery can be measured on synthetic DAGs; no standard suite
state_of_art: Apache Airflow (Astronomer); BMC Control-M; Dagster+; Prefect Cloud
open_tools: Apache Airflow; Dagster; Prefect; Argo Workflows; Luigi

name: Distributed batch processing
definition: Given a large dataset and a data-parallel program, partition and execute it across a cluster with fault tolerance.
inputs: distributed datasets, map-reduce or dataflow program
outputs: transformed datasets, job metrics
benchmark_note: TPC-DS on Spark, TeraSort and HiBench give fixed workloads with known outputs
state_of_art: Databricks; Amazon EMR; Google Dataproc
open_tools: Apache Spark; Apache Hadoop; Apache Flink (batch); Dask; Ray

name: Messaging and stream processing
definition: Given continuous event streams, deliver them reliably between producers and consumers and compute windowed results with bounded latency.
inputs: event streams, topics or queues, streaming queries
outputs: delivered messages, continuous results, lag metrics
benchmark_note: the OpenMessaging Benchmark measures broker throughput and latency; Nexmark gives streaming queries with reference semantics
state_of_art: Confluent Cloud (Kafka); Amazon Kinesis; IBM MQ
open_tools: Apache Kafka; Apache Flink; RabbitMQ; Apache Pulsar; NATS

name: Application integration and service bus
definition: Given applications with different interfaces, route, transform and orchestrate messages between them, including business-to-business document exchange.
inputs: application endpoints, message formats, routing rules
outputs: integrated flows, transformed messages, exchange acknowledgments
benchmark_note: integration value is in fitting specific systems; there are no reference integration tasks
state_of_art: MuleSoft Anypoint; Boomi; IBM App Connect; Microsoft Azure Logic Apps
open_tools: Apache Camel; WSO2 Micro Integrator; Apache ServiceMix

name: Data format transformation and schema mapping
definition: Given data in one structured format or schema, map and convert it to another format or schema.
inputs: source documents or records, source and target schemas
outputs: converted data, mapping specification
benchmark_note: the W3C XSLT and JSON Schema test suites check conformance; schema-matching benchmarks such as Valentine score mappings
state_of_art: Altova MapForce; Saxon-EE

name: Change data capture and replication
definition: Given a source database, capture committed changes and apply them to replicas or downstream systems with ordering and low lag.
inputs: source database logs, target systems
outputs: replicated tables, change event streams
benchmark_note: replication lag and correctness can be measured on fixed write workloads
state_of_art: Oracle GoldenGate; Qlik Replicate; AWS Database Migration Service

name: Master data management and record matching
definition: Given overlapping records about the same entities from several systems, match, merge and publish a single trusted record per entity.
inputs: records from source systems, matching rules
outputs: golden records, match clusters, survivorship decisions
benchmark_note: entity-matching datasets (Abt-Buy, DBLP-ACM, Amazon-Google) give labeled matches
state_of_art: Informatica MDM; Reltio; Tamr; Informatica Customer 360; Salesforce duplicate management

name: Data modeling and metadata management
definition: Given business entities and existing data sources, design logical and physical data models and maintain a catalog of datasets, definitions and lineage.
inputs: entity requirements, source schemas, pipeline definitions
outputs: data models, generated DDL, data dictionary, lineage graph
benchmark_note: model and catalog quality are judged by fit to the organization, not against reference answers
state_of_art: erwin Data Modeler; Collibra; Alation; Atlan

name: Operating systems and virtualization
definition: Given computer hardware, manage processes, memory, devices and users, and present virtual machines or desktops to the software above.

name: General-purpose operating systems
definition: Given hardware and many concurrent programs, schedule processes, manage memory, files and devices, and enforce isolation between users.
inputs: hardware, system configuration, workloads
outputs: running system, scheduling and I/O behavior
benchmark_note: LMbench and the Phoronix Test Suite compare kernels; the Linux Test Project checks behavior
state_of_art: Microsoft Windows; Red Hat Enterprise Linux; Apple macOS and iOS; IBM z/OS
open_tools: Linux; FreeBSD; Android Open Source Project; illumos

name: Command shells and system scripting
definition: Given an administrative goal, express it as shell commands or scripts that the operating system executes.
inputs: goal or task description, system state
outputs: command sequence or script, resulting system state
benchmark_note: NL2Bash and Terminal-Bench score command generation by resulting system state
state_of_art: PowerShell; Bash; zsh
open_tools: Bash; PowerShell; zsh; fish; GNU coreutils

name: Device drivers
definition: Given a hardware device and an operating system's driver model, implement the driver that exposes the device safely to the system.
inputs: device specification, kernel interfaces
outputs: loadable driver, device nodes
benchmark_note: SV-COMP Linux driver verification tasks give defects with known verdicts
state_of_art: Windows Driver Kit; Linux kernel driver framework
open_tools: Linux kernel; Windows Driver Frameworks (open source)

name: Hardware virtualization and emulation
definition: Given a physical host, partition it into isolated virtual machines, or emulate another instruction set, with near-native performance.
inputs: host hardware, guest images, resource allocations
outputs: running virtual machines, migration and performance behavior
benchmark_note: SPECvirt and nested benchmark suites compare hypervisors on fixed workloads
state_of_art: VMware vSphere; Microsoft Hyper-V; Nutanix AHV

name: Desktop and application virtualization
definition: Given centrally hosted desktops or applications, deliver them to remote users' devices with interactive performance.
inputs: hosted desktop images or applications, user sessions
outputs: remote sessions, session performance
benchmark_note: session-density and latency tests exist (Login VSI), but are vendor-run
state_of_art: Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops; Omnissa (VMware) Horizon; Azure Virtual Desktop

name: Cloud infrastructure and automation
definition: Given declared infrastructure and workloads, provision compute, containers and configuration automatically and keep services running across failures.

name: Cloud compute provisioning
definition: Given a request for machines, networks and storage, allocate them on demand from a shared pool and bill for use.
inputs: instance requests, images, quotas
outputs: running virtual machines, networks, volumes, usage records
benchmark_note: provisioning latency and price-performance can be measured (for example with PerfKit Benchmarker)
state_of_art: Amazon Web Services; Microsoft Azure; Google Cloud

name: Container packaging and orchestration
definition: Given containerized services and their resource needs, place, scale, restart and connect them across a cluster.
inputs: container images, deployment manifests, cluster nodes
outputs: scheduled pods or tasks, service endpoints, scaling events
benchmark_note: Kubernetes conformance tests check behavior; scheduler quality can be scored by simulation on public cluster traces
state_of_art: Kubernetes (EKS, GKE, AKS); Red Hat OpenShift; Docker
open_tools: Kubernetes; containerd; Podman; HashiCorp Nomad (source-available); K3s

name: Infrastructure as code
definition: Given a declarative description of desired infrastructure, plan and apply the changes that make the real infrastructure match it.
inputs: infrastructure definitions, provider credentials, current state
outputs: change plan, provisioned resources, state file
benchmark_note: IaC-Eval scores generated infrastructure code against requirements and deployability
state_of_art: HashiCorp Terraform; AWS CloudFormation; Pulumi

name: Host and endpoint configuration management
definition: Given a desired configuration for servers or endpoints, detect drift and bring each machine into compliance.
inputs: configuration policies, inventory of hosts
outputs: applied configurations, drift and compliance reports
benchmark_note: idempotence and convergence time can be checked on reference machine images
state_of_art: Ansible Automation Platform; Puppet Enterprise; Microsoft Intune; Tanium

name: Software packaging, deployment and patching
definition: Given an application or patch, package it and install it on many machines in a controlled, reversible rollout.
inputs: application files, installers, target machine groups
outputs: installed software, rollout status, patch compliance
benchmark_note: success is operational (coverage, failures) with no reference task set
state_of_art: Microsoft Configuration Manager; Ivanti Patch; Flexera InstallShield

name: Cluster workload scheduling
definition: Given a queue of batch jobs with resource requests, allocate cluster nodes to maximize utilization and meet fairness and deadline goals.
inputs: job queue, resource requests, cluster state, policies
outputs: job placements, wait times, utilization
benchmark_note: Parallel Workloads Archive and public cluster traces let schedulers be scored by simulation
state_of_art: Slurm (SchedMD); Altair PBS Professional; IBM Spectrum LSF

name: High-availability clustering and failover
definition: Given a service replicated across nodes, detect failures and move work so the service stays available and consistent.
inputs: replicated service, cluster membership, fencing policies
outputs: failover events, availability and consistency behavior
benchmark_note: Jepsen-style fault injection checks consistency and availability claims
state_of_art: Oracle RAC; Veritas InfoScale; Microsoft Failover Clustering

name: Network operations and communications
definition: Given a network of routers, switches, links and services, configure it, keep names and addresses consistent, observe traffic and carry voice, mail and remote sessions.

name: Routing, switching and traffic engineering
definition: Given a topology and policies, configure routers and switches so traffic reaches its destination with the intended paths, redundancy and quality of service.
inputs: topology, routing policies, device configurations
outputs: forwarding behavior, verified reachability, traffic shaping
benchmark_note: Batfish-style analysis checks configurations against intended reachability; configuration-synthesis tasks can be scored this way
state_of_art: Cisco IOS XE and NX-OS; Juniper Junos; Arista EOS
open_tools: FRRouting; BIRD; Open vSwitch; SONiC; Batfish

name: Address and name management
definition: Given hosts and services, allocate IP addresses and answer name lookups correctly and quickly.
inputs: address plans, zone data, lease policies
outputs: DHCP leases, DNS answers, address inventory
benchmark_note: dnsperf measures resolver and server throughput; DNS conformance tests check answers
state_of_art: Infoblox; BlueCat; Cloudflare DNS
open_tools: BIND; Kea DHCP; PowerDNS; Knot DNS; Unbound; dnsmasq

name: Network availability and performance monitoring
definition: Given network devices and links, poll and collect telemetry, detect outages and degradation, and alert operators.
inputs: device inventory, SNMP or flow telemetry, thresholds
outputs: availability status, utilization graphs, alerts
benchmark_note: alerting can be scored against injected faults in emulated networks; no standard suite
state_of_art: SolarWinds Network Performance Monitor; Cisco ThousandEyes; Kentik
open_tools: Nagios Core; Zabbix; LibreNMS; Icinga; ntopng

name: Packet capture and protocol analysis
definition: Given traffic on a link, capture packets and decode protocol fields and conversations to diagnose problems.
inputs: network interface or capture file, filters
outputs: decoded packets, conversations, protocol statistics
benchmark_note: dissector correctness can be checked against public sample captures; diagnosis is open-ended
state_of_art: Wireshark; NetScout nGeniusONE; Riverbed Packet Analyzer

name: Network modeling and planning
definition: Given a proposed topology, traffic demands and radio or link parameters, simulate network behavior to plan capacity and coverage.
inputs: topology, traffic matrix, link or radio parameters
outputs: predicted throughput, delay, coverage maps
benchmark_note: simulators can be validated against testbed measurements; no single reference suite
state_of_art: Riverbed Modeler (OPNET); Forsk Atoll; Keysight EXata

name: Voice over IP and unified communications
definition: Given users and endpoints, set up, route and bill voice and video calls and messaging over IP networks.
inputs: dial plans, endpoints, trunks
outputs: call sessions, call records, voicemail
benchmark_note: SIPp load tests and SIP conformance tests measure call handling; call quality needs MOS estimation
state_of_art: Cisco Unified Communications Manager; Microsoft Teams Phone; Zoom Phone

name: Mail transfer and messaging servers
definition: Given messages from users and other servers, route, store and deliver mail with authentication and spam handling.
inputs: inbound and outbound mail, domains, policies
outputs: delivered and stored mail, delivery logs
benchmark_note: delivery throughput is measurable; spam filtering is scored on public corpora under content filtering
state_of_art: Microsoft Exchange Online; Google Workspace Gmail

name: Remote terminal and file access
definition: Given a remote host, open an interactive terminal or graphical session, or transfer files, over the network.
inputs: host address, credentials, protocol
outputs: terminal or desktop session, transferred files
benchmark_note: functionality is protocol-defined; differences are usability and security, not scorable outputs
state_of_art: TeamViewer; Microsoft Remote Desktop; Progress MOVEit

name: Identity, access and protection
definition: Given users, devices, data and network boundaries, authenticate who is acting, limit what they can do, and block or encrypt to prevent compromise.

name: Directory services
definition: Given users, groups, devices and policies, store them in a hierarchical directory and answer lookups and policy queries for the network.
inputs: identity records, organizational structure, policies
outputs: directory answers, group memberships, applied policies
benchmark_note: LDAP protocol conformance and lookup throughput are testable
state_of_art: Microsoft Active Directory and Entra ID; Oracle Unified Directory
open_tools: OpenLDAP; FreeIPA; 389 Directory Server; Samba (Active Directory domain controller)

name: Authentication and single sign-on
definition: Given a user's credentials or factors, verify identity and issue tokens or assertions trusted by many applications.
inputs: credentials, authentication factors, relying-party configuration
outputs: authentication decisions, tokens or assertions
benchmark_note: the OpenID Foundation conformance suite checks protocol correctness; security strength is not a single score
state_of_art: Okta; Microsoft Entra ID; Ping Identity

name: Privileged access and identity governance
definition: Given accounts and entitlements across systems, grant, review, vault and revoke access, especially administrative access, according to policy.
inputs: accounts, entitlements, access policies, requests
outputs: provisioned or revoked access, session records, certification reports
benchmark_note: effectiveness depends on organizational policy, with no reference outcomes
state_of_art: CyberArk; SailPoint; BeyondTrust; HashiCorp Vault
open_tools: midPoint; OpenBao; Teleport Community Edition; Bitwarden

name: Firewalls and network segmentation
definition: Given traffic and a rule set, permit or block connections at network and application layers and segment the network.
inputs: packets or flows, firewall rules, zones
outputs: allowed and blocked traffic, rule hit logs
benchmark_note: NetSecOPEN tests measure throughput with security enabled; rule-set anomaly detection can be checked on synthetic policies
state_of_art: Palo Alto Networks NGFW; Fortinet FortiGate; Check Point Quantum
open_tools: nftables; pfSense CE; OPNsense; OpenBSD pf

name: Virtual private networking
definition: Given remote users or sites, establish authenticated, encrypted tunnels across untrusted networks.
inputs: endpoints, keys or certificates, tunnel policies
outputs: encrypted tunnels, connection logs
benchmark_note: tunnel throughput and latency are measurable; protocol security is verified formally rather than benchmarked
state_of_art: Cisco Secure Client; Palo Alto GlobalProtect; Zscaler Private Access
open_tools: WireGuard; OpenVPN; strongSwan; Tailscale client; Headscale

name: Malware detection and endpoint protection
definition: Given files, processes and behavior on an endpoint, detect and block malicious software.
inputs: files, process behavior, signatures or models
outputs: detections, quarantined items, alerts
benchmark_note: EMBER and SOREL-20M give labeled malware sets; AV-TEST and AV-Comparatives run detection tests
state_of_art: CrowdStrike Falcon; Microsoft Defender for Endpoint; SentinelOne

name: Encryption and key management
definition: Given data at rest or in transit and keys, encrypt, sign and verify it, and generate, store and rotate the keys.
inputs: plaintext or ciphertext, keys, algorithms
outputs: ciphertext, signatures, verified data, key lifecycle records
benchmark_note: Project Wycheproof and NIST CAVP test vectors check implementations; throughput is measurable
state_of_art: Thales CipherTrust; AWS Key Management Service; BitLocker

name: Content filtering and data loss prevention
definition: Given web, mail or file traffic, block unwanted content and detect sensitive data leaving the organization.
inputs: traffic or files, content policies, sensitive-data patterns
outputs: blocked items, data-loss alerts
benchmark_note: public spam and phishing corpora score filtering; DLP detection can be scored on synthetic sensitive-data sets
state_of_art: Zscaler Internet Access; Microsoft Purview DLP; Proofpoint

name: Security assessment, detection and response
definition: Given systems and their activity, find weaknesses before attackers do, detect attacks in progress, and investigate what happened.

name: Vulnerability scanning
definition: Given hosts, networks or images, enumerate software and configurations and report known vulnerabilities with severity.
inputs: target addresses or images, credentials, vulnerability feeds
outputs: vulnerability findings, risk scores, remediation advice
benchmark_note: deliberately vulnerable images with known CVEs score detection, but coverage depends on feeds
state_of_art: Tenable Nessus; Qualys VMDR; Rapid7 InsightVM; Wiz

name: Web application security testing
definition: Given a running web application, probe it for injection, authentication and logic flaws and report exploitable findings.
inputs: application URL, credentials, scope
outputs: confirmed vulnerabilities with proof requests
benchmark_note: OWASP Benchmark and WAVSEP give labeled test cases for true and false positives
state_of_art: Burp Suite Professional; Invicti; Checkmarx DAST

name: Penetration testing and exploitation
definition: Given an authorized target environment, discover services, exploit weaknesses and chain them to demonstrate compromise.
inputs: scope, target network, credentials if any
outputs: compromised hosts, attack paths, report
benchmark_note: capture-the-flag suites (Cybench, NYU CTF Bench) give tasks with verifiable flags
state_of_art: Cobalt Strike; Core Impact; Horizon3 NodeZero
open_tools: Metasploit Framework; Nmap; John the Ripper; Hashcat; Impacket

name: Security event monitoring and correlation
definition: Given logs and alerts from many sources, correlate them into detections of attacker techniques and prioritize incidents.
inputs: logs, alerts, detection rules, threat intelligence
outputs: correlated incidents, mapped attacker techniques, triage queue
benchmark_note: Splunk Boss of the SOC datasets and ATT&CK evaluations give labeled attack activity
state_of_art: Splunk Enterprise Security; Microsoft Sentinel; Google Security Operations
open_tools: Wazuh; Security Onion; Sigma rules; Elastic Security (free tier)

name: Network intrusion detection and prevention
definition: Given network traffic, detect and optionally block attacks by signature or anomaly.
inputs: packets or flows, signatures or models
outputs: alerts, blocked sessions
benchmark_note: CIC-IDS2017 and UNSW-NB15 give labeled traffic for scoring detection
state_of_art: Cisco Secure IPS (Snort 3); Palo Alto Threat Prevention; Vectra AI

name: Digital forensics
definition: Given disk images, memory captures or devices, recover and interpret artifacts to reconstruct what happened, preserving evidence integrity.
inputs: forensic images, memory dumps, case questions
outputs: recovered artifacts, timelines, evidence reports
benchmark_note: NIST CFReDS provides reference images with documented artifacts
state_of_art: EnCase Forensic; Exterro FTK; Magnet AXIOM; Cellebrite; OpenText EnCase
open_tools: Autopsy; The Sleuth Kit; Volatility; Plaso

name: Binary reverse engineering
definition: Given a compiled binary, disassemble and decompile it into readable code and recover its structure and behavior.
inputs: executable or firmware binary
outputs: disassembly, decompiled pseudocode, annotated functions
benchmark_note: recompiling decompiled output and testing equivalence against the original gives a correctness score
state_of_art: IDA Pro; Binary Ninja; Ghidra
open_tools: Ghidra; radare2; Rizin and Cutter; angr

name: Storage, backup and recovery
definition: Given data on disks, arrays and cloud stores, organize it into file systems and objects, keep copies, and restore it after loss.

name: Backup, imaging and restore
definition: Given systems and data sets, take scheduled full, incremental or image copies to separate media and restore them on demand.
inputs: source volumes or files, schedules, retention policies
outputs: backup sets, catalogs, restored data
benchmark_note: deduplication ratio, backup throughput and restore correctness are measurable on reference data sets
state_of_art: Veeam Backup & Replication; Veritas NetBackup; Commvault; Rubrik

name: Disaster recovery and standby replication
definition: Given production systems, keep standby copies at another site and fail over within target recovery time and recovery point.
inputs: production systems, replication links, recovery objectives
outputs: standby systems, failover runbooks, achieved recovery time and point
benchmark_note: achieved recovery time and data loss can be measured in scripted failover drills
state_of_art: Zerto; Oracle Data Guard; AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery

name: File systems and volume management
definition: Given block devices, organize them into volumes and a hierarchical file namespace with consistency, quotas and snapshots.
inputs: block devices, volume layout, file operations
outputs: mounted file systems, snapshots, consistency after crashes
benchmark_note: xfstests checks correctness; fio, filebench and IO500 measure performance
state_of_art: NetApp ONTAP; Veritas InfoScale Storage; IBM Storage Scale (GPFS)
open_tools: OpenZFS; ext4; Btrfs; XFS; Samba; Lustre

name: Block and network-attached storage
definition: Given storage arrays and hosts, present volumes or shares over a storage network with provisioning, replication and multipathing.
inputs: storage pools, host connections, provisioning requests
outputs: presented LUNs or shares, performance and replication status
benchmark_note: SPC-1 and fio workloads measure delivered IOPS and latency
state_of_art: Dell PowerMax; NetApp ONTAP; Pure Storage FlashArray
open_tools: Ceph; TrueNAS; LINSTOR; Linux LIO target

name: Object storage
