definition: Given objects with keys and metadata, store them durably at large scale and serve them over an HTTP API.
inputs: objects, buckets, access policies
outputs: stored objects, retrieval, lifecycle actions
benchmark_note: COSBench and warp measure object-store throughput on fixed workloads
state_of_art: Amazon S3; Azure Blob Storage; Google Cloud Storage
open_tools: Ceph RADOS Gateway; MinIO; SeaweedFS; Garage

name: Lossless data compression
definition: Given a file or stream, encode it into fewer bytes and decode it back exactly.
inputs: input data, compression level
outputs: compressed data, ratio, speed
benchmark_note: the Silesia corpus, enwik9 and lzbench give fixed data for ratio and speed comparison
state_of_art: WinZip; WinRAR; Zstandard

name: Data recovery from damaged media
definition: Given a failed, corrupted or deleted-from storage device, recover as much readable data as possible.
inputs: damaged device or image
outputs: recovered files, recovery report
benchmark_note: NIST file-carving test images and DFRWS challenges give known recoverable contents
state_of_art: R-Studio; Ontrack EasyRecovery

name: IT service management and observability
definition: Given an organization's IT services and the telemetry they emit, track requests, assets and capacity, and detect, explain and resolve service problems.

name: IT service desk and incident management
definition: Given user requests and incident reports, log, categorize, route and track them to resolution against service levels.
inputs: tickets, categories, service-level targets, knowledge articles
outputs: routed and resolved tickets, service-level reports
benchmark_note: public ticket datasets allow scoring automatic categorization and routing
state_of_art: ServiceNow ITSM; Jira Service Management; BMC Helix ITSM

name: IT asset and configuration inventory
definition: Given hardware, software and their relationships, discover and record them in a configuration database and track licenses.
inputs: network discovery data, purchase records, license entitlements
outputs: asset inventory, configuration items, license compliance
benchmark_note: inventories are organization-specific with no reference answers
state_of_art: ServiceNow Discovery and CMDB; Flexera One; Lansweeper
open_tools: GLPI; Snipe-IT; OCS Inventory NG; NetBox

name: Capacity planning
definition: Given historical utilization and growth forecasts, predict when resources will run out and size systems to meet demand.
inputs: utilization history, growth assumptions, service targets
outputs: capacity forecasts, sizing recommendations
benchmark_note: public cluster traces (Google, Alibaba) let utilization forecasts be scored against held-out data
state_of_art: VMware Aria Operations; TeamQuest (Fortra); BMC Helix Capacity Optimization

name: Metrics and application performance monitoring
definition: Given time-series metrics and traces from services, store and query them, chart dashboards and alert on anomalies.
inputs: metrics, traces, alert rules
outputs: dashboards, alerts, latency breakdowns
benchmark_note: the Numenta Anomaly Benchmark scores alerting on labeled time series; time-series stores can be compared with TSBS
state_of_art: Datadog; Dynatrace; New Relic; Grafana Cloud

name: Log aggregation and analysis
definition: Given large volumes of machine logs, collect, parse into structured events, search and summarize them.
inputs: raw log streams, parsing rules, queries
outputs: structured events, search results, log patterns
benchmark_note: Loghub log-parsing benchmarks give ground-truth templates for scoring parsers
state_of_art: Splunk; Elastic Observability; Datadog Logs
open_tools: OpenSearch; Grafana Loki; Fluent Bit; Graylog; Vector

name: Incident root-cause analysis
definition: Given an outage and the metrics, logs and traces around it, identify the faulty component and the cause.
inputs: alerts, metrics, logs, traces, topology
outputs: ranked root-cause candidates, explanation
benchmark_note: fault-injection testbeds such as the Train-Ticket microservice system give ground-truth causes
state_of_art: Dynatrace Davis AI; BigPanda; Moogsoft (Dell)

name: Machine-learning platforms and operations
definition: Given models and data, provide the frameworks and infrastructure that train, track, deploy and serve machine-learning models reliably and efficiently.

name: Tensor computation and training frameworks
definition: Given a model defined as tensor operations, differentiate and execute it efficiently on CPUs, GPUs or other accelerators, across many devices.
inputs: model code, training data, hardware
outputs: trained weights, throughput and time-to-accuracy
benchmark_note: MLPerf Training measures time to a target accuracy on fixed models and data
state_of_art: PyTorch; JAX; TensorFlow

name: Experiment tracking and model registry
definition: Given training runs and their artifacts, record parameters, metrics and lineage, and version models and datasets for reuse.
inputs: run parameters, metrics, model and data artifacts
outputs: searchable run history, versioned models and datasets
benchmark_note: these are bookkeeping systems with no reference outputs
state_of_art: Weights & Biases; MLflow (Databricks); Hugging Face Hub

name: Machine-learning pipeline orchestration
definition: Given data preparation, training and evaluation steps, run them reproducibly on cluster resources and promote passing models.
inputs: pipeline definition, compute resources, data
outputs: trained and evaluated models, pipeline run records
benchmark_note: reproducibility and resource efficiency can be measured on fixed pipelines; no standard suite
state_of_art: Amazon SageMaker; Google Vertex AI; Azure Machine Learning; Databricks
